title.zh: 卷六十四 列傳第五十二: 韋孝寬 韋瑱 柳虯
title.en: Volume 64 Biographies 52: Wei Xiaokuan, Wei Zhen, Liu Qiu
title.raw: 卷六十四 列傳第五十二: 韋孝寬 韋瑱 柳虯 Volume 64 Biographies 52: Wei Xiaokuan, Wei Zhen, Liu Qiu

sentences.zh: 韋孝寬 韋瑱 柳虯

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan, Wei Zhen, Liu Qiu
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan, Wei Zhen, and Liu Qiu

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十二

translations.literal: Biographies 52
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 52

sentences.zh: 韋孝寬兄夐夐子世康韋瑱子師柳虯弟檜慶慶子機機子述機弟弘旦肅機從子謇之

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan's elder brother Xiong; Xiong's son Shikang; Wei Zhen's son Shi; Liu Qiu's younger brothers Gui and Qing; Qing's son Ji; Ji's son Shu; Ji's younger brothers Hong, Dan, and Su; Ji's nephew Jianzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan's elder brother Xiong; Xiong's son Shikang; Wei Zhen's son Shi; Liu Qiu's younger brothers Gui and Qing; Qing's son Ji; Ji's son Shu; Ji's younger brothers Hong, Dan, and Su; and Ji's nephew Jianzhi

sentences.zh: 韋叔裕，字孝寬，京兆杜陵人也，少以字行。

translations.literal: Wei Shuyu, styled Xiaokuan, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao; from youth he was known by his style.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shuyu, styled Xiaokuan, came from Duling in Jingzhao and was known from youth by his style name rather than his given name.

sentences.zh: 世為三輔著姓。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been a prominent clan of the Three Adjuncts.
translations.idiomatic: His family had for generations ranked among the great clans of the Three Adjuncts around the capital.

sentences.zh: 祖直善，魏馮翊、扶風二郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhishan had been prefect of the two Wei commanderies of Fengyi and Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhishan had served as prefect of both Fengyi and Fufeng under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父旭，武威郡守。

translations.literal: His father Xu had been prefect of Wuwei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu had been prefect of Wuwei commandery.

sentences.zh: 建義初，為大行台右丞，加輔國將軍、雍州大中正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he served as Right Director of the Grand Secretariat and was additionally appointed General Who Assists the State and Chief Rectifier of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianyi era he became Right Director of the Grand Secretariat, with the additional titles of General Who Assists the State and Chief Rectifier of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，拜右將軍、南豳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an he was appointed General of the Right and Governor of Southern Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an he was appointed General of the Right and governor of Southern Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 時氐賊數為抄竊，旭隨機招撫，並即歸附。

translations.literal: At that time Di bandits repeatedly raided and plundered; Xu won them over as circumstances allowed, and they all submitted at once.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Di raiders struck again and again; Xu pacified them as opportunity allowed, and they all submitted without delay.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官，贈司空、冀州刺史，諡曰文惠。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died in office; posthumously he was given the titles of Minister of Works and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died in office and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works and governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 孝寬沈敏和正，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was deep, keen, harmonious, and upright, and ranged broadly through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan was grave, perceptive, even-tempered, and upright, with wide learning in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，屬蕭寶夤作亂關右，乃詣闕，請為軍前驅。

translations.literal: At his coming of age, when Xiao Baoyin rebelled in the Guanxi region, he went to the capital and asked to serve as vanguard of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, Xiao Baoyin rose in rebellion in the Guanxi region; Xiaokuan went to court and asked to lead the van of the punitive force.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，即拜統軍。

translations.literal: The court praised this and at once appointed him Commander of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his offer and immediately appointed him army commander.

sentences.zh: 隨馮翊公長孫承業西征，每戰有功。

translations.literal: He followed the Duke of Fengyi, Changsun Chengye, on the western campaign and distinguished himself in every battle.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Duke of Fengyi, Changsun Chengye, on the western campaign and won merit in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 拜國子博士，行華山郡事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University and acted as administrator of Huashan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an erudite of the Imperial University and put in charge of Huashan commandery.

sentences.zh: 屬侍中楊侃為大都督，出鎮潼關，引孝寬為司馬。

translations.literal: When the Palace Attendant Yang Kan became Grand Commander and went out to guard Tong Pass, he brought in Xiaokuan as Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Attendant Yang Kan became grand commander and took up post at Tong Pass, he took Xiaokuan on as his chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 侃奇其才，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Kan marveled at his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his ability, Kan gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 永安中，授宣威將軍、給事中，尋賜爵山北縣男。

translations.literal: During the Yong'an era he was given the posts of General Who Proclaims Might and Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, and soon received the noble rank of Baron of Shanbei county.
translations.idiomatic: During Yong'an he was made General Who Proclaims Might and Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, and soon received the title Baron of Shanbei county.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，以都督從荊州刺史源子恭鎮穰城，以功除淅陽郡守。

translations.literal: In the Putai era, as commander he followed the Governor of Jingzhou, Yuan Zigong, in garrisoning Rangcheng, and for his merit was appointed Prefect of Xiyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Putai era he served as commander under Jingzhou governor Yuan Zigong at Rangcheng and, for his achievements, was appointed prefect of Xiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 時獨孤信為新野郡守，同隸荊州，與孝寬情好款密，政術俱美，荊部吏人號為連璧。

translations.literal: At that time Dugu Xin was prefect of Xinye commandery; both were under Jingzhou. He and Xiaokuan were on terms of warm intimacy, and both excelled in governance; the officials and people of Jing called them paired jades.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin was then prefect of Xinye, likewise under Jingzhou. He and Xiaokuan were close friends, both renowned for their administration, and the people of Jing called them a matched pair of jades.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，以都督鎮城。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, as commander he garrisoned the city.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he garrisoned the city as area commander.

sentences.zh: 周文帝自原州赴雍州，命孝寬隨軍。

translations.literal: When the Zhou Emperor Wen went from Yuanzhou to Yongzhou, he ordered Xiaokuan to accompany the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou moved from Yuanzhou to Yongzhou, he ordered Xiaokuan to march with the army.

sentences.zh: 及克潼關，即授弘農郡守。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass was taken, he was at once appointed prefect of Hongnong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Tong Pass fell, he was immediately made prefect of Hongnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 從拎竇泰，兼左丞，節度宜陽兵馬事。

translations.literal: He followed Dou Tai and concurrently served as Left Director, directing the military affairs of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Dou Tai, serving concurrently as Left Director and overseeing military affairs at Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 仍與獨孤信入洛，為陽城郡守，復與宇文貴、怡峰應接潁川義徒，破東魏將任祥、堯雄於潁川。

translations.literal: He then entered Luoyang with Dugu Xin, became prefect of Yangcheng commandery, and again with Yuwen Gui and Yi Feng received the righteous bands of Yingchuan, defeating the Eastern Wei generals Ren Xiang and Yao Xiong at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered Luoyang with Dugu Xin and became prefect of Yangcheng. With Yuwen Gui and Yi Feng he linked up with the loyalist bands of Yingchuan and defeated the Eastern Wei generals Ren Xiang and Yao Xiong there.

sentences.zh: 孝寬又進平樂口，下豫州，獲刺史馮邕。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan further advanced and pacified Leyukou, took Yuzhou, and captured the governor Feng Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan went on to secure Leyukou, reduced Yuzhou, and took its governor Feng Yong prisoner.

sentences.zh: 又從戰於河橋。

translations.literal: He again followed into battle at Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 時大軍不利，邊境騷然，乃令孝寬以本將軍行宜陽郡事。

translations.literal: When the main army met with defeat and the frontier was in turmoil, Xiaokuan was ordered to act as prefect of Yiyang with his existing rank of general.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army was beaten and the frontier erupted in alarm, Xiaokuan was ordered to administer Yiyang commandery while retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 尋遷南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to be Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，東魏將段琛、堯傑復據宜陽，遣其陽州刺史牛道恆扇誘邊人。

translations.literal: That year the Eastern Wei generals Duan Chen and Yao Jie again seized Yiyang and sent their Governor of Yangzhou, Niu Daoheng, to incite and entice the border people.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Eastern Wei generals Duan Chen and Yao Jie reoccupied Yiyang and sent their Yangzhou governor Niu Daoheng to stir up and win over the border population.

sentences.zh: 孝寬深患之，乃遣諜人訪獲道恆手跡，令善學書者偽作道恆與孝寬書，論歸款意，又為落燼燒跡，若火下書者，還令諜人送于琛營。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was deeply troubled by this. He sent spies who obtained samples of Daoheng's handwriting, had skilled calligraphers forge a letter from Daoheng to Xiaokuan discussing surrender, and further scorched the edges with embers so that it looked as if written under fire; he then had the spies deliver it to Chen's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply alarmed, Xiaokuan sent agents who obtained specimens of Daoheng's hand. Skilled scribes forged a letter from Daoheng to Xiaokuan discussing defection; the edges were charred with embers to look as if the letter had been written in a fire. The agents then carried it to Duan Chen's camp.

sentences.zh: 琛得書，果疑道恆，其所欲經略，皆不見用。

translations.literal: When Chen received the letter he indeed suspected Daoheng, and none of the plans Daoheng wished to carry out were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Chen received the letter and duly grew suspicious of Daoheng; none of Daoheng's proposed operations were heeded.

sentences.zh: 孝寬知其離阻，因出奇兵掩襲，禽道恆及琛等，崤澠遂清。

translations.literal: Knowing they were divided and estranged, Xiaokuan launched a surprise force in a sudden strike, captured Daoheng and Chen and the rest, and the Xiaomian region was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that they were divided, Xiaokuan struck with a surprise force, captured Daoheng, Chen, and their fellows, and the Xiaomian region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong his noble rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong his title was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉晉州刺史，尋移鎮玉壁，兼攝南汾州事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Governor of Jinzhou; soon he moved his garrison to Yubi and concurrently administered Southern Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became governor of Jinzhou and soon transferred his headquarters to Yubi, while also overseeing Southern Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，山胡負險，屢為劫盜，孝寬示以威信，州境肅然。

translations.literal: Earlier the Mountain Hu had relied on rugged terrain and repeatedly plundered as bandits; Xiaokuan displayed authority and good faith, and the commandery became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The Mountain Hu had long used the hills to raid and plunder; Xiaokuan won them with a mix of authority and reassurance, and the region grew calm.

sentences.zh: 進授大都督。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to grand commander.

sentences.zh: 十二年，齊神武傾山東之眾，志圖西入，以玉壁沖要，先命攻之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Qi Shenwu mobilized the hosts of Shandong, intending to drive west; because Yubi was strategically vital, he ordered it attacked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Gao Huan of Qi mustered the armies of the east with plans to advance west. Because Yubi was a critical choke point, he ordered it attacked first.

sentences.zh: 連營數十里，至於城下。

translations.literal: He pitched camp in a continuous line for several tens of li, reaching to the foot of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: His camps stretched for dozens of li, right up to the foot of the walls.

sentences.zh: 乃于城南起土山，欲乘之以入。

translations.literal: He then raised an earthen mound south of the city, intending to use it to enter.
translations.idiomatic: South of the city he built an earthen ramp, planning to storm the walls from its height.

sentences.zh: 當其山處，城上先有兩高樓。

translations.literal: Where the mound was to rise, there were already two tall towers on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: At the point where the ramp was aimed, two tall towers already stood on the wall.

sentences.zh: 孝寬更縛木接之，令極高峻，多積戰具以禦之。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan bound more timbers to extend them, making them extremely high and steep, and piled up many weapons of war to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan lashed on more timber to raise them still higher, stockpiled arms on top, and prepared to meet the assault.

sentences.zh: 齊神武使謂城中曰：「縱爾縛樓至天，我會穿城取爾。」

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu sent word into the city: "Even if you bind your towers up to heaven, I shall tunnel through the wall and take you.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent a message into the city: "Even if you raise your towers to the sky, I will bore through the wall and take you.

sentences.zh: 遂于城南鑿地道，又於城北起土山，攻具，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: He then dug tunnels south of the city and also raised an earthen mound north of the city; siege engines worked day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove tunnels under the south wall and built another earthen ramp to the north; siege engines hammered the defenses day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 孝寬復掘長塹，要其地道，仍簡戰士屯塹。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan in turn dug a long trench to intercept their tunnels and selected fighting men to hold the trench.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan countered by cutting a long trench to block the tunnels and posted picked fighters along it.

sentences.zh: 城外每穿至塹，戰土即擒殺之。

translations.literal: Whenever the enemy outside broke through to the trench, the warriors seized and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the enemy broke through into the trench, the defenders seized and killed them.

sentences.zh: 又于塹外積柴貯火，敵人有在地道內者，便下柴火，以皮排吹之。

translations.literal: He also piled firewood and stored fire outside the trench; when enemies were in the tunnels, they dropped firewood and kindling and blew the flames with leather bellows.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the trench he piled fuel and kept fires ready; when enemies appeared in a tunnel, his men dropped burning brands and fanned the flames with leather bellows.

sentences.zh: 火氣一沖，咸即灼爛。

translations.literal: When the blast of fire struck them, all were scorched and burned.
translations.idiomatic: A single blast of fire scorched them all.

sentences.zh: 城外又造攻車，車之所及，莫不摧毀，雖有排楯，莫之能抗。

translations.literal: Outside the walls they also built assault towers; wherever the towers reached, nothing failed to be smashed; though there were mantlets and shields, none could withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the walls they built assault towers that shattered everything in reach; no mantlet or shield could hold them off.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乃縫布為縵，隨其所向則張設之。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan then sewed cloth into great sheets and spread them wherever the towers were aimed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan had great sheets of cloth sewn and hung them wherever the towers bore.

sentences.zh: 布懸于空中，其車竟不能壞。

translations.literal: With the cloth hanging in the air, the towers could not break through after all.
translations.idiomatic: Suspended in midair, the cloth blunted the towers' blows.

sentences.zh: 城外又縛松於竿，灌油加火，規以燒布，並欲焚樓。

translations.literal: Outside they also bound pine to poles, poured on oil and set them afire, intending to burn the cloth and also to set the towers ablaze.
translations.idiomatic: Outside they lashed pine to poles, soaked them in oil, and set them burning to destroy the cloth and set the towers afire.

sentences.zh: 孝寬復長作鐵鉤，利其鋒刃，火竿一來，以鉤遙豁之，松麻俱落。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan in turn had long iron hooks made with sharp blades; when a fire pole came, they hooked it from afar and pulled, and pine and hemp alike fell away.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan had long iron hooks forged with sharp blades; as each fire pole came up, men snagged it from a distance and pulled, and pine and tow alike fell away.

sentences.zh: 外又於城四面穿地，作二十一道，分為四路，于其中各施梁柱。

translations.literal: Outside they also tunneled under the city on all four sides, making twenty-one passages divided into four routes, and in each they set up pillars and beams.
translations.idiomatic: They also mined under the walls on all four sides, opening twenty-one galleries in four directions and propping each with beams and posts.

sentences.zh: 作訖，以油灌柱，放火燒之，柱折，城並崩壞。

translations.literal: When the work was finished they poured oil on the pillars and set them afire; the pillars broke and the wall collapsed as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done they soaked the posts with oil and burned them; the posts gave way and sections of the wall collapsed.

sentences.zh: 孝寬又隨崩處，豎木柵以捍之，敵不得入。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan again, wherever the wall had collapsed, set up wooden palisades to block them, and the enemy could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the wall fell, Xiaokuan threw up wooden palisades, and the enemy could not break in.

sentences.zh: 城外盡其攻擊之術，孝寬咸拒破之。

translations.literal: Outside the walls they exhausted every method of attack; Xiaokuan repelled and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: The besiegers tried every assault they knew; Xiaokuan defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 神武無如之何，乃遣倉曹參軍祖孝征謂曰：「未聞救兵，何不降也？」

translations.literal: Shenwu could do nothing about it and sent the Registrar of the Granary Office, Zu Xiaozheng, to say: "No relief army has been heard of—why not surrender?
translations.idiomatic: At his wits' end, Gao Huan sent Registrar Zu Xiaozheng to ask: "No relief has come—why not surrender?

sentences.zh: 孝寬報云：「我城池嚴固，兵食有餘，攻者自勞，守者常逸，豈有旬朔之間，已須救援？

translations.literal: Xiaokuan replied: "Our walls are strong and our troops and provisions ample; attackers wear themselves out while defenders remain at ease—how could relief already be needed within a month or so?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan answered: "Our walls are strong and our stores ample. Attackers tire themselves while defenders rest easy. Why should we need relief within a month?

sentences.zh: 適憂爾眾有不反之危。

translations.literal: I am rather concerned that your host may face the peril of mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: I am more worried that your army may turn on you.

sentences.zh: 孝寬關西男子，必不為降將軍也。」

translations.literal: Xiaokuan is a man of Guanxi and will certainly not become a surrendering general."
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of the Guanxi west and will never become a general who surrenders."

sentences.zh: 俄而孝征復謂城中人曰：「韋城主受彼榮祿，或復可爾，自外軍士，何事相隨入湯火中邪？」

translations.literal: Soon Xiaozheng again said to the people in the city: "Commandant Wei enjoys rank and salary from them—perhaps that can be excused—but you other soldiers, why follow him into boiling water and fire?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zu Xiaozheng called out to the garrison: "Commandant Wei draws pay from the enemy—perhaps he has his reasons. But you other soldiers—why follow him into fire and flood?"

sentences.zh: 乃射募格于城中云：「能斬城主降者，拜太尉，封開國郡公，邑萬戶，賞帛萬匹。」

translations.literal: He then shot a recruitment notice into the city saying: "Whoever can behead the commandant and surrender shall be appointed Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Duke of a State-Founding Commandery with a fief of ten thousand households, and rewarded with ten thousand bolts of silk."
translations.idiomatic: He shot a bounty notice into the city: "Whoever slays the commandant and surrenders shall be made Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Duke of a State-Founding Commandery with ten thousand households, and given ten thousand bolts of silk."

sentences.zh: 孝寬手題書背，反射城外，云：「若有斬高歡者，一依此賞。」

translations.literal: Xiaokuan wrote on the back with his own hand and shot it back outside, saying: "Whoever can behead Gao Huan shall receive the same reward."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan wrote on the back and shot it back: "Whoever slays Gao Huan shall receive the same reward."

sentences.zh: 孝寬弟子遷，先在山東，又鎖至城下，臨以白刃云：「若不早降，便行大戮。」

translations.literal: Xiaokuan's nephew Qian, who had earlier been in Shandong, was again brought in chains to the foot of the wall; a naked blade was held to him with the words: "If you do not surrender soon, he shall be put to great execution."
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Qian, who had been in the east, was brought in chains to the wall. A blade was laid to his throat: "Surrender at once, or he dies."

sentences.zh: 孝寬慷慨激揚，略無顧意。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was ardent and resolute, with not the slightest sign of concern.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan showed no sign of wavering; his bearing was fierce and unshaken.

sentences.zh: 士卒莫不感勵，人有死難之心。

translations.literal: The soldiers were all moved and inspired; each had the will to die in the cause.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were stirred to the core; every man was ready to die where he stood.

sentences.zh: 神武苦戰六旬，傷及病死者十四五，智力俱困，因而發疾。

translations.literal: Shenwu fought bitterly for sixty days; the wounded and sick who died were four or five in ten; wit and strength were both exhausted, and he fell ill as a result.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan fought bitterly for sixty days. Four or five men in ten were killed, wounded, or sick; his wits and strength were spent, and illness followed.

sentences.zh: 其夜遁去。

translations.literal: That night he fled in secret.
translations.idiomatic: That night he stole away.

sentences.zh: 後因此忿恚，遂殂。

translations.literal: Later, because of this resentment and rage, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later, brooding over the defeat, he died.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝嘉孝寬功，令殿中尚書長孫紹遠、左丞王悅至玉壁勞問，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵建忠郡公。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei commended Xiaokuan's merit and sent the Director of the Palace Secretariat Changsun Shaoyuan and the Left Director Wang Yue to Yubi to offer congratulations and inquiries, appointing him General of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Department with the same rank as the Three Excellencies, and advancing his noble rank to Duke of the Commandery of Establishing Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei honored Xiaokuan's achievement and sent Changsun Shaoyuan of the Palace Secretariat and Left Director Wang Yue to Yubi with congratulations. Xiaokuan was made General of Agile Cavalry with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and his title was raised to Duke of Establishing Loyalty commandery.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二年，為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of the deposed emperor he became Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei he became governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，路側一里置一土堠，經雨頹毀，每須修之。

translations.literal: Earlier, along the roads a earthen marker was set up every li; rain caused them to collapse and they had to be repaired constantly.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, earthen mile markers had been set along the roads every li; rain ruined them and they had to be repaired again and again.

sentences.zh: 自孝寬臨州，乃勒部內，當堠處植槐樹代之。

translations.literal: From the time Xiaokuan took charge of the province, he ordered his jurisdiction that wherever there had been a marker, locust trees should be planted in place of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaokuan took office he ordered that locust trees be planted at every former marker site.

sentences.zh: 既免修復，行旅又得庇陰。

translations.literal: This both spared repairs and gave travelers shade.
translations.idiomatic: Repairs were no longer needed, and travelers gained shade.

sentences.zh: 周文後見，怪問知之，曰：「豈得一州獨爾，當令天下同之。」

translations.literal: When Zhou Wen later saw this he wondered and asked how it had come about; on learning he said: "How can one province alone be thus? It should be made the same throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai later saw this he asked how it had been done and said: "Why should one province alone have this? Let the whole realm follow suit.

sentences.zh: 於是令諸州夾道一里種一樹，十里種三樹，百里種五樹焉。

translations.literal: He then ordered all provinces: along the roads plant one tree per li, three trees per ten li, and five trees per hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered every province to plant one tree per li along the highways, three per ten li, and five per hundred li.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年，以大將軍與燕公於謹伐江陵，平之，以功封穰縣公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong, as Grand General he joined the Duke of Yan, Yu Jin, in attacking Jiangling; when it was pacified, for his merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong he marched as grand general with the Duke of Yan, Yu Jin, against Jiangling. After its fall he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiang county for his service.

sentences.zh: 還，拜尚書右僕射，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 三年，周文北巡，命孝寬還鎮玉壁。

translations.literal: In the third year Zhou Wen toured the north and ordered Xiaokuan to return and garrison Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Yuwen Tai toured the north and ordered Xiaokuan back to Yubi.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，拜小司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded, Xiaokuan was appointed Lesser Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Xiaokuan was appointed lesser minister of education.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，參麟趾殿學士，考校圖籍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he joined the Academicians of the Linzhi Hall and collated the maps and records.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign he became an academician of the Linzhi Hall and collated the library collections.

sentences.zh: 保定初，以孝寬立勳玉壁，置勳州，仍授勳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, because Xiaokuan had established merit at Yubi, Merit Prefecture was created and he was appointed its governor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Baoding, in honor of Xiaokuan's defense of Yubi, Merit Prefecture was created and he was made its governor.

sentences.zh: 齊人遣使至玉壁，求通互市。

translations.literal: The people of Qi sent envoys to Yubi requesting to open mutual markets.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent envoys to Yubi seeking to open border trade.

sentences.zh: 晉公護以其相持日久，絕無使命，一日忽來求交易，疑別有故。

translations.literal: The Duke of Jin, Hu, because they had faced each other for so long with absolutely no missions, thought that this sudden request for trade one day must hide some other purpose.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jin, Yuwen Hu, noted that after long hostility there had been no contact at all, and suspected some hidden motive when Qi suddenly asked to trade.

sentences.zh: 又以皇姑、皇世母先沒在彼，因其請和之際，或可致之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the emperor's paternal aunt and the emperor's father's mother had earlier perished in their territory; on this occasion of their request for peace, perhaps they could be brought back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's paternal aunt and his father's mother were still held in the east; perhaps they could be recovered while Qi was suing for peace.

sentences.zh: 遂令司門下大夫尹公正至玉壁，共孝寬詳議。

translations.literal: He therefore sent the Grand Master of the Department of Gatekeeping, Yin Gongzheng, to Yubi to deliberate in detail with Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand Master of the Gate Yin Gongzheng to Yubi to work out the details with Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乃于郊盛設供帳，令公正接對使人，兼論皇家親屬在東之意。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan then set out a lavish reception in the suburbs and had Gongzheng receive the envoys, also raising the matter of imperial kin held in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan staged a lavish reception outside the city and had Gongzheng receive the envoys while raising the question of imperial relatives held in the east.

sentences.zh: 使者辭色甚悅。

translations.literal: The envoys' words and expressions were very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys responded with evident satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 時又有汾州胡抄得關東人，孝寬復放東還，並致書一牘，具陳朝廷欲敦鄰好。

translations.literal: At that time there were also Hu of Fenzhou who had captured people from Guandong; Xiaokuan again released them to return east and also sent a letter stating in full that the court wished to cultivate good relations with its neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Some Fenzhou Hu had captured people from the east; Xiaokuan released them and sent a letter stating the court's wish for neighborly peace.

sentences.zh: 遂以禮送皇姑及護母等。

translations.literal: They then sent back in accordance with ritual the emperor's paternal aunt and Hu's mother and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Qi then ceremoniously returned the emperor's paternal aunt, Yuwen Hu's mother, and the others.

sentences.zh: 孝寬善於撫禦，能得人心，所遣間諜入齊者，皆為盡力。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was skilled at comforting and controlling men and could win people's hearts; the spies he sent into Qi all served him with full effort.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan excelled at winning loyalty; every spy he sent into Qi served him wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 亦有齊人得孝寬金貨，遙通書疏。

translations.literal: There were also men of Qi who received Xiaokuan's gold and goods and sent him letters from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Some men of Qi took his gold and reported back by letter.

sentences.zh: 故齊動靜，朝廷皆先知。

translations.literal: Thus Qi's movements and stillness were all known beforehand at court.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore learned of Qi's movements before they happened.

sentences.zh: 時有主帥許盆，孝寬度以心膂，令守一城。

translations.literal: At that time there was a commander, Xu Pen; Xiaokuan judged him a trusted confidant and ordered him to hold a city.
translations.idiomatic: A commander named Xu Pen had won Xiaokuan's full trust and was put in charge of a city.

sentences.zh: 盆乃以城東入。

translations.literal: Pen then surrendered the city to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Pen promptly surrendered the city to Qi.

sentences.zh: 孝寬怒，遣諜取之，俄而斬首而還。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was angry and sent spies to take him; before long they returned with his severed head.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Xiaokuan sent agents after him; they soon returned with his head.

sentences.zh: 其能致物情如此。

translations.literal: Such was his power to command the feelings of things and men.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his hold on men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 汾州之北，離石以南，悉是生胡，抄掠居人，阻斷河路。

translations.literal: North of Fenzhou and south of Lishi were all raw Hu who raided the inhabitants and blocked the river routes.
translations.idiomatic: North of Fenzhou and south of Lishi lived unassimilated Hu who raided settlers and cut the river routes.

sentences.zh: 孝寬深患之，而地入于齊，無方誅剪。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was deeply troubled by this, but the territory had passed into Qi and there was no means to punish and cut them down.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan was deeply alarmed, but the land lay within Qi's reach and he had no way to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 欲當其要處，置一大城。

translations.literal: He wished to place a great city at a strategic point.
translations.idiomatic: He resolved to build a major fortress at the key point.

sentences.zh: 乃於河西征役徒十萬，甲士百人，遣開府姚嶽監築之。

translations.literal: He then levied a hundred thousand corvée laborers west of the river and a hundred armored soldiers, and sent the Director of a Department, Yao Yue, to supervise the construction.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a hundred thousand laborers west of the river with a hundred armored men and sent Director Yao Yue to supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 嶽色懼，以兵少為難。

translations.literal: Yue looked afraid and took the small number of troops as a difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Yue looked alarmed and protested that the force was too small.

sentences.zh: 孝寬曰：「計成此城，十日即畢。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan said: "By my reckoning this city can be finished in ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan said: "By my plan the city will be finished in ten days.

sentences.zh: 既去晉州四百餘里，一日創手，二日偽境始知，設令晉州徵兵，二日方集，謀議之間，自稽三日，計其軍行，二日不到。

translations.literal: It is already more than four hundred li from Jinzhou; on the first day work begins, on the second day the enemy territory first learns of it; even if Jinzhou mobilizes troops, two days are needed to assemble them, and in the time for counsel and deliberation three days pass of themselves; reckoning their march, two days more they will not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhou is more than four hundred li away. Work begins on day one; Qi learns on day two. Even if Jinzhou mobilizes, two days pass before troops gather, three more for councils, and two more on the march—they cannot arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 我之城隍，足得辦矣」。

translations.literal: Our walls and moat will be quite sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Our walls and moat will be complete."

sentences.zh: 乃令築之。

translations.literal: He then ordered the building to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered construction to begin.

sentences.zh: 齊人果至南首，疑有大軍，乃停留不進。

translations.literal: The men of Qi indeed came to the southern end, suspected a great army was present, and halted without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Qi forces did reach the south bank, suspected a large army, and halted without advancing.

sentences.zh: 其夜，又令汾水以南，傍介山、稷山諸村，所在縱火。

translations.literal: That night he again ordered that south of the Fen River, in the villages along Jie Mountain, Ji Mountain, and the rest, fires be set everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: That night he ordered fires set in every village south of the Fen, along Jie Mountain, Ji Mountain, and beyond.

sentences.zh: 齊人謂是軍營，遂收兵自固。

translations.literal: The men of Qi took them for military camps and thereupon drew in their troops to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi troops took the fires for encampments and pulled back to consolidate.

sentences.zh: 版築克就，卒如其言。

translations.literal: The rammed-earth work was completed, and in the end it was exactly as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: The fortifications were finished exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 四年，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his rank was advanced to Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護將東討，孝寬遣長史辛道憲啟陳不可，護不納。

translations.literal: At that time the Duke of Jin, Hu, was about to campaign east; Xiaokuan sent his Chief Clerk Xin Daoxian with a memorial stating it could not be done, but Hu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Jin, Yuwen Hu, prepared an eastern campaign, Xiaokuan sent Chief Clerk Xin Daoxian to argue against it; Hu refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 既而大軍果不利。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the main army indeed met with defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The main army was indeed defeated.

sentences.zh: 後孔城遂陷，宜陽被圍。

translations.literal: Later Kongcheng fell, and Yiyang was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Kongcheng soon fell and Yiyang came under siege.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乃謂其將帥曰：「宜陽一城之地，未能損益。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan then said to his generals: "The territory of Yiyang city alone can neither harm nor benefit us.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan told his commanders: "Yiyang itself is neither gain nor loss for us.

sentences.zh: 然兩國爭之，勞師數載。

translations.literal: Yet the two states have contested it and wearied their armies for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both states have fought over it for years and exhausted their armies.

sentences.zh: 彼多君子，甯乏謀猷？

translations.literal: They have many gentlemen—could they lack plans and schemes?
translations.idiomatic: They have able men—do they lack stratagems?

sentences.zh: 若棄崤東，來圖汾北，我之疆界，必見侵擾。

translations.literal: If they abandon the east of Xiao and come to scheme against the north of Fen, our borders will surely suffer encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: If they abandon the east of Xiao and strike north of the Fen, our frontier will surely be threatened.

sentences.zh: 今宜於華穀及長秋速築城，以杜賊志。

translations.literal: Now we should quickly build cities at Huagu and Changqiu to block the enemy's intent.
translations.idiomatic: We should quickly fortify Huagu and Changqiu to forestall them.

sentences.zh: 脫其先我，圖之實難。」

translations.literal: If they get there before us, it will truly be hard to act.
translations.idiomatic: If they move first, we will find it hard to counter.

sentences.zh: 於是畫地形，具陳其狀。

translations.literal: He then drew the terrain and set forth the situation in full.
translations.idiomatic: He drew a map and laid out the situation in detail.

sentences.zh: 晉公護令長史叱羅協謂使人曰：「韋公子孫雖多，數不滿百。

translations.literal: The Duke of Jin had his Chief Clerk Chiluo Xie tell the envoy: "Although Commander Wei's descendants are many, they do not number a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu had Chief Clerk Chiluo Xie tell the envoy: "Wei may have many descendants, but they number fewer than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 汾北築城，遣誰固守？」

translations.literal: Building cities north of Fen—whom will you send to hold them firm?
translations.idiomatic: Who will you leave to hold fortresses north of the Fen?

sentences.zh: 事遂不行。

translations.literal: The matter therefore was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The plan went no further.

sentences.zh: 天和五年，進爵鄖國公，增邑通前一萬戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhe his noble rank was advanced to Duke of the State of Yun, and his fief was increased to ten thousand households in all with what had gone before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianhe he was made Duke of Yun state, with a combined fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 是歲，齊人果解宜陽之圍，經略汾北，遂築城守之。

translations.literal: That year the men of Qi indeed lifted the siege of Yiyang, extended their strategy to the north of Fen, and built cities to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qi lifted the siege of Yiyang, turned to the north of the Fen, and built fortified posts.

sentences.zh: 其丞相斛律明月至汾東，請與孝寬相見。

translations.literal: Their Chancellor Hulu Mingyue came to the east of Fen and asked to meet Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's chancellor Hulu Mingyue came to the east bank of the Fen and asked to meet Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 明月云：「宜陽小城，久勞戰爭。

translations.literal: Mingyue said: "Yiyang is a small city that has long wearied us with war.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue said: "Yiyang is a small place that has cost us years of war.

sentences.zh: 今既入彼，欲於汾北取償，幸勿怪也。」

translations.literal: Now that we have entered it, we wish to take compensation north of Fen—please do not take offense.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we hold it, we mean to take our due north of the Fen—please do not be offended.

sentences.zh: 孝寬答曰：「宜陽彼之要衝，汾北我之所棄。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan replied: "Yiyang is their vital pass; north of Fen is what we have abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan answered: "Yiyang is your vital pass; the north of the Fen is ground we have let go.

sentences.zh: 我棄彼圖，取償安在？

translations.literal: We abandon and they scheme—where is the compensation?
translations.idiomatic: We yield while you seize—where is the compensation in that?

sentences.zh: 且若輔翼幼主，位重望隆，理宜調陰陽，撫百姓，焉用極武窮兵，構怨連禍！

translations.literal: Moreover, if one assists and supports a young lord, with heavy rank and lofty repute, one ought by right to harmonize yin and yang and comfort the hundred surnames—why use extreme arms and exhaust the troops, building resentment and linking calamities!
translations.idiomatic: You who should steady a young ruler and soothe the people—why exhaust your armies, breed hatred, and invite disaster after disaster?

sentences.zh: 且滄、瀛大水，千里無煙，復欲使汾、晉之間，橫屍暴骨，苟貪尋常之地，塗炭疲弊之人，竊為君不取。」

translations.literal: Moreover, in Cang and Ying great floods have left a thousand li without smoke; you would again make between Fen and Jin corpses lie across the land and bones lie exposed, greedily grasping for ordinary territory and smearing with ash the worn and exhausted people—I venture to think this is not for you to take."
translations.idiomatic: Floods have already laid Cang and Ying waste for a thousand li. To heap corpses between Fen and Jin for a scrap of land and crush an exhausted people—I do not think that suits a man of your station."

sentences.zh: 孝寬參軍曲岩頗知卜筮，謂孝寬曰：「來年東朝必大相殺戮。」

translations.literal: Xiaokuan's aide Qu Yan was well versed in divination and augury and said to Xiaokuan: "Next year the eastern court will surely see great slaughter."
translations.idiomatic: His aide Qu Yan, skilled in divination, told Xiaokuan: "Next year the eastern court will see bloodshed on a great scale."

sentences.zh: 孝寬因令岩作謠歌曰：「百升飛上天，明月照長安。」

translations.literal: Xiaokuan therefore had Yan compose a ballad saying: "A hundred sheng flies up to heaven; the bright moon shines on Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan had Yan compose a song: "A hundred sheng flies to heaven; the bright moon shines on Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 百升，斛也。

translations.literal: A hundred sheng" is hu [Hulu].
translations.idiomatic: A hundred sheng" puns on hu—the character in Hulu's name.

sentences.zh: 又言：「高山不摧自崩，槲樹不扶自豎。」

translations.literal: It also said: "A high mountain without being struck collapses of itself; an oak without being propped stands upright of itself.
translations.idiomatic: It also ran: "High mountains fall without a blow; oaks stand upright without a prop.

sentences.zh: 令諜人多賚此文，遺之於鄴。

translations.literal: He ordered many spies to carry this text and leave it in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He sent agents to spread the verses in Ye.

sentences.zh: 祖孝征既聞，更潤色之，明月竟以此誅。

translations.literal: When Zu Xiaozheng heard of it he further polished it, and Mingyue was indeed executed because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaozheng heard of it, polished the verses further, and Mingyue was executed because of them.

sentences.zh: 建德之後，武帝志在平齊。

translations.literal: After Jiande, Emperor Wu's intent was to pacify Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiande era, Emperor Wu set his mind on conquering Qi.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乃上疏陳三策。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan then submitted a memorial setting forth three strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan submitted a memorial outlining three strategies.

sentences.zh: 其第一策曰：「臣在邊積年，頗見間隙，不因際會，難以成功。

translations.literal: The first strategy said: "Your servant has spent years on the frontier and has seen many openings; without seizing the moment, success is hard.
translations.idiomatic: The first strategy read: "I have spent years on the frontier and have seen many openings; without seizing the moment, success is hard.

sentences.zh: 是以往歲出軍，徒有勞費，功績不立，由失機會。

translations.literal: Therefore when armies went out in past years there was only toil and expense and no achievement established, because opportunity was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Past campaigns have cost labor and treasure without result because the moment was missed.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 長淮之南，舊為沃土，陳氏以破亡餘燼，猶能一舉平之。

translations.literal: South of the Long Huai had formerly been fertile land; Chen, with the embers of a broken and perishing state, could still pacify it in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Long Huai was once rich land; Chen, though reduced to embers, still took it in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 齊人歷年赴救，喪敗而反。

translations.literal: The men of Qi went year after year to the rescue and returned in defeat and loss.
translations.idiomatic: Qi sent armies year after year and returned in defeat.

sentences.zh: 內離外叛，計盡力窮。

translations.literal: Within there was estrangement and without there was rebellion; plans were exhausted and strength spent.
translations.idiomatic: Within they are divided and without they face rebellion; their plans and strength are spent.

sentences.zh: 傳不雲乎：'讎有釁焉，不可失也。

translations.literal: Does not the tradition say: 'When the foe shows a crack, it must not be missed'?
translations.idiomatic: Does not the tradition say: 'When the foe shows a crack, it must not be missed'?

sentences.zh: '今大軍若出軹關，方軌而進，兼與陳氏共為掎角；

translations.literal: If now the great army issues from Zhiguan and advances in parallel tracks, and together with Chen acts as pincers;
translations.idiomatic: If the main army marches out through Zhiguan in full array and coordinates with Chen in a pincer;

sentences.zh: 並令廣州義旅出自三

translations.literal: and also order the righteous bands of Guangzhou to issue from San
translations.idiomatic: and order Guangzhou's loyalist forces to advance from San

sentences.zh: 鵶；

translations.literal: ya;
translations.idiomatic: ya;

sentences.zh: 又募山南驍銳，沿河而下，復遣北山稽胡絕其並、晉之路。

translations.literal: and also recruits the fierce elite south of the mountains to descend along the river, and again sends the Ji Hu of the northern mountains to cut off their routes through Bing and Jin;
translations.idiomatic: recruits fierce fighters south of the mountains to descend the rivers, and sends the Ji Hu of the northern hills to cut the Bing and Jin roads;

sentences.zh: 凡此諸軍，仍令各募關、河之外勁勇之士，厚其爵賞，使為前驅。

translations.literal: for all these armies, further order each to recruit stalwart warriors beyond the passes and the river, enrich their ranks and rewards, and make them vanguards;
translations.idiomatic: each of these columns should recruit bold men beyond the passes and the Yellow River, reward them richly, and use them as van;

sentences.zh: 岳動川移，雷駭電激，百道俱進，並趨虜庭。

translations.literal: mountains shifting and rivers moving, thunder startling and lightning flashing, a hundred routes advancing together, all rushing toward the barbarian court—
translations.idiomatic: with forces like moving mountains and rivers, thunder and lightning, a hundred columns advancing together on the enemy capital—

sentences.zh: 必當望旗奔潰，所向摧殄。

translations.literal: they will surely flee at the sight of banners and be shattered wherever they are aimed.
translations.idiomatic: they will flee at the first banner and be crushed wherever you strike.

sentences.zh: 一戎大定，實在此機。」

translations.literal: To settle all in one campaign—truly the moment is now."
translations.idiomatic: To settle all in one campaign—the moment is now."

sentences.zh: 其第二策曰：「若國家更為後圖，未即大舉，宜與陳人分其兵勢。

translations.literal: The second strategy said: "If the state makes further plans and does not at once launch a great campaign, it should share the enemy's military strength with the men of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The second strategy read: "If the state defers a full campaign, it should share the burden with Chen and divide Qi's forces.

sentences.zh: 三鵶以北，萬春以南，廣事屯田，預為貯積。

translations.literal: North of Sanya and south of Wanchun, broadly undertake garrison farming and store up supplies in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Between Sanya in the north and Wanchun in the south, expand garrison farming and build up stores.

sentences.zh: 募其驍悍，立為部伍。

translations.literal: Recruit their fierce and bold and establish them in companies.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit their boldest men and organize them into units.

sentences.zh: 彼既東南有敵，戎馬相持，我出奇兵，破其疆埸。

translations.literal: Since they already have an enemy in the southeast and warhorses face each other, we send out surprise troops and break their borders.
translations.idiomatic: With an enemy in the southeast tying down their horses, we strike with surprise forces and raid their borders.

sentences.zh: 彼若興師赴援，我則堅壁清野，待其去遠，還復出師。

translations.literal: If they raise armies to go to the rescue, we then hold the walls firm and clear the countryside, wait until they are far away, and again send out troops.
translations.idiomatic: If they march to relieve a post, we fortify and strip the countryside, wait until they withdraw, and strike again.

sentences.zh: 常以邊外之軍，引其腹心之眾。

translations.literal: We constantly use armies on the outer borders to draw out their core hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Always use frontier raids to pull their main armies out.

sentences.zh: 我無宿舂之費，彼有奔命之勞。

translations.literal: We have no cost of overnight milling; they have the toil of emergency marches.
translations.idiomatic: We pay no cost of overnight grain; they exhaust themselves in forced marches.

sentences.zh: 一二年中，必自離叛。

translations.literal: Within a year or two they will surely split and rebel of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year or two they will split and rebel on their own.

sentences.zh: 且齊氏昏暴，政出多門，鬻獄賣官，唯利是視，荒淫酒色，忌害忠良。

translations.literal: Moreover the Qi house is benighted and violent; government issues from many gates; they sell justice and traffic in offices, looking only to profit; they are dissolute in wine and women and jealous and harmful to the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: Qi is benighted and cruel, with government split among factions, offices sold for profit, and debauchery joined to persecution of the loyal.

sentences.zh: 闔境熬然，不勝其弊。

translations.literal: The whole realm is in turmoil and cannot bear its abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm groans under these abuses.

sentences.zh: 以此而觀，覆亡可待。

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, overthrow and ruin can be awaited.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this, their fall is only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 然後乘間電掃，事等摧枯。」

translations.literal: Then seize the opening and sweep like lightning; the affair will be like breaking dry wood."
translations.idiomatic: Then strike at the opening like lightning, and the task will be like snapping dry wood."

sentences.zh: 其第三策曰：「竊以大周土宇，跨據關、河，蓄席捲之威，持建瓴之勢。

translations.literal: The third strategy said: "I venture to consider that Great Zhou's territory straddles the passes and the river, stores the might of rolling up a mat, and holds the momentum of water poured from a high eave.
translations.idiomatic: The third strategy read: "Great Zhou holds the passes and the Yellow River, with the power to sweep all before it and the momentum of water poured from a height.

sentences.zh: 太祖受天明命，與物更新，是以二紀之中，大功克舉。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor received Heaven's bright mandate and renewed all things with them; therefore within two cycles great achievements were accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor received Heaven's mandate and renewed the realm; within two reign-cycles great deeds were achieved.

sentences.zh: 南清江、漢，西龕巴、蜀，塞表無虞，河右底定。

translations.literal: The south was cleared to the Jiang and Han, the west enclosed Ba and Shu, the frontier tables were without worry, and the right bank of the river was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The south was pacified to the Jiang and Han, the west secured in Ba and Shu, the frontiers were quiet, and the lands west of the river were settled.

sentences.zh: 唯彼趙、魏，獨為榛梗者，正以有事三方，未遑東略。

translations.literal: Only Zhao and Wei there alone remain as brambles and stems, precisely because there were affairs on three sides and no leisure to plan eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhao and Wei remain as thorns, because affairs on three fronts left no leisure for an eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 遂使漳、滏遊魂，更存餘晷。

translations.literal: Thus the wandering souls of Zhang and Fu were allowed a few remaining moments of daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the stray remnants along the Zhang and Fu rivers were granted a little more time.

sentences.zh: 昔勾踐亡吳，尚期十載；

translations.literal: Formerly Goujian destroyed Wu and still set a term of ten years;
translations.idiomatic: Goujian destroyed Wu only after ten years;

sentences.zh: 武王取亂，猶煩再舉。

translations.literal: King Wu took a disordered state and still found it troublesome to raise the campaign twice.
translations.idiomatic: even King Wu needed two campaigns to conquer a fallen state.

sentences.zh: 今若更存遵養，且復相時，臣謂宜還崇鄰好，申其盟約，安人和眾，通商惠工，蓄銳養威，觀釁而動。

translations.literal: If now we again preserve compliance and nurturing and moreover watch the times, your servant says we should return to honoring good relations with neighbors, renew the covenant, settle the people and harmonize the masses, open trade and benefit craftsmen, store sharpness and nurture might, and move on seeing a crack.
translations.idiomatic: If we now practice forbearance and watch the times, I advise renewing neighborly ties and treaties, calming the people, encouraging trade and craft, storing strength, and striking only when a crack appears.

sentences.zh: 斯則長策遠馭，坐自兼併也。」

translations.literal: This then is the long plan and distant control; merger will come of itself while seated."
translations.idiomatic: That is the long view: absorb them without stirring from your seat."

sentences.zh: 書奏，武帝遣小司寇淮南西元偉、開府伊婁謙等重幣聘齊。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Wu sent the Lesser Minister of Justice Huainan Xi Yuanwei, the Director of a Department Yilou Qian, and others with heavy gifts to pay a friendly visit to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Wu sent Lesser Minister of Justice Xi Yuanwei of Huainan, Director Yilou Qian, and others with rich gifts to court Qi.

sentences.zh: 爾後遂大舉，再駕而定山東。

translations.literal: Thereafter he launched a great campaign; on the second expedition he settled Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He then launched a great campaign and on the second expedition settled the east.

sentences.zh: 卒如孝寬之策。

translations.literal: In the end it was exactly as Xiaokuan's strategies had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end events unfolded exactly as Xiaokuan had foretold.

sentences.zh: 孝寬每以年迫懸車，屢請致仕。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan, because his years pressed upon the age of hanging up the carriage, repeatedly asked to retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: As age pressed on him, Xiaokuan repeatedly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝以海內未平，優詔弗許。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the realm within the seas was not yet settled, with gracious edicts did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm was not yet settled, the emperor graciously refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，復稱疾乞骸骨。

translations.literal: At this time he again pleaded illness and asked for his bones.
translations.idiomatic: Now he again pleaded illness and asked to be released.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「往已面申本懷，何煩重請也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Earlier you already stated your true intent in person—why trouble to ask again?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You have already told me your mind in person—why ask again?"

sentences.zh: 五年，帝東伐，過幸玉壁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor campaigned east and on the way favored Yubi with a visit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor marched east and visited Yubi on the way.

sentences.zh: 觀禦敵之所，深歎美之，移時乃去。

translations.literal: He viewed the places for repelling the enemy, sighed deeply in admiration, and only after a long while departed.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the defenses, sighed in deep admiration, and lingered long before leaving.

sentences.zh: 孝寬自以習練齊人虛實，請為先驅。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan, considering himself practiced in the realities of the men of Qi, asked to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Qi's strengths and weaknesses, Xiaokuan asked to lead the van.

sentences.zh: 帝以玉壁要衝，非孝寬無以鎮之，乃不許。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yubi was a vital pass and without Xiaokuan there was no one to hold it firm, therefore did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Yubi was vital and could be held only by Xiaokuan, and refused.

sentences.zh: 及趙王招率兵出稽胡，與大軍掎角，乃敕孝寬為行軍總管，圍守華谷以應接之。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhao of Zhao led troops out against the Ji Hu in coordination with the main army as pincers, he then ordered Xiaokuan as Campaign Commander to besiege and hold Huagu in support.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhao led troops against the Ji Hu in concert with the main army, the emperor ordered Xiaokuan as campaign commander to besiege Huagu in support.

sentences.zh: 孝寬克其四城。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan captured its four cities.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan took four of its cities.

sentences.zh: 武帝平晉州，復令孝寬還舊鎮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu pacified Jinzhou, he again ordered Xiaokuan back to his former garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took Jinzhou, Xiaokuan was sent back to his old post.

sentences.zh: 及帝凱旋，復幸玉壁。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned in triumph, he again favored Yubi with a visit.
translations.idiomatic: On his triumphant return he visited Yubi again.

sentences.zh: 從容謂孝寬曰：「世稱老人多智，善為軍謀。

translations.literal: At ease he said to Xiaokuan: "The age calls old men wise and skilled at military planning.
translations.idiomatic: He said easily to Xiaokuan: "People say old men are wise and skilled in strategy.

sentences.zh: 然朕唯共少年一舉平賊，公以為如何？」

translations.literal: Yet I alone with the young in one stroke pacified the rebels—what do you think of that?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I alone, still young, settled the rebels in one stroke—what do you think of that?

sentences.zh: 孝寬對曰：「臣今衰耄，唯有誠心而已。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan replied: "Your servant is now decrepit and aged; I have only sincere heart, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan answered: "I am old and feeble now and have only loyalty to offer.

sentences.zh: 然昔在少壯，亦曾輸力先朝，以定關右。」

translations.literal: Yet formerly in my youth and prime I also once contributed strength to the former court to settle the Guanxi right."
translations.idiomatic: But in my youth I too served the former court and helped settle the Guanxi west."

sentences.zh: 帝大笑曰：「實如公言。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly and said: "It is truly as you say."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said: "You are quite right."

sentences.zh: 乃詔孝寬隨駕還京。

translations.literal: He then ordered Xiaokuan to follow the imperial carriage back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Xiaokuan to return to the capital with the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 拜大司空，出為延州總管，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Minister of Works, sent out to serve as Regional Commander of Yan Province, and advanced in rank to Supreme Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Minister of Works, assigned as regional commander of Yan Province, and promoted to Supreme Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝崩，隋文帝輔政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Emperor Wen of Sui served as regent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan passed away, Yang Jian assumed the regency.

sentences.zh: 時尉遲迥先為相州總管，詔孝寬代之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuwen Jiong had previously served as Regional Commander of Xiang Province; an edict ordered Xiaokuan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong was then regional commander of Xiang Province; an imperial edict named Xiaokuan to replace him.

sentences.zh: 又以小司徒叱列長叉為相州刺史，先令赴鄴。

translations.literal: Furthermore, Chilie Changcha was appointed Governor of Xiang Province with the rank of Junior Minister of Education, and was first ordered to proceed to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Chilie Changcha was also made governor of Xiang Province with the rank of Junior Minister of Education and sent on ahead to Ye.

sentences.zh: 孝寬續進，至朝歌，迥遣其大都督賀蘭貴賚書候孝寬。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan continued his advance; when he reached Chaoge, Jiong sent his Grand Commander Helan Gui with a letter to inquire after Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan pressed on, and at Chaoge Yuwen Jiong's grand commander Helan Gui met him with a greeting letter.

sentences.zh: 孝寬留貴與語以察之，疑其有變，遂稱疾徐行。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan detained Gui and spoke with him to observe him; suspecting there might be a plot, he then claimed illness and proceeded slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan kept Gui for conversation to take his measure, suspected trouble brewing, and feigned illness to slow his march.

sentences.zh: 又使人至相州求醫藥，密以伺之。

translations.literal: He also sent men to Xiang Province to seek medicine, secretly to spy on the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent agents to Xiang Province under the pretense of seeking medicine, to watch events in secret.

sentences.zh: 既到湯陰，逢長叉奔還。

translations.literal: When he had reached Tangyin, he encountered Changcha fleeing back.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Tangyin, Changcha was already racing back in flight.

sentences.zh: 孝寬兄子魏郡守藝又棄郡南走。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan's nephew Yi, Administrator of Wei Commandery, also abandoned the commandery and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan's nephew Yi, prefect of Wei Commandery, had likewise abandoned his post and fled south.

sentences.zh: 孝寬審知其狀，乃馳還。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan thoroughly understood the situation and then galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiaokuan had confirmed what was happening, he turned and rode back at full speed.

sentences.zh: 所經橋道，皆令毀撤，驛馬悉擁以自隨。

translations.literal: At every bridge and road he passed, he ordered them destroyed and dismantled, and he gathered all the relay horses to take with him.
translations.idiomatic: He had every bridge and stretch of road he crossed torn up, and requisitioned every relay horse along the route.

sentences.zh: 又勒驛將曰：「蜀公將至，可多備肴酒及芻粟以待之。」

translations.literal: He also instructed the relay station masters, saying: "The Duke of Shu is about to arrive—you should prepare ample food, wine, and fodder to await him.
translations.idiomatic: He told the relay masters that "the Duke of Shu is coming—lay in plenty of food, wine, and fodder for him.

sentences.zh: 迥果遣儀同梁子康將數百騎追孝寬，驛司供設豐厚，所經之處，皆輒停留，由是不及。

translations.literal: Jiong did indeed send Palace Attendant Liang Zikang leading several hundred horsemen in pursuit of Xiaokuan; the relay offices provided lavish supplies, and at every place they passed they invariably halted, and for this reason they could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong sent Palace Attendant Liang Zikang after him with several hundred cavalry; at each station the pursuers found lavish provisions and lingered, so they never caught up.

sentences.zh: 時或勸孝寬，以為洛京虛弱，素無守備，河陽鎮防，悉是關東鮮卑，迥若先往據之，則為禍不小。

translations.literal: At the time some urged Xiaokuan, reasoning that Luoyang was weak and had long lacked defenses, that the garrison at Heyang consisted entirely of Eastern-pass Xianbei, and that if Jiong went there first to seize it, the disaster would be no small one.
translations.idiomatic: Some advised Xiaokuan that Luoyang was thinly defended, that Heyang's garrison was all Xianbei from east of the pass, and that if Yuwen Jiong seized it first the consequences would be grave.

sentences.zh: 乃入保河陽。

translations.literal: He therefore entered Heyang to hold it in defense.
translations.idiomatic: So he withdrew into Heyang to secure it.

sentences.zh: 河陽城內，舊有鮮卑八百人，家並在鄴，見孝寬輕來，謀欲應迥。

translations.literal: Within Heyang city there were originally eight hundred Xianbei whose families were all in Ye; seeing Xiaokuan had come lightly, they plotted to respond to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred Xianbei inside Heyang, whose families were in Ye, saw Xiaokuan arrive with a small force and plotted to join Yuwen Jiong.

sentences.zh: 孝寬知之，遂密造東京官司，詐稱遣行，分人詣洛受賜。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan learned of it, and thereupon secretly forged documents from the Eastern Capital offices, falsely claiming they were being sent on assignment, and sent the men in groups to Luoyang to receive rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the plot, he forged orders in the name of the Eastern Capital government and sent the men to Luoyang in batches for supposed imperial grants.

sentences.zh: 既至洛陽，並留不遣。

translations.literal: Once they reached Luoyang, all were detained and not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Once they reached Luoyang, he kept them there and refused to let them return.

sentences.zh: 因此離解，其謀不成。

translations.literal: Because of this they were separated and dispersed, and their plot did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: That broke up their conspiracy and foiled the plot.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔發關中兵，以孝寬為元帥東伐。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, an edict ordered the mobilization of Guanzhong troops, with Xiaokuan as commander-in-chief for an eastern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month an edict mobilized the armies of Guanzhong and named Xiaokuan supreme commander for the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 七月，軍次河陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the army halted at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the army encamped at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 迥所署儀同薛公禮等圍逼懷州，孝寬遣兵擊破之。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendants Xue Gongli and others appointed by Jiong besieged and pressed Huai Province; Xiaokuan sent troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong's appointee, Palace Attendant Xue Gongli, besieged Huai Province; Xiaokuan sent troops and routed him.

sentences.zh: 進次懷縣永橋城之東南，其城既在要衝，雉堞牢固，迥已遣兵據之。

translations.literal: He advanced and halted southeast of Yongqiao city in Huai County; the city stood at a strategic junction, its battlements solid, and Jiong had already sent troops to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on and camped southeast of Yongqiao in Huai County—a stronghold on a vital route that Yuwen Jiong's troops already held.

sentences.zh: 諸將士以此城當路，請先攻取。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers, considering that this city blocked the road, requested that it be attacked and taken first.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged him to take the city first since it blocked their path.

sentences.zh: 孝寬曰：「城小而固，若攻而不拔，損我兵威。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan said: "The city is small but solid; if we attack and fail to take it, we will diminish the martial prestige of our army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan replied: "The place is small but strong. If we besiege it and fail, we will lose face.

sentences.zh: 今破其大軍，此亦何能為也？」

translations.literal: If we now defeat their main army, what can this place do?
translations.idiomatic: Break their main force and what can this outpost do?

sentences.zh: 於是引軍次於武陟，大破迥子惇，惇輕騎奔鄴。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the army to halt at Wuzhi, and inflicted a great defeat on Jiong's son Dun; Dun fled to Ye with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to Wuzhi, crushed Yuwen Jiong's son Dun, and Dun fled to Ye with a light escort.

sentences.zh: 軍次於鄴西門豹祠之南，迥自出戰，又破之。

translations.literal: The army halted south of the Ximen Bao Shrine at Ye; Jiong came out personally to fight, and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted south of the Ximen Bao Shrine outside Ye; Yuwen Jiong came out to fight in person and was beaten again.

sentences.zh: 迥窮迫自殺。

translations.literal: Jiong, driven to extremity, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Jiong, cornered, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 兵士在小城中者，盡坑之于遊豫園。

translations.literal: The soldiers in the small cities were all buried alive at the Youyu Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who held out in smaller cities were buried alive at the Youyu Garden.

sentences.zh: 諸有未服，皆隨機討之。

translations.literal: All who had not yet submitted were, each according to circumstance, suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Every holdout was dealt with as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 關東悉平。

translations.literal: The entire Eastern Pass region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: East of the pass was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 十月，凱還京師。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he returned in triumph to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he returned to the capital in triumph.

sentences.zh: 十一月，薨，時年七十二。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he died; he was then seventy-two years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he died, at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅、十二州諸軍事、雍州牧，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Twelve Provinces, and Governor of Yong Province; his posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, supreme commander of twelve provinces, and governor of Yong Province, with the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 孝寬在邊多載，屢抗強敵。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan served on the frontier for many years and repeatedly resisted powerful enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan spent many years on the frontier, repeatedly facing formidable foes.

sentences.zh: 所有經略，佈置之初，人莫之解；

translations.literal: In all the strategies and deployments he undertook, when they were first laid out no one understood them;
translations.idiomatic: No one understood his strategic dispositions when he first made them;

sentences.zh: 見其成事，方乃驚服。

translations.literal: Only when they saw the results accomplished did they then marvel and submit in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they saw them succeed did they marvel and defer to his judgment.

sentences.zh: ，雖在軍中，篤意文史，政事之餘，每自披閱。

translations.literal: , although he was in the army, he devoted himself deeply to literature and history; in the intervals of government affairs, he would personally peruse texts each time.
translations.idiomatic: Even while on campaign, he devoted himself to scholarship, and whenever duties allowed he read on his own.

sentences.zh: 末年患眼，猶令學士讀而聽之。

translations.literal: In his later years he suffered from eye disease, yet he still had scholars read aloud for him to listen.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, though his eyes failed, he still had scholars read to him.

sentences.zh: 又早喪父母，事兄嫂甚謹，所得俸祿，不入私房。

translations.literal: He also lost his parents early; he served his elder brother and sister-in-law with great respect; the salary he received did not go into his private household.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he treated his elder brother and sister-in-law with scrupulous care, and never kept his official salary for himself.

sentences.zh: 親族有孤遺者，必加振贍。

translations.literal: Among kinsmen there were orphans and the destitute; he always extended relief and support to them.
translations.idiomatic: He unfailingly supported orphaned or needy members of the clan.

sentences.zh: 朝野以此稱焉。

translations.literal: Court and commoners alike praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was praised throughout court and country.

sentences.zh: 長子諶，年十歲，魏文帝欲以女妻之。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chen, at ten years of age—the Emperor Wen of Wei wished to give him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When his eldest son Chen was ten, Emperor Wen of Wei wanted to marry a princess to him.

sentences.zh: 孝寬辭以兄子世康年長。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan declined on the ground that his elder brother's son Shikang was older.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan declined, citing his elder brother's son Shikang as the elder candidate.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，遂以妻世康。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised this and thereupon gave the princess in marriage to Shikang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired the gesture and gave the princess to Shikang instead.

sentences.zh: 孝寬有六子，總、壽、霽、津知名。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan had six sons; Zong, Shou, Ji, and Jin were renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan had six sons; Zong, Shou, Ji, and Jin were the best known.

sentences.zh: 總字善會，聰敏好學。

translations.literal: Zong's courtesy name was Shanhui; he was clever and quick-witted and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, courtesy name Shanhui, was clever and loved learning.

sentences.zh: 位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、納言、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He held the positions of General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with Staff Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, Chief Clerk for Imperial Communications, and Governor of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry, grand master with privileges equal to the three ducal ministers, chief clerk for imperial communications, and governor of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗戲總曰：「卿師尹帝鄉，故當不以富貴威福鄉里邪？」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once joked with Zong, saying: "You command and govern the imperial homeland—surely you do not wield wealth and rank to tyrannize over your native place, do you?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once teased Zong: "As magistrate of the imperial homeland, you surely don't use your rank to lord it over the neighborhood, do you?

sentences.zh: 總乃正色對曰：「陛下擢臣非分，竊謂已鑒愚誠。

translations.literal: Zong then replied with a stern countenance: "Your Majesty raised me beyond my deserts; I privately presumed Your Majesty had already discerned my sincere though humble loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zong answered gravely: "Your Majesty promoted me beyond my merit; I had thought you saw my plain good faith.

sentences.zh: 今奉嚴旨，便似未照丹赤。

translations.literal: Now receiving your stern command, it seems as if my loyal heart has not yet been made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Now this stern admonishment makes me feel my loyalty has not truly been seen.

sentences.zh: 豈可久忝此職，用疑聖慮。

translations.literal: How could I long occupy this post while arousing doubts in Your Majesty's sacred mind?
translations.idiomatic: I cannot hold this office and leave Your Majesty in doubt.

sentences.zh: 請解印綬，以避賢能。」

translations.literal: I request to surrender my seal and cord of office, to yield place to the worthy and capable."
translations.idiomatic: I ask to be relieved of my seal and give way to worthier men."

sentences.zh: 帝大笑曰：「前言戲之耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed greatly and said: "My earlier words were only in jest."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed: "I was only joking."

sentences.zh: 五年，從武帝東征。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he accompanied Emperor Wu on the eastern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined Emperor Wu's eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 總每率麾下，先驅陷敵，遂于并州戰歿，時年二十九。

translations.literal: Zong each time led his troops as vanguard, charging into the enemy; he then died in battle at Bing Province, aged twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Zong always led his men in the van and fell at Bing Province; he was twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈上大將軍，追封河南郡公，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Grand General, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Henan Commandery; his posthumous title was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand General and Duke of Henan Commandery, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 六年，重贈柱國、五州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was again posthumously honored as Pillar of State and Commander of Five Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was further ennobled as Pillar of State and governor of five provinces.

sentences.zh: 子國成嗣，後襲孝寬爵鄖國公。

translations.literal: His son Guocheng succeeded him; later he inherited Xiaokuan's title, Duke of Yun State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guocheng succeeded him and later inherited Xiaokuan's title as Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝追錄孝寬舊勳，開皇初，詔國成食封三千戶，收其租賦。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui recalled Xiaokuan's old merits; at the beginning of the Kaihuang era, an edict granted Guocheng a fief of three thousand households, collecting their rents and taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui remembered Xiaokuan's old service; in the first year of Kaihuang, Guocheng was granted a fief of three thousand households with its revenues.

sentences.zh: 壽字世齡，以貴公子早有令譽。

translations.literal: Shou's courtesy name was Shiling; as the son of a noble house, he early gained a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Shou, courtesy name Shiling, won an excellent reputation early as a nobleman's son.

sentences.zh: 位京兆尹。

translations.literal: He held the position of Governor of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 武帝親征齊，委以後事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally campaigned against Qi, he entrusted him with affairs in his absence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu marched against Qi in person, he left Shou in charge at home.

sentences.zh: 以父軍功，賜爵永安縣侯。

translations.literal: Because of his father's military achievements, he was granted the title Marquis of Yong'an County.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his father's military service he was made Marquis of Yong'an County.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，以其父平尉遲迥，拜夀儀同三司，進封滑國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor, because his father had pacified Yuwen Jiong, Shou was appointed Palace Attendant of the Third Rank and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Hua State.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was regent, in recognition of his father's role in suppressing Yuwen Jiong, Shou was made Palace Attendant of the Third Rank and promoted to Duke of Hua.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，歷位恆、毛二州刺史，頗有能名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, he successively held the posts of Governor of Heng and Mao Provinces, and had a considerable reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jian took the throne, he served as governor of Heng and Mao provinces and earned a solid reputation.

sentences.zh: 以疾征還，卒於家。

translations.literal: He was recalled because of illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled on account of illness, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Ding.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，文帝為晉王昭納其女為妃。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era, Emperor Wen took his daughter as consort for Prince Jin Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era, Emperor Wen married Shou's daughter to his son, Prince Jin Zhao.

sentences.zh: 其子保巒嗣。

translations.literal: His son Baoluan inherited his line.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoluan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 壽弟霽，位太常少卿、安邑縣伯。

translations.literal: Shou's younger brother Ji held the positions of Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Baron of Anyi County.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's younger brother Ji served as vice director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Baron of Anyi County.

sentences.zh: 霽弟津，位內史侍郎、戶部侍郎、判尚書事。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Jin held the positions of Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat, Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, and Acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Jin was vice director of the palace secretariat and the Ministry of Revenue, and acted as director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝寬兄夐。
