translations.literal: Xiaokuan's elder brother Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan's elder brother was Xiong.

sentences.zh: 夐字敬遠，志尚夷簡，澹于榮利。

translations.literal: Xiong's courtesy name was Jingyuan; his aspirations favored tranquility and simplicity, and he was detached from glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong, courtesy name Jingyuan, lived for plain simplicity and cared nothing for rank or gain.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，被召拜雍州中從事，非其好也，遂謝疾去。

translations.literal: At his coming of age he was summoned and appointed Attendant of Yong Province; this was not to his liking, and so he pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he was appointed attendant of Yong Province, declined the post as not to his taste, and withdrew on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 前後十見徵辟，皆不應命。

translations.literal: Ten times in all he was summoned and recruited, yet he never accepted appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Ten separate summonses left him unmoved—he never took office.

sentences.zh: 屬周文帝經綸王業，側席求賢，聞夐養高不仕，虛心敬悅，遣使辟之，備加禮命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was laying the foundations of his royal enterprise, he sat sideways on his mat seeking the worthy; hearing that Xiong lived in lofty reclusion and would not serve, he was sincerely pleased in admiration and sent envoys to recruit him with full ceremonial honors.
translations.idiomatic: As Yuwen Tai was building the Zhou regime, he heard of Xiong's reclusive life and sent envoys with every mark of honor to recruit him.

sentences.zh: 雖情諭甚至，而竟不能屈。

translations.literal: Although his earnest persuasion went to the utmost, in the end he could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: For all his earnest persuasion, he could not prevail upon him.

sentences.zh: 彌以重之，亦弗之奪也。

translations.literal: He only held him in greater esteem and did not force him to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai only respected him the more and did not press the matter.

sentences.zh: 所居之宅，枕帶林泉。

translations.literal: The residence where he lived bordered upon forests and springs.
translations.idiomatic: His home nestled among woods and springs.

sentences.zh: 夐對玩琴書，蕭然自逸，時人號為居士焉。

translations.literal: Xiong would face them playing the zither and reading books, carefree and at ease; people of the time called him a householder-recluse.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his days with lute and books in tranquil ease, and contemporaries called him the Lay Recluse.

sentences.zh: 至有慕其閑素者，或載酒從之，夐亦為之盡歡，接對忘倦。

translations.literal: Even those who admired his quiet simplicity would sometimes bring wine and follow him; Xiong also for their sake gave himself wholly to merriment, receiving and conversing without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Admirers of his quiet life sometimes brought wine to visit; Xiong welcomed them wholeheartedly and never tired of their company.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，禮敬愈厚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, his ritual courtesy and respect grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, his respect for Xiong grew even deeper.

sentences.zh: 乃為詩以貽之曰：「六爻貞遁世，三辰光少微。

translations.literal: He then composed a poem and sent it to him, saying: "The six lines show steadfast withdrawal from the world; the three heavenly bodies shine with the light of Shaowei.
translations.idiomatic: He sent him a poem that began: "Six lines show steadfast withdrawal from the world; three stars burn bright as Shaowei.

sentences.zh: 潁陽讓逾遠，滄州去不歸。

translations.literal: The yielding of Yingyang grows ever more distant; from Cangzhou one departs and does not return.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyang's refusal grows more distant still; from Cangzhou you departed and will not return.

sentences.zh: 香動秋蘭佩，風飄蓮葉衣。

translations.literal: Fragrance stirs on the autumn orchid pendant; wind flutters the lotus-leaf robe.
translations.idiomatic: Orchid scent stirs on your autumn pendant; lotus-leaf robes flutter in the wind.

sentences.zh: 坐石窺仙洞，乘槎下釣磯。

translations.literal: Seated on stone, gazing into an immortal's grotto; riding a raft down to the angler's reef.
translations.idiomatic: You sit on stone and peer into immortal caverns; you ride a raft down to the angler's reef.

sentences.zh: 嶺松千仞直，岩泉百丈飛。

translations.literal: Ridge pines stand a thousand ren straight; cliff springs leap a hundred zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Ridge pines rise a thousand feet straight; cliff springs plunge a hundred yards.

sentences.zh: 聊登平樂觀，遙望首陽薇。

translations.literal: For a moment one climbs the Pingle Observatory, gazing far toward the fern of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: You climb for a while to the Pingle terrace, gazing toward the fern-covered slopes of Mount Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 詎能同四陷，來參余萬機？」

translations.literal: How could you sink together with the four submerged ones, coming to share in my myriad burdens of state?
translations.idiomatic: Could you truly remain sunk in reclusion like the four and yet come share my myriad cares of state?

sentences.zh: 夐答帝詩，願時朝謁。

translations.literal: Xiong replied to the Emperor's poem, expressing the wish to attend court audiences from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong answered with a poem of his own and offered to visit court from time to time.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，敕有司日給河東酒一斗，號之曰逍遙公。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered the relevant offices to supply him daily with one dou of Hedong wine; he styled him the Duke of Carefree Roaming.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, ordered a daily ration of one dou of Hedong wine, and titled him the Carefree Duke.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護執政，廣營第宅。

translations.literal: At that time the Duke of Jin Hu held power and extensively built mansions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuwen Hu, Duke of Jin, held power and built many grand estates.

sentences.zh: 嘗召夐至宅，訪以政事。

translations.literal: He once summoned Xiong to his residence and consulted him on governance.
translations.idiomatic: He once summoned Xiong to his mansion to discuss affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 夐仰視其堂，徐而歎曰：「酣酒嗜音，峻宇雕牆，有一於此，未或弗亡。」

translations.literal: Xiong looked up at his hall and slowly sighed, saying: "Intoxication with wine, love of music, lofty halls and carved walls—if there is one of these, none have ever failed to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong looked up at the hall and sighed: "Drunkenness, debauchery, towering halls and carved walls—where any one of these appears, ruin is never far behind.

sentences.zh: 護不悅。

translations.literal: Hu was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu was displeased.

sentences.zh: 有識者以為知言。

translations.literal: Those with understanding regarded it as words of insight.
translations.idiomatic: The discerning judged his warning prophetic.

sentences.zh: 陳遣其尚書周弘正來聘，素聞夐名，請與相見。

translations.literal: Chen sent its Secretary Director Zhou Hongzheng on a diplomatic visit; having long heard of Xiong's name, he requested a meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Chen sent Minister Zhou Hongzheng on an embassy; knowing Xiong's fame, he asked to meet him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷許之。

translations.literal: The court granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 弘正乃造夐，談謔盡日，恨相遇之晚。

translations.literal: Hongzheng then went to visit Xiong; they talked and jested the whole day, regretting that they had met so late.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng then called on Xiong, and they talked and laughed the day away, lamenting that they had not met sooner.

sentences.zh: 後請夐至賓館，夐不時赴。

translations.literal: Later he invited Xiong to the guest lodge, but Xiong did not come at the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked Xiong to the embassy guesthouse, but Xiong did not appear when expected.

sentences.zh: 弘正乃贈詩曰：「德星猶未動，真車詎肯來？」

translations.literal: Hongzheng then presented a poem saying: "The star of virtue has not yet moved—how would the true carriage deign to come?
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng sent him a poem in reply: "The man of virtue has not stirred; why should an honored guest condescend to come?

sentences.zh: 其為當時所欽挹如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he was admired and respected throughout the age.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗與夐夜宴，大賜之縑帛，令侍臣數人負以送出。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once held a night banquet with Xiong and bestowed on him a great quantity of silk, ordering several attending ministers to carry it out and escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once feasted with Xiong at night and gave him a lavish gift of silk, sending several courtiers to carry the bundles and see him out.

sentences.zh: 夐唯取一匹，示承恩旨而已，帝以此益重之。

translations.literal: Xiong took only one bolt, merely to show that he accepted the imperial favor; the Emperor for this reason esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong accepted only a single bolt, enough to acknowledge the grace shown him, and the emperor valued him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 孝寬為延州總管，夐至州，與孝寬相見。

translations.literal: When Xiaokuan was grand governor of Yan Province, Xiong came to the province and met with Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiaokuan served as grand governor of Yan Province, Xiong traveled there to see him.

sentences.zh: 將還，孝寬以所乘馬及轡勒與夐。

translations.literal: When he was about to return, Xiaokuan gave Xiong the horse he himself rode and its bridle and reins.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiong prepared to leave, Xiaokuan offered him his own mount, complete with bridle and reins.

sentences.zh: 夐以其華飾，心弗欲之。

translations.literal: Xiong, because of its ornate trappings, inwardly did not wish to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong disliked the horse's showy fittings and had no wish to take it.

sentences.zh: 笑謂孝寬曰：「昔人不棄遺簪墜履者，惡與之同出，不與同歸。

translations.literal: Smiling, he said to Xiaokuan: "In olden days men did not abandon a lost hairpin or a fallen shoe, for they disliked setting out together yet not returning together.
translations.idiomatic: He smiled and told Xiaokuan: "Men of old would not leave behind a lost hairpin or fallen shoe, because they hated to set out together yet not return together.

sentences.zh: 吾之操行，雖不逮前烈，然舍舊錄新，亦非吾志也。」

translations.literal: My conduct, though it does not reach that of the ancients, yet to discard the old and record the new is also not my wish.
translations.idiomatic: My principles may fall short of those of the ancients, but to cast aside the old for something new is not my way either.

sentences.zh: 於是乃乘舊馬以歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rode his old horse home.
translations.idiomatic: So he rode his old horse home.

sentences.zh: 武帝又以佛、道、儒三教不同，詔夐辨其優劣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because the three teachings of Buddhism, Daoism, and Confucianism differed, ordered Xiong to distinguish their relative merits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu also ordered Xiong to weigh the relative merits of Buddhism, Daoism, and Confucianism, since the three teachings differed.

sentences.zh: 夐以三教雖殊，同歸於善，其跡似有深淺，其致理如無等級。

translations.literal: Xiong held that although the three teachings differed, they alike returned to goodness; their traces seemed to have depth and shallowness, yet in reaching to principle they were as if without rank or grade.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong replied that though the three teachings differed, all led to goodness; their outward paths might seem deep or shallow, but in ultimate principle they stood on no ladder of rank.

sentences.zh: 乃著《三教序》奏之。

translations.literal: He then composed "A Preface to the Three Teachings" and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote A Preface to the Three Teachings and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and approved.

sentences.zh: 時宣帝在東宮，亦遺夐書，並令以帝所乘馬迎之，問以立身之道。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan was in the Eastern Palace; he also sent Xiong a letter and ordered that the crown prince's own horse be used to welcome him, questioning him on the way to establish oneself in life.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the crown prince, later Emperor Xuan, was in the Eastern Palace; he too wrote to Xiong, sent the prince's own horse to fetch him, and asked how a man should conduct his life.

sentences.zh: 夐對曰：「《傳》不雲乎，儉為德之恭，侈為惡之大。

translations.literal: Xiong replied: "Does not the Commentary say, 'Frugality is the reverence of virtue; extravagance is the greatest of evils'?
translations.idiomatic: Xiong answered: "Does not the Commentary say, 'Frugality is the reverence of virtue, and extravagance the greatest of evils'?

sentences.zh: 欲不可縱，志不可滿。

translations.literal: Desire must not be indulged; ambition must not be filled to fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Desire must not be indulged, and ambition must never be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 並聖人之訓也，願殿下察之。」

translations.literal: Both are the admonitions of sages; I hope Your Highness will consider them."
translations.idiomatic: These are the teachings of the sages; I hope Your Highness will weigh them carefully."

sentences.zh: 夐子瓘，行隨州刺史，因疾物故。

translations.literal: Xiong's son Guan, acting governor of Suizhou, died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's son Guan, who was serving as acting governor of Suizhou, died of illness.

sentences.zh: 孝寬子總復于并州戰歿。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan's son Zong likewise fell in battle at Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan's son Zong also died fighting at Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 一日之中，凶問俱至。

translations.literal: Within a single day, tidings of both deaths arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On the same day news of both deaths arrived.

sentences.zh: 家人相對悲慟，而夐神色自若，謂之曰：「死生命也，去來常事，亦何足悲！」

translations.literal: The family members faced one another in grief and lamentation, but Xiong's expression remained as usual. He said to them: "Life and death are fate; coming and going are ordinary affairs—what is there worth grieving over?
translations.idiomatic: The household wept together, but Xiong's face stayed calm. He told them: "Life and death are fate, and departure an ordinary thing—what is there to mourn?

sentences.zh: 援琴撫之如舊。

translations.literal: He took up his zither and played it as before.
translations.idiomatic: Then he took up his zither and played as he always had.

sentences.zh: 夐又雅好名義，虛襟善誘，雖耕夫牧豎，有一介可稱者，皆接引之。

translations.literal: Xiong also by nature loved reputation and righteousness; with an open breast he was skilled at guiding others. Even plowmen and swineherds, if they had even a little merit to their name, he would all draw them in and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong also cherished honor and integrity, and with an open mind he drew people toward what was good; even farmers and herdsmen, if they showed the least worth, he welcomed and befriended.

sentences.zh: 特與族人處玄及安定梁曠為放逸之友。

translations.literal: In particular he took as friends in free and easy living his clansman Chuxuan and Liang Kuang of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close in his carefree companionship with his kinsman Chuxuan and Liang Kuang of Anding.

sentences.zh: 少愛文史，留情著述，手自抄錄數十萬言。

translations.literal: In youth he loved literature and history, devoting attention to writing, and copied out with his own hand several hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved literature and history, took pleasure in writing, and copied out several hundred thousand characters in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 晚年虛靜，唯以體道會真為務，舊所制述，咸削其槁，故文筆多並不存。

translations.literal: In his later years he became empty and still, devoting himself solely to embodying the Way and meeting with truth; of his old compositions he cut away all the drafts, so that most of his writings no longer survive.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he grew serene and withdrawn, caring only to embody the Way and attain truth; he destroyed the drafts of his earlier writings, so little of his prose survives.

sentences.zh: 建德中，夐以年老，預戒其子等曰：「昔士安以籧篨束體，王孫以布囊繞屍，二賢高達，非庸才能繼。

translations.literal: In the Jiande era, Xiong, because of his advanced age, beforehand admonished his sons and others, saying: "In former times Shi'an bound his body in coarse bamboo matting, and Wang Sun wrapped his corpse in a cloth bag—two worthies of lofty attainment, not men of mediocrity who could follow after them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiande era, feeling his age, Xiong warned his sons in advance: "Long ago Ruan Ji wrapped himself in coarse matting and Wang Sun bound his corpse in a cloth sack—two sages of exalted detachment, not examples any ordinary man can follow.

sentences.zh: 吾死之日，可斂舊衣，勿更新造。

translations.literal: On the day of my death, you may enshroud me in old clothes; do not make new ones.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, dress me in old clothes; do not have new ones made.

sentences.zh: 使棺足周屍，牛車載柩，墳高四尺，壙深一丈。

translations.literal: Let the coffin be just enough to enclose the corpse; let an ox cart carry the bier; let the mound be four feet high and the burial chamber one zhang deep.
translations.idiomatic: Let the coffin be only large enough for my body, let an ox cart carry the bier, let the mound rise four feet and the grave pit be one zhang deep.

sentences.zh: 其餘煩雜，悉無用也。

translations.literal: All other troublesome and elaborate matters are wholly unnecessary.
translations.idiomatic: All other elaborate funeral customs are useless.

sentences.zh: 朝晡奠食，於事彌煩，吾不能頓絕汝輩之情，可朔望一奠而已。

translations.literal: Morning and evening offerings of food would only add to the trouble; I cannot abruptly cut off your feelings, so one offering at the new and full moons will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening sacrifices would only add to the burden; I cannot ask you to stifle your feelings all at once, so offer food once at the new and full moon only.

sentences.zh: 仍薦蔬素，勿設牲牢。

translations.literal: Moreover, offer vegetables and plain fare; do not set out sacrificial livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Use only vegetables and simple fare; do not sacrifice animals.

sentences.zh: 親友欲以物弔祭者，並不得為受。

translations.literal: If relatives and friends wish to offer goods in condolence and sacrifice, you must on no account accept them on my behalf.
translations.idiomatic: If friends and relatives wish to bring gifts for mourning sacrifices, you must not accept them for me.

sentences.zh: 吾常恐臨終恍惚，故以此言預戒汝輩。

translations.literal: I have often feared that at the end I might be confused and unsteady, and therefore use these words beforehand to warn you.
translations.idiomatic: I have often feared I might be confused at the end, so I give you this warning in advance.

sentences.zh: 瞑目之日，勿違吾志也。」

translations.literal: On the day my eyes close, do not go against my wishes.
translations.idiomatic: When I close my eyes, do not betray my wishes.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年二月，卒于家，時年七十七。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Xuanzheng, he died at home, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Xuanzheng he died at home, at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 武帝遣使弔祭，賻賵有加。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices, with additional funeral gifts and contributions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice on his behalf, with generous funeral gifts besides.

sentences.zh: 其喪制葬禮，諸子等並遵其遺戒。

translations.literal: As for mourning regulations and burial rites, his sons all followed his final admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: His sons observed his last instructions in every detail of mourning and burial.

sentences.zh: 子世康。

translations.literal: His son was Shikang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shikang.

sentences.zh: 世康幼而沈敏，有器度。

translations.literal: Shikang from youth was grave and quick-witted, and possessed capacity and breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang was thoughtful and quick-witted from childhood, with real breadth of character.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: At the age of ten he was recruited by the province as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he was recruited by the province as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 在魏，弱冠為直寢，封漢安縣公，尚周文帝女襄樂公主，授儀同三司。

translations.literal: Under Wei, at the capping age he became a guard of the inner quarters, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an County, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was appointed Grand Master with Staff Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei, upon coming of age he became a guard of the imperial bedchamber, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an County, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and received the rank of grand master equal in honor to the three ducal ministers.

sentences.zh: 仕周，歷位典祠下大夫，沔、硤二州刺史。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou, he successively held the posts of lower grand master in the Directorate of Sacrifices and governor of the two provinces of Mian and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he rose through the directorate of sacrifices to lower grand master, and served as governor of Mian and Xia provinces.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，授司州總管長史。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi and was appointed chief administrator to the grand governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu in the conquest of Qi and was made chief administrator to the grand governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 時東夏初定，百姓未安，世康綏撫之，士庶胥悅。

translations.literal: At that time eastern Xia had just been pacified and the common people were not yet settled; Shikang soothed and comforted them, and gentry and commoners alike were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Xia had only just been pacified and the people were still unsettled; Shikang reassured them, and officials and commoners alike were delighted.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部中大夫，進位上開府，轉司會中大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court as middle grand master in the Household Department, was promoted to upper grand master with an independent command, and was transferred to middle grand master in the Directorate of Finance.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as middle grand master in the household department, was promoted to upper grand master with an independent command, and then became middle grand master in the directorate of finance.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥之亂，隋文謂世康曰：「汾、絳舊是周、齊分界，因此亂階，恐生搖動，今以委公。」

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Yuchi Tong, Emperor Wen of Sui said to Shikang: "Fen and Jiang were formerly the boundary between Zhou and Qi; because of this turmoil, I fear unrest may arise there—henceforth I entrust it to you.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuchi Tong's rebellion, Yang Jian told Shikang: "Fen and Jiang were once the border between Zhou and Qi; this uprising may unsettle the region, so I am entrusting it to you.

sentences.zh: 因授絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Accordingly he was appointed governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly appointed governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 以雅望鎮之，闔境清肅。

translations.literal: By his refined reputation he held the province in order, and the whole territory was clear and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: His moral authority kept the province in order, and the whole region grew calm and orderly.

sentences.zh: 世康性恬，素好古，不以得喪幹懷。

translations.literal: Shikang was by nature tranquil, always fond of antiquity, and did not let gain or loss disturb his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang was even-tempered by nature, loved the ways of antiquity, and was unmoved by gain or loss.

sentences.zh: 在州有止足之志，與子弟書曰：「吾生因緒餘，夙沾纓弁，驅馳不已，四紀於茲，亟登袞命，頻蒞方嶽，志除三惑，心慎四知，以不貪而為實，處脂膏而莫潤。

translations.literal: While in the province he had the will to know when to stop; he wrote to his sons and younger brothers, saying: "I was born through inherited lineage, early touched by cap and girdle; without cease I have rushed about, and four decades have passed since then. Repeatedly I have received imperial appointments and often presided over great provinces. I aimed to remove the three confusions and kept my heart wary of the four knows, taking not being greedy as my substance and dwelling amid fat and grease without being stained.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the province he felt it was time to know when enough was enough, and wrote to his sons and brothers: "I was born into a distinguished line and entered official life young; for forty years I have never stopped running from post to post, repeatedly receiving imperial favor and governing great provinces. I have tried to guard against the three temptations and to heed the four knows, making integrity my substance and living amid wealth without being stained by it.

sentences.zh: 如斯之事，頗為時悉。

translations.literal: Matters such as these were quite well known to the age.
translations.idiomatic: The world knows these things of me well enough.

sentences.zh: 今耄雖未及，壯年已謝。

translations.literal: Though I have not yet reached extreme old age, my vigorous years are already gone.
translations.idiomatic: I am not yet truly old, but my prime is already past.

sentences.zh: 霜早梧楸，風先蒲柳。

translations.literal: Frost comes early to the parasol tree and toona; wind strikes first the rushes and willows.
translations.idiomatic: Like the parasol tree and toona that feel the frost early, or the rushes and willows that bow first to the wind, I am aging before my time.

sentences.zh: 眼闇更劇，不見細書；

translations.literal: My eyes have grown dimmer still, and I cannot see fine script;
translations.idiomatic: My eyes have grown dimmer still, and I can no longer read fine script;

sentences.zh: 足疾彌增，非可趨走。

translations.literal: my foot ailment grows worse, and I am no longer fit to hurry about.
translations.idiomatic: my legs trouble me more each day, and I am no longer fit to hurry about.

sentences.zh: 祿豈須多，防滿則退；

translations.literal: Need salary be great? Guard against fullness and withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: One need not hoard rank and salary—when the measure is full, it is time to step back;

sentences.zh: 年不待暮，有疾便辭。

translations.literal: one need not wait for old age—if there is illness, then resign.
translations.idiomatic: one need not wait for old age—when illness comes, one should resign.

sentences.zh: 況昿襄春秋已高，溫清宜奉，晨昏有闕，罪在我躬。

translations.literal: Moreover, Xiong and Xiang are already advanced in years; warm and cool care ought to be offered, and if morning and evening attendance is lacking, the fault lies in my person.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, my parents are already old; I ought to tend to them with filial care, and if I fail them morning and evening, the fault is mine alone.

sentences.zh: 今世穆、世文，並從武役，吾與世沖，復嬰遠任，陟岵瞻望，此情彌切。

translations.literal: Now Shimug and Shiwen are both on military service, while Shichong and I again bear distant appointments; climbing the barren hill and gazing out, this feeling grows ever keener.
translations.idiomatic: Shimug and Shiwen are both away on military duty, while Shichong and I again hold distant posts; the longing I feel when I think of home and parents grows ever sharper.

sentences.zh: 桓山之悲，倍深常戀。

translations.literal: The sorrow of Mount Huan is twice as deep as ordinary longing.
translations.idiomatic: The grief of parting from one's kin is twice as keen as ordinary homesickness.

sentences.zh: 意欲上聞，乞遵禮教，未訪汝等，故遣此及。

translations.literal: I intend to report this above and beg to follow the teachings of ritual; not having yet consulted you, I therefore send this letter to you.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to petition the throne and ask leave to observe filial duty; before consulting you I send this letter.

sentences.zh: 興言遠慕，感咽難勝。」。

translations.literal: At these words my distant yearning rises, and choked emotion is hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: As I write, my longing for home overwhelms me and grief chokes my voice.

sentences.zh: 諸弟報以事恐難遂，乃止。

translations.literal: His younger brothers replied that the matter would probably be hard to accomplish, and so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers answered that the request would likely fail, and he abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 在任有惠政，奏課連最，擢為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: While in office he had benevolent administration; in submitted evaluations he ranked at the top year after year, and he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His tenure brought real benefit to the people, and year after year his performance reviews ranked first; he was promoted to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 世康寡嗜欲，不慕勢貴，未嘗以位望矜物。

translations.literal: Shikang had few desires, did not covet power and rank, and never used position and reputation to look down on others.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang had few desires, cared nothing for power and rank, and never used his station to condescend to others.

sentences.zh: 聞人之善，若己有之，亦不顯人過咎，以求名譽。

translations.literal: When he heard of another's goodness, it was as if he possessed it himself; nor did he expose others' faults and errors in order to seek reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoiced in others' virtues as though they were his own, and never exposed their faults to burnish his own name.

sentences.zh: 進爵上庸郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Shangyong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was ennobled as Duke of Shangyong commandery.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書，選用平允，請托不行。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Civil Service; his selections were fair and even, and private requests did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of the civil service, chose officials fairly, and would not bend to private solicitation.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，固辭，乞終私制。

translations.literal: On mourning for his mother he left office, firmly declined recall, and begged to complete the full private mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office, refused recall, and asked to complete the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 開皇七年，將事江南，議重方鎮，拜襄州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kaihuang, when preparations were being made for affairs in Jiangnan, it was decided that frontier commands should be strengthened, and he was appointed governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kaihuang, as the court prepared for the campaign against the south and sought to strengthen key frontier posts, he was appointed governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office because of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 未幾授安州總管，遷信州總管。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed grand governor of An Province, then transferred to grand governor of Xin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made grand governor of An Province, then transferred to grand governor of Xin Province.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復拜吏部尚書，前後十餘年間，多所進拔，朝廷稱為廉平。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was again appointed Minister of the Civil Service; over the more than ten years before and after, he promoted many men, and the court called him incorrupt and even-handed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he returned as minister of the civil service; over more than a decade in that role he advanced many worthy men, and the court praised him as incorrupt and fair.

sentences.zh: 嘗因休暇，謂子弟曰：「吾聞功遂身退，古人常道。

translations.literal: Once, during a period of rest, he said to his sons and younger brothers: "I have heard that when merit is achieved one withdraws from the body—this is the constant way of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while on leave, he told his sons and brothers: "I have heard that when one's work is done one should withdraw—this is the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 今年將耳順，志在懸車，汝輩以為云何？」

translations.literal: This year I am nearing sixty; my will is to hang up my carriage—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: This year I am nearing sixty, and my wish is to retire; what do you think?

sentences.zh: 子福嗣答曰：「大人澡身浴德，名立官成。

translations.literal: His son Fusi answered: "Father, you have bathed body and bathed virtue; your name is established and your office fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fusi replied: "Father, you have refined your character and fulfilled your office; your name stands secure.

sentences.zh: 盈滿之戒，先哲所重，欲追蹤二疏，伏奉尊命。」

translations.literal: The warning against fullness is what former sages valued; wishing to follow in the footsteps of the Two Shus, I respectfully accept your honored command."
translations.idiomatic: The warning against overreaching is one the ancients took to heart; if you wish to follow the example of the Two Shus, we respectfully agree."

sentences.zh: 後因侍宴，世康再拜陳讓，願乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Later, while attending a banquet, Shikang bowed twice and declared his wish to decline, begging to surrender his bones.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a court banquet, Shikang bowed low and formally asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「冀與公共理天下，今之所請，深乖本望。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I hoped to govern the realm jointly with you; your present request deeply goes against my original wish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I had hoped to govern the realm with you; this request goes deeply against my wishes.

sentences.zh: 縱筋力衰謝，猶屈公臥臨一隅。」

translations.literal: Even if your sinews and strength have declined, I would still bend you to oversee one corner while reclining.
translations.idiomatic: Even if your strength is failing, I would still ask you to govern one region from your repose.

sentences.zh: 於是出拜荊州總管。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went out and was appointed grand governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out as grand governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 時天下唯置荊、並、楊、益四大總管，並、楊、益三州並親王臨統，唯荊州委于世康，時論以此為美。

translations.literal: At that time in the realm only the four grand governorships of Jing, Bing, Yang, and Yi were established; Bing, Yang, and Yi were all directly ruled by imperial princes, and only Jing Province was entrusted to Shikang—contemporary opinion regarded this as a mark of honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time only four grand governorships existed—Jing, Bing, Yang, and Yi; princes directly ruled Bing, Yang, and Yi, while Jing alone was entrusted to Shikang, a distinction widely admired.

sentences.zh: 世康為政簡靜，百姓愛悅。

translations.literal: Shikang's governance was simple and tranquil, and the common people loved and were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang governed with simplicity and calm, and the people loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 卒於州。

translations.literal: He died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 上聞而痛惜，贈大將軍，諡曰文。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it he grieved and regretted the loss; he posthumously awarded him the title of Grand General and gave him the posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved at the news, posthumously honored him as grand general, and gave him the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 世康性孝友，初以諸弟位並隆貴，獨季弟世約宦途不達，共推父時田宅盡以與之。

translations.literal: Shikang was by nature filial and friendly; at first, because all his younger brothers held lofty and honored positions while his youngest brother Shiyue alone had not prospered on the official path, they together yielded all the fields and houses from their father's time and gave them entirely to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang was filial and devoted to his brothers; when all his younger brothers had risen to high rank except his youngest brother Shiyue, who had not prospered, they jointly gave him all their father's land and houses.

sentences.zh: 世多其義。

translations.literal: The age widely praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The world widely praised his generosity.

sentences.zh: 長子福子，位司隸別駕。

translations.literal: His eldest son Fuzi held the position of vice governor of the Metropolitan Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Fuzi served as vice governor of the metropolitan protectorate.

sentences.zh: 次子福嗣，位內史舍人。

translations.literal: His second son Fusi held the position of palace secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Fusi served as a secretary in the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後以罪黜。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed because of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之亂，從衛玄戰，敗於城北，為玄感所獲。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Yang Xuangan, he followed Wei Xu into battle, was defeated north of the city, and was captured by Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: During Yang Xuangan's rebellion he fought under Wei Xu, was defeated north of the city, and was captured by Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 令為文檄，詞甚不遜。

translations.literal: Xuangan ordered him to compose a written proclamation; its language was very insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan forced him to draft a proclamation, and its language was brazenly defiant.

sentences.zh: 尋背玄感還東都，帝銜之，車裂于高陽。

translations.literal: Before long he turned against Xuangan and returned to the Eastern Capital; the Emperor harbored resentment against him and had him torn apart by chariots at Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon deserted Xuangan and returned to the eastern capital, but the emperor never forgave him and had him torn apart by chariots at Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 少子福獎，通事舍人。

translations.literal: His youngest son Fujiang was a communications attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Fujiang served as a communications attendant.

sentences.zh: 在東都，與玄感戰沒。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Capital, he died in battle with Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern capital he fell in battle against Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 世康兄洸，字世穆。

translations.literal: Shikang's elder brother Guang, styled Shimu.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang's elder brother Guang, whose courtesy name was Shimu.

sentences.zh: 性剛毅，有器幹，少便弓馬。

translations.literal: By nature he was firm and resolute; he had capacity and leadership, and from youth was skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was firm and resolute by nature, possessed both talent and authority, and from youth excelled at archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 仕周，釋褐直寢上士。

translations.literal: He served the Zhou; upon first appointment he became Upper Officer of the Direct Attendants of the Inner Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service under the Zhou and, upon leaving mourning, was appointed upper officer of the direct attendants of the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 數從征伐，累遷開府，賜爵衛國縣公。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he followed on campaigns; step by step he was promoted to General Who Opens an Office and was enfeoffed as Duke of Weiguo county.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly took part in campaigns, rose through the ranks to general who opens an office, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Weiguo county.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，從季父孝寬擊尉遲迥于相州，以功拜柱國，進襄陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, he followed his father's younger brother Xiaokuan to attack Yuwen Jiong at Xiang Province; for his merit he was appointed Pillar of State and advanced to Duke of Xiangyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, he followed his uncle Xiaokuan to attack Yuwen Jiong at Xiang Province; for his service he was made pillar of state and advanced to Duke of Xiangyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 時突厥寇邊，皇太子屯咸陽，令洸統兵出原州道。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks raided the frontier; the crown prince stationed at Xianyang and ordered Guang to command troops out along the Yuanzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided the frontier, the crown prince was encamped at Xianyang and ordered Guang to lead troops out by the Yuanzhou route.

sentences.zh: 與虜相遇，擊破之。

translations.literal: He encountered the barbarians and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: He met the enemy and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 拜江陵總管，俄拜安州總管。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand governor of Jiangling; soon afterward he was appointed grand governor of An Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand governor of Jiangling and soon afterward grand governor of An Province.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之役，為行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Chen, he served as campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Chen he served as campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，拜江州總管。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was appointed grand governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was pacified, he was appointed grand governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 略定九江，遂進圖嶺南。

translations.literal: He roughly pacified Jiujiang and then advanced to plan for Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He brought Jiujiang roughly under control and then pressed on toward Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 上與書慰勉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent him a letter of consolation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him a letter of encouragement and praise.

sentences.zh: 洸至廣州，嶺表皆降之。

translations.literal: When Guang reached Guangzhou, all south of the ranges submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang reached Guangzhou, all the lands south of the ranges submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 上聞而大悅，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and was greatly pleased; he granted him discretion to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased at the news and authorized him to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 洸所綏集二十四州，拜廣州總管。

translations.literal: The twenty-four prefectures Guang had brought to submission made him appointed grand governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying twenty-four prefectures, he was appointed grand governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，番禺夷王仲宣反，以兵圍洸，洸拒之，中流矢卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year, the Yue king Zhongxuan of Panyu rebelled, besieged Guang with troops; Guang resisted him but was struck by an arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the Yue chieftain Zhongxuan of Panyu rebelled and besieged Guang with troops; Guang held him off but was struck by an arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 贈上柱國，賜綿絹萬段，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded Upper Pillar of State, granted ten thousand rolls of silk, and given the posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as upper pillar of state, granted ten thousand bolts of silk, and given the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 子協，字欽仁。

translations.literal: His son Xie, styled Qinren.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie, whose courtesy name was Qinren.

sentences.zh: 好學有雅量，位秘書郎。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had generous breadth of mind; he held the position of secretary in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and possessed a generous temperament; he served as a secretary in the palace library.

sentences.zh: 其父在廣州有功，上命協齎詔書勞問，未至而父卒。

translations.literal: His father had merit at Guangzhou; the Emperor ordered Xie to carry an edict of commendation and inquiry, but before he arrived his father died.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had rendered distinguished service at Guangzhou, the emperor ordered Xie to carry an edict of commendation—but before he arrived, his father had died.

sentences.zh: 上以其父死王事，拜協柱國，曆定、息、秦三州刺史，有能名。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because his father had died in the king's service, appointed Xie Pillar of State; he served successively as governor of Ding, Xi, and Qin provinces and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died in the emperor's service, the emperor appointed Xie pillar of state; he served in turn as governor of Ding, Xi, and Qin provinces and earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 洸弟瓘，字世恭。

translations.literal: Guang's younger brother Guan, styled Shigong.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's younger brother Guan, whose courtesy name was Shigong.

sentences.zh: 禦正下大夫，儀同三司、行隨州刺史。

translations.literal: Lower Grand Master of Imperial Rectification, Equal in Rank to Three Offices, and acting governor of Sui Province.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of lower grand master of imperial rectification, equal in rank to three offices, and acting governor of Sui Province.

sentences.zh: 瓘弟藝，字世文。

translations.literal: Guan's younger brother Yi, styled Shiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's younger brother Yi, whose courtesy name was Shiwen.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，以軍功位上儀同，賜爵修武縣侯，授左旅下大失，出為魏郡太守。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wu of Zhou, for military merit he attained Upper Equal in Rank, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu county, was appointed Lower Grand Master of the Left Brigade, and went out as prefect of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he rose for military merit to upper equal in rank, was enfeoffed as marquis of Xiuwu county, appointed lower grand master of the left brigade, and sent out as prefect of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝為丞相，尉遲迥陰圖不軌，朝廷遣藝季父孝寬馳往代迥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Yuwen Jiong secretly plotted rebellion; the court dispatched Yi's father's younger brother Xiaokuan to hurry and replace Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister and Yuwen Jiong was secretly plotting rebellion, the court sent Yi's uncle Xiaokuan posthaste to replace him.

sentences.zh: 孝寬將至鄴，詐病止傳舍，從迥求藥，以密觀變。

translations.literal: When Xiaokuan was about to reach Ye, he feigned illness and stopped at a relay station, asking Jiong for medicine in order secretly to observe developments.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiaokuan was nearing Ye, he feigned illness and halted at a relay station, asking Jiong for medicine so he could secretly watch how matters stood.

sentences.zh: 藝因投孝寬，即從孝寬擊迥。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon went over to Xiaokuan and at once followed him in attacking Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Yi then defected to Xiaokuan and immediately joined him in attacking Jiong.

sentences.zh: 以功進位上大將軍，改封武威縣公，以修武縣侯別封一子。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced to Grand General-in-Chief, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Wuwei county, and one son was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu county.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to grand general-in-chief, his enfeoffment was changed to duke of Wuwei county, and one son was separately enfeoffed as marquis of Xiuwu county.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，進封魏興郡公，拜齊州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, he was advanced to Duke of Weixing commandery and appointed governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen accepted the abdication, Yi was advanced to duke of Weixing commandery and appointed governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 為政通簡，士庶懷惠。

translations.literal: His governance was open and simple, and scholars and commoners cherished his bounty.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with openness and simplicity, and both gentry and common people were grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 遷營州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to grand governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 藝容貌瑰偉，每夷狄參謁，必整儀衛，盛服以見之，獨坐滿一榻。

translations.literal: Yi's appearance was magnificent; whenever barbarians came to pay their respects, he always arrayed guards of honor and received them in full regalia, sitting alone and filling an entire couch.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was imposing in appearance; whenever barbarians came to pay their respects, he always arrayed an honor guard, received them in full ceremonial dress, and sat alone occupying an entire couch.

sentences.zh: 蕃人畏懼，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: The frontier peoples feared him, and none dared look up at him.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier peoples feared him and none dared meet his gaze.

sentences.zh: 而大修產業，與北夷貿易，家資巨萬。

translations.literal: Yet he greatly expanded estates and traded with the northern barbarians until his household wealth reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he greatly expanded his estates, traded with the northern tribes, and amassed household wealth in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 頗為清論所譏。

translations.literal: He was much ridiculed by men of pure reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely criticized by men of upright reputation.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰懷。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Huai.

sentences.zh: 藝弟沖，字世沖。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Chong, styled Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Chong, whose courtesy name was Shichong.

sentences.zh: 以名家子，在周釋褐衛公府禮曹參軍。

translations.literal: As the son of an eminent family, in Zhou upon first appointment he became a member of the Rituals Section staff in the Duke of Wei's office.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a distinguished family, he entered Zhou service upon leaving mourning as a member of the rituals section in the office of the Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍元定度江伐陳，為陳人所虜。

translations.literal: He followed Grand General Yuan Ding in crossing the Yangzi to attack Chen and was captured by the Chen forces.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand General Yuan Ding in crossing the Yangzi to attack Chen and was captured by the Chen.

sentences.zh: 周武帝以幣贖還之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou redeemed him with gifts and had him returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou ransomed him with gifts and had him returned.

sentences.zh: 帝復令沖以馬千匹使陳，贖開府賀拔華等五十人及元定之柩而還。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent Chong as envoy to Chen with a thousand horses, redeemed fifty men including General Who Opens an Office Heba Hua and Yuan Ding's coffin, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Chong as envoy to Chen with a thousand horses, redeemed fifty men including General Who Opens an Office Heba Hua along with Yuan Ding's coffin, and returned.

sentences.zh: 沖有辭辯，奉使稱旨。

translations.literal: Chong had eloquence; on diplomatic missions he fully met the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was eloquent, and on diplomatic missions he fully satisfied the emperor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 累遷小禦伯下大夫，加上儀同，拜汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Step by step he was promoted to Lower Grand Master of the Lesser Imperial Guard, given Upper Equal in Rank, and appointed governor of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to lower grand master of the lesser imperial guard, was given upper equal in rank, and was appointed governor of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐阼，征兼散騎常侍，進位開府，賜爵安固縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui acceded to the throne, he was summoned and made concurrent Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, advanced to General Who Opens an Office, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Angu county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui acceded to the throne, Chong was summoned and made concurrent regular attendant-in-ordinary, advanced to general who opens an office, and enfeoffed as marquis of Angu county.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，發南汾州胡千餘人北築長城，在途皆亡。

translations.literal: After more than a year, over a thousand Hu of southern Fen Province were dispatched north to build the Great Wall, and all fled en route.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, over a thousand Hu from southern Fen Province were sent north to build the Great Wall, and all of them fled along the way.

sentences.zh: 上呼沖問計，沖曰：「皆由牧宰不稱所致，請以理綏靜，可不勞兵而定。」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Chong to ask his plan; Chong said: "This is all caused by unfit local governors; I ask to calm them through reason, and they can be settled without troubling the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Chong to ask his advice. Chong said, "This is all because the local governors are unfit. Allow me to calm them through reason, and they can be settled without sending troops.

sentences.zh: 上因命沖綏懷叛者，月餘，並赴長城。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon ordered Chong to win over and soothe the rebels; after more than a month, they all went to the Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Chong to win over the deserters, and after little more than a month they all reported to the Great Wall.

sentences.zh: 上降書勞勉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued a letter downward commending and encouraging him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent down a letter commending and encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 尋拜石州刺史，甚得諸胡歡心。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Shi Province and won the hearts of the various Hu very well.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Shi Province and won the wholehearted support of the various Hu peoples.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office due to mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 俄起為南寧州總管，持節撫慰，復遣柱國王長述以兵繼進。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as grand governor of Nanning Province, bearing the tally to comfort and reassure; the Pillar of State Wang Changshu was again dispatched with troops to follow after.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as grand governor of Nanning Province with imperial credentials to reassure the region, and the pillar of state Wang Changshu was again sent with troops to follow in support.

sentences.zh: 沖既至南寧，渠帥首領皆詣府參謁。

translations.literal: When Chong reached Nanning, all the chieftain leaders came to the headquarters to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong reached Nanning, all the tribal chieftains came to his headquarters to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，下詔褒揚之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 其兄子伯仁隨沖在府，掠人之妻，士卒縱暴，邊人失望。

translations.literal: His nephew Boren followed Chong at the headquarters, seized another man's wife, and the soldiers ran wild; the frontier people lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Boren accompanied Chong at headquarters, seized another man's wife, and the soldiers ran wild; the frontier people lost all hope in them.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，大怒，令蜀王秀按其事。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he was furious and ordered Prince Xiu of Shu to investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he was furious and ordered Prince Xiu of Shu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 益州長史元岩性方正，按沖無所寬貸。

translations.literal: The chief administrator of Yi Province, Yuan Yan, was by nature upright; in investigating Chong he showed no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yan, chief administrator of Yi Province, was upright by nature and showed Chong no leniency in the investigation.

sentences.zh: 竟坐免官。

translations.literal: In the end Chong was dismissed from office because of the case.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Chong was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 其弟太子洗馬世約譖岩于皇太子。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shiyue, Crown Prince's Court Man, slandered Yan to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shiyue, a court man of the crown prince, slandered Yuan Yan to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 上謂太子曰：「古人云：'酤酒酸而不售者，為噬犬耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the crown prince: "The ancients say: 'When wine for sale turns sour and will not sell, it is because of the biting dog.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the crown prince, "The ancients said, 'When wine turns sour and will not sell, it is because of the dog that bites.

sentences.zh: '今何用世約乎！」

translations.literal: Why employ Shiyue now!
translations.idiomatic: Why should we employ Shiyue now!

sentences.zh: 世約遂除名。

translations.literal: Shiyue was thereupon struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyue was thereupon struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 後令沖檢校括州事。

translations.literal: Later Chong was ordered to inspect and oversee affairs of Kuo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chong was ordered to inspect affairs in Kuo Province.

sentences.zh: 時東陽賊帥陶子定、吳州賊帥羅慧方並聚眾為亂，沖率兵破之。

translations.literal: At that time the bandit chief Taozi Ding of Dongyang and the bandit chief Luo Huifang of Wu Province both gathered crowds and rebelled; Chong led troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the bandit leaders Taozi Ding of Dongyang and Luo Huifang of Wu Province both gathered followers in rebellion; Chong led troops and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 改封義豐縣侯，檢校泉州事，遷營州總管。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Yifeng county; he inspected affairs of Quan Province and was transferred to grand governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: His enfeoffment was changed to marquis of Yifeng county; he was assigned to inspect affairs in Quan Province and then transferred to grand governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 沖容貌都雅，寬厚得眾心，撫靺羯、契丹，皆能致其死力。

translations.literal: Chong's appearance was refined and elegant; generous and steady, he won men's hearts; in governing the Mohe and Khitan, he could bring out their utmost effort unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was refined and elegant in appearance, generous and steady, and won the hearts of his men; in governing the Mohe and Khitan he could bring them to give their utmost, even unto death.

sentences.zh: 奚、勣畏懼，朝貢相續。

translations.literal: The Xi and Kumo Xi feared him, and tribute missions followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi and Kumo Xi were awed into submission, and tribute missions followed in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 高麗嘗入寇，衝擊走之。

translations.literal: Goguryeo once raided the border; Chong struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo once raided the border, Chong struck and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 及文帝為豫章王暕納沖女為妃，徵拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took Chong's daughter as consort for Prince Zhang of Yuzhang, Yang Jian, Chong was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took Chong's daughter as consort for Prince Zhang of Yuzhang, Yang Jian, Chong was summoned and appointed minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 少子挺知名。

translations.literal: His youngest son Ting became well known.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Ting became well known.

sentences.zh: 韋瑱，字世珍，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhen, styled Shizhen, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhen, whose courtesy name was Shizhen, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 世為三輔著姓。

translations.literal: For generations his family had been a prominent clan of the Three Adjuncts.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been a prominent clan of the Three Adjuncts.

sentences.zh: 曾祖惠度，姚泓尚書郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Huidu had been a Secretariat Gentleman under Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Huidu had served Yao Hong as a secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 隨劉義真過江，仕宋為順陽太守、行南雍州事。

translations.literal: He followed Liu Yizhen in crossing the Yangzi, served Song as prefect of Shunyang and acting governor of Southern Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Liu Yizhen in crossing the Yangzi and served the Song as prefect of Shunyang and acting governor of Southern Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 後於襄陽歸魏，拜中書侍郎，贈洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Later at Xiangyang he submitted to Wei, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and posthumously awarded Governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at Xiangyang, he submitted to Wei, was appointed vice director of the secretariat, and was posthumously honored as governor of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 祖千雄，略陽郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qianxiong had been commandery prefect of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qianxiong had been prefect of Lueyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父英，代郡守，贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ying had been commandery prefect of Dai and was posthumously awarded Governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ying had been prefect of Dai commandery and was posthumously honored as governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 瑱幼聰敏，有夙成之量。

translations.literal: Zhen was clever from childhood and had the measure of precocious maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was clever from childhood and showed the promise of precocious maturity.

sentences.zh: 起家太尉府法曹參軍，累遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He began his career as a member of the Law Section staff in the Grand Marshal's office and was promoted step by step to Remonstrating and Advising Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a law-section staff member in the grand marshal's office and rose through the ranks to remonstrating and advising grand master.

sentences.zh: 周文帝為丞相，封長安縣男。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was chief minister, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Chang'an county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was chief minister, he was enfeoffed as baron of Chang'an county.

sentences.zh: 轉行台左丞，遷南郢州刺史，復令為行台左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Director of the Branch Secretariat, promoted to governor of Southern Ying Province, and then again made Left Director of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left director of the branch secretariat, promoted to governor of Southern Ying Province, and then again appointed left director of the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 瑱明察有幹局，再居左轄，時論榮之。

translations.literal: Zhen was perceptive and had administrative capacity; holding the left directorship twice, contemporary opinion regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was perceptive and capable in administration; to hold the left directorship twice was regarded at the time as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 從復弘農，戰沙苑，加衛大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He followed in the recovery of Hongnong and fought at Shayuan; he was given the titles of Guard General and Left Grand Master of Radiant Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the recovery of Hongnong and fought at Shayuan, and was given the titles of guard general and left grand master of radiant virtue.

sentences.zh: 從戰河橋，進爵為子。

translations.literal: He followed in the battle at Heqiao and was advanced in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Heqiao and was advanced in rank to viscount.

sentences.zh: 大統八年，齊神武侵汾、絳，瑱從周文禦之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Datong, Gao Huan of Qi invaded Fen and Jiang; Zhen followed Emperor Wen of Zhou to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Datong, when Gao Huan of Qi invaded Fen and Jiang, Zhen followed Emperor Wen of Zhou to resist him.

sentences.zh: 軍還，以本官鎮蒲津關，帶中氵單城主。

translations.literal: When the army returned, with his former office he garrisoned Pujin Pass and concurrently served as garrison commander of Zhongmian city.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he retained his former rank to garrison Pujin Pass and concurrently served as garrison commander of Zhongmian city.

sentences.zh: 曆鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He served successively as Chamberlain for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chamberlain for dependencies.

sentences.zh: 以望族兼領鄉兵，加帥都督，進散騎常侍。

translations.literal: As a member of an eminent clan he concurrently led local militia, was given the rank of commander-in-chief, and advanced to Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of an eminent clan he concurrently led local militia, was made commander-in-chief, and advanced to regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 三年，除瓜州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed governor of Gua Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed governor of Gua Province.

sentences.zh: 州通西域，蕃夷往來，前後刺史多受賂遺，胡寇犯邊，又莫能禦。

translations.literal: The province connected to the Western Regions; barbarians of many kinds came and went; successive governors often accepted bribes, and when Hu raiders violated the frontier none could repel them.
translations.idiomatic: The province lay on the route to the Western Regions, with many tribes passing through; successive governors had often taken bribes, and when Hu raiders struck the frontier none had been able to repel them.

sentences.zh: 瑱雅性清儉，兼有武略，蕃夷贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: Zhen was by nature refined and frugal and also possessed military strategy; from barbarian gifts he accepted not a single one.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was refined and frugal by nature and also possessed military talent; he accepted none of the gifts offered by the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 胡人畏威，不敢為寇。

translations.literal: The Hu feared his authority and did not dare raid.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu feared his authority and did not dare raid.

sentences.zh: 公私安靜，夷夏懷之。

translations.literal: Public and private affairs were peaceful; both barbarians and Chinese cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private life were peaceful, and both barbarians and Chinese held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，進爵平齊縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, he was advanced to Baron of Pingqi county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou acceded to the throne, Zhen was advanced to baron of Pingqi county.

sentences.zh: 秩滿還京，吏人戀慕，老幼追送，留連十數日方得出境。

translations.literal: When his term expired he returned to the capital; officials and people yearned after him, old and young pursued to see him off, and for more than ten days he lingered before he could leave the border.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired and he returned to the capital, officials and people alike were loath to see him go; old and young pursued him to bid farewell, and for more than ten days he lingered before he could leave the region.

sentences.zh: 明帝嘉之，授侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming commended this and appointed him Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Director of a Department with the same rank as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming praised this and appointed him palace attendant, general of agile cavalry, and director of a department equal in rank to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈岐、宜二州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Governor of the two provinces of Qi and Yi, with the posthumous name Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made governor of Qi and Yi provinces, with the posthumous name Hui.

sentences.zh: 又追封為公，詔其子峻襲。

translations.literal: He was further enfeoffed posthumously as duke, and an edict ordered his son Jun to succeed to the title.
translations.idiomatic: He was further enfeoffed posthumously as duke, and an edict ordered his son Jun to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 峻位至車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Jun rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Jun rose to general of chariots and cavalry with rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 峻子德政，隋大業中給事郎。

translations.literal: Jun's son Dezheng, during the Daye era of Sui, was Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son Dezheng served as attendant gentleman during the Daye reign of Sui.

sentences.zh: 峻弟師。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's younger brother was Shi.

sentences.zh: 師字公穎。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Gongying.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, styled Gongying.

sentences.zh: 少沈謹，有至性。

translations.literal: From youth he was deep and careful, with utmost sincerity of nature.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was thoughtful and reserved, with a deeply sincere nature.

sentences.zh: 初就學，始讀《孝經》，舍書而歎曰：「名教之極，其在茲乎！」

translations.literal: When he first went to study and began reading the Classic of Filial Piety, he set down the book and sighed, saying, "The ultimate of the teaching of names—is it not here!
translations.idiomatic: When he first went to school and began reading the Classic of Filial Piety, he put the book aside and sighed, "The highest point of moral teaching—is it not here!

sentences.zh: 少丁父母憂，居喪盡禮，州裏稱其有孝行。

translations.literal: While still young he suffered the loss of his parents; in mourning he fulfilled every rite, and the district praised his filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he lost both parents; in mourning he observed every rite, and the district praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及長，略涉經史，尤工騎射。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he broadly touched upon the classics and histories and was especially skilled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, he gained a general knowledge of the classics and histories and was especially skilled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為中外府記室，轉賓曹參軍。

translations.literal: Yuwen Hu, Grand Minister of the Zhou, brought him in as secretary of the Central and External Office, then transferred him to aide of the Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu, the Zhou grand minister, brought him in as secretary of the central and external office, then transferred him to aide in the guests bureau.

sentences.zh: 師雅知諸蕃風俗及山川險易，其有夷狄朝貢，師必接對，論其國俗，如視諸掌。

translations.literal: Shi was well acquainted with the customs of the various frontier peoples and with the ease or difficulty of mountains and rivers. Whenever barbarians came to court with tribute, Shi always received them and discussed their national customs, as if viewing them in the palm of his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Shi knew the customs of the frontier peoples and the lay of their mountains and rivers intimately. Whenever foreign envoys came with tribute, he received them and discussed their countries' ways as clearly as if they lay in the palm of his hand.

sentences.zh: 夷人驚服，無敢陷情。

translations.literal: The barbarians were astonished and submitted; none dared conceal the truth.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys were astonished and deferential, and none dared withhold the truth.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲為雍州牧，引為主簿，本官如故。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Xian was governor of Yong Province, he brought him in as chief clerk; his former office remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xian of Qi became governor of Yong Province, he brought Shi in as chief clerk while Shi retained his former rank.

sentences.zh: 及武帝親總萬機，轉少府大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs of state, he was transferred to Grand Officer of the Privy Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu personally assumed control of state affairs, Shi was transferred to grand officer of the privy treasury.

sentences.zh: 及齊平，詔師安撫山東。

translations.literal: When Qi was pacified, an edict ordered Shi to pacify and reassure Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was conquered, an edict ordered Shi to pacify and reassure the Shandong region.

sentences.zh: 徙為賓部大夫。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Officer of the Guests Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand officer of the guests department.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，拜吏部侍郎，賜爵井陘侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and granted the title Marquis of Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Shi was appointed vice director of the ministry of personnel and granted the title Marquis of Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 遷河北道行台兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War of the Hebei Circuit Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of war of the Hebei circuit mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 奉詔為山東、河南十八州安撫大使。

translations.literal: By imperial order he became Pacification Commissioner over the eighteen provinces of Shandong and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he was made pacification commissioner over the eighteen provinces of Shandong and Henan.

sentences.zh: 奏事稱旨，兼領晉王廣司馬。

translations.literal: His memorials pleased the emperor, and he additionally served as secretary to Prince Jin Guang.
translations.idiomatic: His reports pleased the emperor, and he was additionally appointed secretary to Prince Jin Yang Guang.

sentences.zh: 其族人世康為吏部尚書，與師素懷勝負。

translations.literal: His clansman Shikang served as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and had long harbored a sense of rivalry with Shi.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Shikang was director of the ministry of personnel and had long nursed a competitive rivalry with Shi.

sentences.zh: 于時廣為雍州牧，盛存望第，以司空楊雄、尚書左僕射高熲並為州都，引師為主簿，而世康弟世約為法曹從事。

translations.literal: At that time Guang was governor of Yong Province; his princely residence flourished and commanded wide admiration. Minister of Works Yang Xiong and Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Gao Jiong were both made provincial chiefs, Shi was brought in as chief clerk, and Shikang's younger brother Shiyue served as aide in the Legal Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Guang was governor of Yong Province, and his princely residence flourished and drew wide admiration. Minister of Works Yang Xiong and Left Vice Director Gao Jiong were both made provincial chiefs; Shi was brought in as chief clerk, while Shikang's younger brother Shiyue served as aide in the legal bureau.

sentences.zh: 世康恚恨不能食，又恥世約在師之下，召世約數之曰：「汝何故為從事！」

translations.literal: Shikang was resentful and could not eat; he was also ashamed that Shiyue served under Shi. He summoned Shiyue and rebuked him, saying, "Why do you serve as an aide!
translations.idiomatic: Shikang was so resentful he could not eat, and he was ashamed that Shiyue ranked below Shi. He summoned Shiyue and rebuked him: "Why are you serving as a mere aide!

sentences.zh: 遂杖之。

translations.literal: He then had him beaten with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: He then had him beaten with a staff.

sentences.zh: 後從上幸醴泉宮，上召師與左僕射高熲、上柱國韓擒等於臥內賜宴，令各敘舊事，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: Later he followed the emperor on a visit to Liquan Palace. The emperor summoned Shi, Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, Supreme Pillar of State Han Qin, and others to a banquet within the inner apartments, ordering each to relate old stories for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the emperor to Liquan Palace. The emperor summoned Shi, Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, supreme pillar of state Han Qin, and others to a banquet in the inner apartments and had each tell old stories for amusement.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以本官領元帥掾。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, with his former office he served as aide to the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign to conquer Chen, he retained his former rank and served as aide to the commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 陳國府藏，悉委于師，秋毫無犯，稱為清白。

translations.literal: The treasuries of the Chen state were all entrusted to Shi; he did not violate even a hair's breadth and was praised as incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: The treasuries of the Chen state were all entrusted to Shi; he did not take so much as a hair's worth and was praised for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 後上為長寧王儼納其女為妃。

translations.literal: Later the emperor had Prince of Changning Yan take his daughter as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor had Prince Yan of Changning take Shi's daughter as his consort.

sentences.zh: 除汴州刺史，甚有政名。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Bian Province and gained an excellent reputation for governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Bian Province and earned a strong reputation for good administration.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was given the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 師宗人暮，仕周，位內史大夫。

translations.literal: Shi's clansman Mu served the Zhou and rose to Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's clansman Mu served the Zhou and rose to grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝初，以定策功，累遷上柱國，封普安郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Sui, for his merit in settling the succession plan he was repeatedly promoted to Supreme Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Pu'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wen of Sui's reign, for his merit in settling the succession he was repeatedly promoted to supreme pillar of state and enfeoffed as Duke of Pu'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，卒于蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he died while serving as governor of Pu Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era he died while serving as governor of Pu Province.

sentences.zh: 柳虯，字仲盤，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Qiu, styled Zhongpan, was a native of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiu, styled Zhongpan, was a native of Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 五世祖恭，仕後趙為河東郡守。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Gong served Later Zhao as Administrator of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Gong served Later Zhao as administrator of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 後以秦、趙喪亂，率人南徙，居汝、潁間，遂仕江表。

translations.literal: Later, because of the chaos and ruin in Qin and Zhao, he led people south to migrate, settling between the Ru and Ying rivers, and then served in the Jianghuai region.
translations.idiomatic: Later, amid the chaos in Qin and Zhao, he led people south to resettle between the Ru and Ying rivers and then entered service in the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 祖緝，宋司州別駕、宋安郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ji was Vice Governor of Si Province under Song and Administrator of Song'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ji served the Song as vice governor of Si Province and administrator of Song'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 父僧習，善隸書，敏於當世。

translations.literal: His father Sengxi was skilled in clerical script and quick-witted in affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengxi was skilled in clerical script and quick-witted in the affairs of his day.

sentences.zh: 與豫州刺史裴叔業據州歸魏，曆北地潁川二郡守、揚州大中正。

translations.literal: Together with Governor of Yu Province Pei Shuye he held the province and submitted to Wei; he served successively as Administrator of the two commanderies Beidi and Yingchuan, and as Chief Rectifier of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Governor of Yu Province Pei Shuye he held the province and submitted to Wei, then served successively as administrator of Beidi and Yingchuan commanderies and as chief rectifier of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 虯年十三，便專精好學。
