translations.literal: At thirteen Qiu devoted himself exclusively to earnest study.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Qiu devoted himself wholeheartedly to study.

sentences.zh: 時貴游子弟就學者，並車服華盛，唯虯不事容飾。

translations.literal: At the time the sons of noble families who went to study all had splendid carriages and dress, but Qiu alone did not bother with adornment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the sons of noble families who went to school all had splendid carriages and dress, but Qiu alone did not bother with adornment.

sentences.zh: 遍受五經，略通大義，兼涉子史，雅好屬文。

translations.literal: He received instruction in all Five Classics, broadly grasped their essential meaning, also ranged into Masters and histories, and greatly loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He studied all Five Classics and grasped their main points, also ranged through the masters and histories, and greatly loved writing.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，揚州刺史李憲舉虯秀才，兗州刺史馮俊引虯為府主簿。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, Governor of Yang Province Li Xian recommended Qiu as a cultivated talent; Governor of Yan Province Feng Jun brought Qiu in as chief clerk of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era, Governor of Yang Province Li Xian recommended Qiu as a cultivated talent, and Governor of Yan Province Feng Jun brought him in as chief clerk of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 既而樊子鵠為吏部尚書，其兄義為揚州刺史，乃以虯為揚州中從事，加鎮遠將軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Fan Zihe became Director of the Ministry of Personnel; his elder brother Yi was governor of Yang Province, and so Qiu was made Central Aide of Yang Province and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Fan Zihe became director of the ministry of personnel; his elder brother Yi was governor of Yang Province, and Qiu was made central aide of Yang Province with the additional title general who pacifies the distance.

sentences.zh: 非其好也，並棄官還洛陽。

translations.literal: These were not to his liking, and he abandoned both offices and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: These posts did not suit him, and he resigned from both and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 屬天下喪亂，乃退耕于陽城，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: As the realm fell into chaos, he withdrew to farm at Yangcheng, with the intent to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: As the realm fell into chaos, he withdrew to farm at Yangcheng, intending to live out his days there.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，馮翊王元季海、領軍獨孤信鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Prince of Fufeng Yuan Jihai and Director of the Guards Dugu Xin garrisoned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, Prince Jihai of Fufeng and Director of the Guards Dugu Xin garrisoned Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 于時舊京荒廢，人物罕存，唯有虯在陽城，裴諏在潁川。

translations.literal: At that time the old capital was desolate and abandoned, and people were rarely to be found; only Qiu was at Yangcheng and Pei Zou was at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the old capital lay in ruins and few people remained; only Qiu was at Yangcheng and Pei Zou at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 信等乃俱征之，以虯為行台郎中，諏為北府屬，並掌文翰。

translations.literal: Xin and the others then summoned them both; Qiu was made Secretariat Director of the Mobile Headquarters and Zou was made aide of the Northern Headquarters, both in charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and the others then summoned them both: Qiu was made secretariat director of the mobile headquarters and Zou aide of the northern headquarters, and both were put in charge of documents.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「北府裴諏，南府柳虯。」

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying: "Pei Zou of the Northern Headquarters, Liu Qiu of the Southern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time had a saying: "Pei Zou of the northern headquarters, Liu Qiu of the southern headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時軍旅務殷，虯勵精從事，或通夜不寢。

translations.literal: At that time military affairs were pressing; Qiu drove himself in his duties and sometimes did not sleep all night.
translations.idiomatic: At that time military affairs were pressing; Qiu threw himself into his work and sometimes went all night without sleep.

sentences.zh: 季海常云：「柳郎中判事，我不復重看。」

translations.literal: Jihai often said, "When Director Liu Qiu decides cases, I need not review them again.
translations.idiomatic: Jihai often said, "When Director Liu Qiu decides cases, I need not look them over again.

sentences.zh: 四年入朝，周文帝欲官之，虯辭母老，乞侍醫藥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered court; Emperor Wen of Zhou wished to appoint him to office, but Qiu declined citing his aged mother, begging to attend her with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he went to court; Emperor Wen of Zhou wished to appoint him to office, but Qiu declined on the grounds that his mother was old and begged to stay with her and tend her with medicine.

sentences.zh: 周文許焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou granted his request.

sentences.zh: 又為獨孤信開府從事中郎。

translations.literal: He also served as Attendant Secretary of Dugu Xin's independent office.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as attendant secretary of Dugu Xin's independent office.

sentences.zh: 信出鎮隴右，因為秦州刺史，以虯為二府司馬。

translations.literal: When Xin went out to garrison Longyou and thereby became governor of Qin Province, he made Qiu secretary of both offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin went out to garrison Longyou and thereby became governor of Qin Province, he made Qiu secretary of both offices.

sentences.zh: 雖處元僚，不綜府事，唯在信左右談論而已。

translations.literal: Although he held a senior staff post, he did not oversee headquarters affairs but merely conversed at Xin's side.
translations.idiomatic: Although he held a senior staff post, he did not manage headquarters affairs but merely talked at Xin's side.

sentences.zh: 因使見周文，被留為丞相府記室。

translations.literal: On a mission he saw Emperor Wen of Zhou and was detained as secretary of the chancellor's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission he saw Emperor Wen of Zhou and was kept on as secretary of the chancellor's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 追論歸朝功，封美陽縣男。

translations.literal: In recognition of his merit in returning to the court, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Meiyang county.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his merit in returning to court, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Meiyang county.

sentences.zh: 虯以史官密書善惡，未足懲勸，乃上疏曰：「古者人君立史官，非但記事而已，蓋所為鑒誡也。

translations.literal: Qiu believed that historians secretly recording good and evil was insufficient to warn and encourage, and so submitted a memorial saying, "In antiquity when rulers established historiographers, it was not merely to record affairs but to serve as mirror and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu believed that historians' secret recording of good and evil was insufficient to warn and encourage, and so submitted a memorial saying, "In antiquity when rulers established historiographers, it was not merely to record events but to provide a mirror and a warning.

sentences.zh: 動則左史書之，言則右史書之，彰善癉惡，以樹風聲。

translations.literal: When they acted, the left historiographer recorded it; when they spoke, the right historiographer recorded it—manifesting good and reproving evil to establish moral influence.
translations.idiomatic: When they acted, the left historiographer recorded it; when they spoke, the right historiographer recorded it—making good manifest and evil reproved, so as to establish moral example.

sentences.zh: 故南史抗節，表崔杼之罪；

translations.literal: Thus the southern historiographer held firm and exposed Cui Zhu's crime;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the southern historiographer held firm and exposed Cui Zhu's crime;

sentences.zh: 董狐書法，明趙盾之愆。

translations.literal: Dong Hu's brushwork made Zhao Dun's fault clear.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Hu's writing made Zhao Dun's fault clear.

sentences.zh: 是知執筆於朝，其來久矣。

translations.literal: From this one knows that wielding the brush at court has a long history.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that wielding the brush at court has a long history.

sentences.zh: 而漢、魏已還，密為記注，徒聞後世，無益當時。

translations.literal: Yet from Han and Wei onward records were kept in secret; later ages alone heard of them, with no benefit to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Han and Wei onward records were kept in secret; later ages alone heard of them, with no benefit to the present age.

sentences.zh: 非所謂將順其美，匡救其惡者。

translations.literal: This is not what is meant by aiding what is beautiful and correcting what is evil.
translations.idiomatic: This is not what is meant by supporting what is good and correcting what is evil.

sentences.zh: 且著述之人，密書縱能直筆，人莫知之。

translations.literal: Moreover, among those who compose histories, even if secret writings could employ an upright brush, no one would know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among those who write history, even if secret records could be written with an upright brush, no one would know of it.

sentences.zh: 何止物生橫議，亦自異端互起。

translations.literal: Not only would the public spawn reckless talk, but heretical views would also arise one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Not only would the public give rise to reckless talk, but conflicting heresies would also arise.

sentences.zh: 故班固致受金之名，陳壽有求米之論。

translations.literal: Thus Ban Gu incurred the name of accepting gold, and Chen Shou faced talk of begging for rice.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Ban Gu was accused of taking bribes, and Chen Shou was accused of begging for rice.

sentences.zh: 著漢、魏者非一氏，造晉史者至數家。

translations.literal: More than one clan wrote histories of Han and Wei; as many as several families compiled Jin histories.
translations.idiomatic: More than one family wrote histories of Han and Wei, and as many as several families compiled Jin histories.

sentences.zh: 後代紛紜，莫知准的。

translations.literal: Later generations were tangled in confusion, with no clear standard.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations were tangled in confusion, with no clear standard to follow.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下則天稽古，勞心庶政，開誹謗之路，納忠讜之言。

translations.literal: I bow and consider that Your Majesty models Heaven and examines antiquity, labors over the myriad affairs of government, opens the path for criticism, and accepts loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty takes Heaven as model and examines antiquity, labors over the myriad affairs of government, opens the path for criticism, and accepts loyal remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 諸史官記事者，請皆當朝顯言其狀，然後付之史閣。

translations.literal: I request that all historiographers who record affairs speak their accounts openly at court, and only then deliver them to the historiographical archive.
translations.idiomatic: I request that all historiographers who record affairs speak their accounts openly at court, and only then deliver them to the historiographical archive.

sentences.zh: 庶令是非明著，得失無陷，使聞善者日修，有過者知懼。」

translations.literal: Thus right and wrong would be clearly shown, gains and losses would not be concealed, those who heard of good would daily improve, and those with faults would know fear.
translations.idiomatic: Thus right and wrong would be made clear, gains and losses would not be hidden, those who heard of good would daily improve, and those with faults would know fear.

sentences.zh: 事遂施行。

translations.literal: The proposal was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was carried out.

sentences.zh: 十四年，除秘書丞，領著作。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Assistant Director of the Secretariat and concurrently head of composition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed assistant director of the secretariat and concurrently head of the historiographical office.

sentences.zh: 舊丞不參史事，自虯為丞，始令監掌焉。

translations.literal: Formerly the assistant director did not participate in historiographical affairs; from Qiu's tenure as assistant director, he was first ordered to supervise and manage them.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the assistant director did not take part in historiographical affairs; from Qiu's tenure as assistant director, he was first ordered to supervise them.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎，修起居注，仍領丞事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, compiled the Diaries of Activity and Repose, and still concurrently held the assistant director's duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the central secretariat, compiled the diaries of activity and repose, and still concurrently held the assistant director's duties.

sentences.zh: 時人論文體者，有今古之異。

translations.literal: People of the time who discussed literary style distinguished ancient from modern.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time who discussed literary style distinguished ancient from modern styles.

sentences.zh: 虯又以為時有古今，非文有古今，乃為文質論。

translations.literal: Qiu also held that times have ancient and modern, but writing does not have ancient and modern, and so he composed the Treatise on Literary Quality.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu also held that times have ancient and modern phases, but writing itself does not, and so he composed the Treatise on Literary Quality.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: Most of the text is not preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the treatise is not preserved.

sentences.zh: 廢帝初，遷秘書監，加車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and given the additional titles General of Chariots and Cavalry and Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the deposed emperor's reign he was transferred to director of the secretariat and given the additional titles general of chariots and cavalry and bearer of rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 虯脫略人間，不事小節，弊衣蔬食，未嘗改操。

translations.literal: Qiu was free and easy toward worldly matters, did not attend to minor points, wore worn clothes and ate plain food, and never altered his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was detached from worldly affairs, did not fuss over minor points, wore worn clothes and ate plain food, and never changed his ways.

sentences.zh: 人或譏之。

translations.literal: Some mocked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Some people mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 虯曰：「衣不過適體，食不過充饑，孜孜營求，徒勞思慮耳。」

translations.literal: Qiu said, "Clothing need only fit the body; food need only fill hunger. To strive constantly in pursuit is merely wasted thought.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu said, "Clothing need only fit the body; food need only fill hunger. To strive constantly after more is merely wasted thought.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年冬卒，時年五十四。

translations.literal: In winter of the first year of Emperor Gong he died, at age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the first year of Emperor Gong he died, at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈兗州刺史，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Governor of Yan Province; posthumous name Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Yan Province and given the posthumous name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 有文章數十篇，行於世。

translations.literal: He had several tens of essays in circulation in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of his essays circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 子鴻漸嗣。

translations.literal: His son Hongjian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongjian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 虯弟檜。

translations.literal: Qiu's younger brother Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's younger brother was Gui.

sentences.zh: 檜字季華。

translations.literal: Gui, styled Jihua.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, styled Jihua.

sentences.zh: 性剛簡，任氣少文，善騎射，果於斷決。

translations.literal: By nature he was firm and plain, relied on spirit and lacked polish, was skilled at horsemanship and archery, and was decisive in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was firm and plain-spoken, hot-tempered and unrefined, skilled at horsemanship and archery, and decisive in judgment.

sentences.zh: 年十八，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: At eighteen he first entered service as Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he first entered service as attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: During mourning for his father he wasted away until only bones remained upright.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he wasted away until he was skin and bones.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除陽城郡丞、防城都督。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Yangcheng commandery and Defense Commissioner of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed assistant administrator of Yangcheng commandery and defense commissioner of the city.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，從周文戰於河橋，先登有功。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong he followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in battle at Heqiao; by being first to ascend he earned merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong he followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in battle at Heqiao and earned merit by being first to scale the walls.

sentences.zh: 授都督，鎮鄯州。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander and garrisoned Shan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander and garrisoned Shan Province.

sentences.zh: 八年，拜湟河郡守，仍典軍事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Administrator of Huanghe commandery and still directed military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed administrator of Huanghe commandery and still directed military affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋加平東將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the East and grand master of palace counsel.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾入寇郡境，時檜兵少，人懷憂懼，檜撫而勉之，眾心乃安。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun invaded the commandery borders. At the time Gui had few troops and the people harbored worry and fear; Gui comforted and encouraged them, and the hearts of the masses then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun invaded the commandery borders. Gui had few troops at the time, and the people were anxious and afraid, but he comforted and encouraged them until their spirits settled.

sentences.zh: 因率數十人先擊之，渾人潰亂，餘眾乘之，遂大敗而走。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led several tens of men in a first strike. The Tuyuhun people fell into rout and chaos; the remaining forces took advantage, and thus they were utterly defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then led several dozen men in a first strike. The Tuyuhun broke and scattered, his remaining troops pressed the advantage, and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 以功封萬年縣子。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wannian county.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as viscount of Wannian county.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾強盛，數侵疆埸，自檜鎮鄯州，屢戰必破之。

translations.literal: At the time Tuyuhun was powerful and repeatedly invaded the frontier. From the time Gui garrisoned Shan Province, in battle after battle he invariably defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun was then at the height of its power and repeatedly raided the frontier. From the time Gui garrisoned Shan Province, he defeated them in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，不敢為寇。

translations.literal: After several years they did not dare make raids.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years they no longer dared raid.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷河州別駕，轉帥都督。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Vice-Governor of He Province and then became regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to vice-governor of He Province, then became regional commander.

sentences.zh: 俄拜使持節、撫軍將軍、大都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Commissioner Bearing the Staff, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed commissioner bearing the staff, general who pacifies the army, and grand commander.

sentences.zh: 居三載，征還京師。

translations.literal: After three years in office he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時檜兄虯為秘書丞，弟慶為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At the time Gui's elder brother Qiu was Secretary Director, and his younger brother Qing was Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gui's elder brother Qiu served as secretary director, and his younger brother Qing as left assistant director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 檜嘗謂兄弟曰：「兄則職典簡牘，褒貶人倫；

translations.literal: Gui once said to his brothers: "The elder brother's duty is to oversee the records and judge human conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Gui once told his brothers, "You, elder brother, oversee the archives and judge human conduct;

sentences.zh: 弟則管轄九司，股肱朝廷。

translations.literal: the younger brother's is to administer the nine ministries and serve as the arms and legs of the court.
translations.idiomatic: you, younger brother, administer the nine ministries and serve as the court's arms and legs.

sentences.zh: 可謂榮寵矣。

translations.literal: One may call this glory and favor indeed.
translations.idiomatic: That is honor enough.

sentences.zh: 然而四方未靜，車書不一，檜唯當蒙矢石，履危難，以報國恩耳。」

translations.literal: Yet the four quarters are not yet tranquil, and chariots and script are not unified. Gui alone must face flying arrows and stones and tread danger and hardship to repay the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: But the realm is still unsettled and not yet united under one rule. I alone must face arrows and stones, endure hardship, and repay the state's grace.

sentences.zh: 頃之，周文謂檜曰；

translations.literal: Before long, Emperor Wen of Zhou said to Gui:
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Emperor Wen of Zhou said to Gui:

sentences.zh: '卿昔在鄯州，忠勇顯著。

translations.literal: "In the past when you were in Shan Province, your loyalty and bravery were manifest.
translations.idiomatic: "When you were in Shan Province, your loyalty and bravery were outstanding.

sentences.zh: 今西境肅清，無勞經略。

translations.literal: Now the western frontier is pacified and cleared; there is no need for further strategic operations.
translations.idiomatic: The western frontier is now secure; there is no need for further campaigning.

sentences.zh: 九曲，國之東鄙，當勞君守之。」

translations.literal: Jiuqu is the state's eastern borderland; you must take on the labor of guarding it."
translations.idiomatic: Jiuqu is the eastern marches of the realm. I must ask you to hold it.

sentences.zh: 遂令檜鎮九曲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Gui to garrison Jiuqu.
translations.idiomatic: With that, he ordered Gui to garrison Jiuqu.

sentences.zh: 尋從大將軍王雄討上津、魏興，平之，即除魏興、華陽二郡守。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the Grand General Wang Xiong in campaigning against Shangjin and Weixing, pacified them, and was immediately appointed administrator of the two commanderies Weixing and Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he followed Grand General Wang Xiong in the campaign against Shangjin and Weixing. After they were pacified, he was immediately appointed administrator of Weixing and Huayang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 安康人黃眾寶謀反，連結黨與，將圍州城，乃相謂曰：「常聞柳府君勇悍有餘，不可當。

translations.literal: A man of Ankang, Huang Zhongbao, plotted rebellion, linked up with fellow conspirators, and was about to besiege the provincial capital. They said to one another: "We have often heard that Prefect Liu is excessively fierce and brave and cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhongbao of Ankang plotted rebellion, rallied allies, and was about to besiege the provincial capital. They said among themselves, "We have often heard that Prefect Liu is fiercely brave beyond measure and cannot be faced.

sentences.zh: 今既在外，方為吾徒腹心之疾也，不如先擊之。」

translations.literal: Now that he is outside, he is precisely the disease in the vitals of our faction; better to strike him first."
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is away, he is the thorn in our side. We had better strike him first.

sentences.zh: 遂圍檜郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon they besieged Gui's commandery.
translations.idiomatic: So they besieged Gui's commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡城卑下，士眾寡弱，又無守禦之備。

translations.literal: The commandery city was low and small, the soldiers and people few and weak, and there were no defenses prepared.
translations.idiomatic: The city was low and vulnerable, its garrison small and weak, and there were no proper defenses.

sentences.zh: 連戰積十餘日，士卒僅有存者。

translations.literal: Battle followed battle for more than ten days, and only a few soldiers survived.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days of fighting, only a handful of men remained.

sentences.zh: 於是力屈城陷，身被十餘創，遂為賊所獲。

translations.literal: Then their strength gave out, the city fell, he received more than ten wounds on his body, and was captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Their strength finally gave out and the city fell. Gui took more than ten wounds and was captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 既而眾寶等進圍東梁州，乃縛檜置城下，欲令誘城中。

translations.literal: Before long Zhongbao and the others advanced to besiege Eastern Liang Province. They bound Gui and placed him below the wall, intending to make him induce the city to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongbao and his followers then moved to besiege Eastern Liang Province. They bound Gui and placed him beneath the wall, hoping to make him persuade the city to submit.

sentences.zh: 檜乃大呼曰：「群賊烏合，糧食已罄，行即退散，各宜勉之！」

translations.literal: Gui then shouted loudly: "These rebels are a rabble in union; their grain is already exhausted and they will soon disperse and withdraw. Each of you should exert yourselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Gui shouted at the top of his voice, "These rebels are a disorderly mob. Their grain is gone, and they will soon break up and withdraw. Hold firm!

sentences.zh: 眾寶大怒，乃臨檜以兵曰：「速更汝辭！

translations.literal: Zhongbao was greatly enraged and confronted Gui with a weapon, saying: "Quickly change your words!
translations.idiomatic: Zhongbao flew into a rage, leveled a weapon at Gui, and said, "Change your words at once!

sentences.zh: 不爾便就戮矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise you will be executed on the spot."
translations.idiomatic: If not, you die here.

sentences.zh: 檜守節不變，遂害之，棄屍水中。

translations.literal: Gui held to his integrity without change, and they killed him and cast his corpse into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Gui would not yield. They killed him and threw his body into the river.

sentences.zh: 城中人皆為之流涕。

translations.literal: Everyone in the city wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the city wept for him.

sentences.zh: 眾寶解圍之後，檜兄子止戈方收檜屍還長安。

translations.literal: After Zhongbao lifted the siege, Gui's elder brother's son Zhige recovered Gui's corpse and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongbao lifted the siege, Gui's nephew Zhige recovered his body and brought it back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 贈東梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored as Inspector of Eastern Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as inspector of Eastern Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 子斌嗣。

translations.literal: His son Bin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 斌字伯達。

translations.literal: Bin, styled Boda.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, styled Boda.

sentences.zh: 年十七，齊公憲召為記室。

translations.literal: At seventeen the Duke of Qi, Xian, summoned him as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, Duke Xian of Qi summoned him as recorder.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 斌弟雄亮，字信誠。

translations.literal: Bin's younger brother Xiongliang, styled Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's younger brother Xiongliang, styled Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 父檜在華陽見害，雄亮時年十四，哀毀過禮，陰有復讎之志。

translations.literal: When his father Gui was killed at Huayang, Xiongliang was fourteen. His grief and wasting exceeded the rites, and secretly he harbored the ambition to avenge him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Gui was killed at Huayang, Xiongliang was fourteen. His mourning exceeded the prescribed rites, and secretly he resolved on revenge.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，眾寶率其部歸長安，帝待之甚厚。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wu's reign, Zhongbao led his followers to submit at Chang'an, and the emperor treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wu's reign, Zhongbao led his followers to Chang'an and submitted. The emperor treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 雄亮手斬眾寶於城中，請罪闕下。

translations.literal: Xiongliang personally beheaded Zhongbao in the city and pleaded for punishment at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongliang personally beheaded Zhongbao in the city, then went to the palace gates to plead for punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝特原之。

translations.literal: The emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 後累遷內史中大夫，賜爵汝陽縣子。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted in succession to Palace Secretary Grand Master and granted the title Viscount of Ruyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to palace secretary grand master and granted the title viscount of Ruyang county.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，拜尚書考功侍郎，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the abdication, he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel for Evaluating Merit, then transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the throne, he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Personnel for evaluating merit, then transferred to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 尚書省凡所奏事，多所駁正，深為公卿所憚。

translations.literal: Of all matters submitted in the Secretariat, he rejected and corrected many, and the high ministers deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Of all matters submitted through the Secretariat, he rejected and corrected many, and the high ministers deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官檢校太子左庶子，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: Soon with his existing office he was made Acting Left Vice-Crown Prince and advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, retaining his existing office, he was made acting left vice-crown prince and advanced in rank to marquis.

sentences.zh: 秦王俊鎮隴右，出為秦州總管府司馬，領山南道行台左丞。

translations.literal: When Prince Jun of Qin garrisoned Longyou, he was sent out as Military Administrator of the Qin Province General Headquarters, also serving as Left Assistant Director of the Southern Mountains Circuit Executive.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jun of Qin garrisoned Longyou, he was sent out as military administrator of the Qin Province general headquarters and also served as left assistant director of the Southern Mountains circuit executive.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子贊嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 檜弟鷟，好學善屬文，卒于魏臨淮王記室參軍事。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Zhuo loved study and was skilled at composition; he died as Recorder and Military Adviser to the Prince of Linhuai of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Zhuo loved learning and was skilled at literary composition. He died while serving as recorder and military adviser to the Prince of Linhuai of Wei.

sentences.zh: 子帶韋，字孝孫。

translations.literal: His son Daiwei, styled Xiaosun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daiwei, styled Xiaosun.

sentences.zh: 深沈有度量，少好學，身長八尺三寸，美風儀，善占對。

translations.literal: Deep and reserved with breadth of mind, from youth he loved learning. He stood eight feet three inches tall, had a fine bearing, and was skilled at extemporaneous replies.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and steady in temperament, from youth he loved learning. He stood eight feet three inches tall, had a fine bearing, and was skilled at impromptu replies.

sentences.zh: 周文辟為參軍事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou recruited him as military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou recruited him as military adviser.

sentences.zh: 侯景作亂江南，周文令帶韋使江、郢二州，與梁邵陵、南平二王通好。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled in the Jiangnan region, Emperor Wen of Zhou sent Daiwei as envoy to Jiang and Ying provinces to establish friendly relations with the two princes of Liang, Shaoling and Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled in the Jiangnan region, Emperor Wen of Zhou sent Daiwei as envoy to Jiang and Ying provinces to establish friendly relations with the Liang princes Shaoling and Nanping.

sentences.zh: 行至安州，遇段寶等反，帶韋乃矯為周文書以安之，並即降附。

translations.literal: When he reached An Province he encountered Duan Bao and others in rebellion. Daiwei then forged a letter from Emperor Wen of Zhou to pacify them, and they immediately submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached An Province he encountered Duan Bao and others in rebellion. Daiwei forged a letter from Emperor Wen of Zhou to pacify them, and they submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 及見邵陵，具申周文意。

translations.literal: When he met Shaoling he fully conveyed Emperor Wen of Zhou's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Shaoling, he fully conveyed Emperor Wen of Zhou's intentions.

sentences.zh: 邵陵遣使隨帶韋報命。

translations.literal: Shaoling dispatched an envoy to accompany Daiwei in reporting back.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoling sent an envoy to accompany Daiwei back with his report.

sentences.zh: 以奉使稱旨，授輔國將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: For fulfilling the mission to the emperor's satisfaction, he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Palace Attendant Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mission fulfilled the emperor's wishes, he was appointed general who assists the state and palace attendant grand master.

sentences.zh: 時譙王儉為益州總管，漢王贊為益州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Jian of Qiao was General Commander of Yi Province and Prince Zan of Han was Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Jian of Qiao was general commander of Yi Province, and Prince Zan of Han was inspector of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 武帝以帶韋為益州總管府長史，領益州別駕，輔弼二王，總知軍事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu appointed Daiwei as Chief Administrator of the Yi Province General Headquarters, also serving as Vice-Governor of Yi Province, to assist the two princes and oversee all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu appointed Daiwei chief administrator of the Yi Province general headquarters and vice-governor of Yi Province, to assist the two princes and oversee all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 及大軍東討，徵為前軍總管齊王憲府長史。

translations.literal: When the great army marched east to campaign, he was summoned as Chief Administrator on the staff of Prince Xian of Qi, Grand Commander of the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army marched east on campaign, he was summoned as chief administrator on the staff of Prince Xian of Qi, grand commander of the forward army.

sentences.zh: 齊平，以功授上開府儀同大將軍，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Qi was pacified, for his merit he was granted Senior Commandant with the Honors Equal to an Independently Established Office and made a duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was pacified, he was granted senior commandant with honors equal to an independently established office and advanced to duke for his merit.

sentences.zh: 陳王純鎮并州，以帶韋為并州司會、并州總管府長史。

translations.literal: When Prince Chun of Chen garrisoned Bing Province, Daiwei was made Bing Province Controller and Chief Administrator of the Bing Province General Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chun of Chen garrisoned Bing Province, Daiwei was made Bing Province controller and chief administrator of the Bing Province general headquarters.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰愷。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumous name Kai.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was given the posthumous name Kai.

sentences.zh: 子祚嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zuo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 少有名譽，位宣納上士。

translations.literal: From youth he had reputation; he reached the rank of Attendant Who Proclaims Affairs, Senior Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed a fine reputation from youth and rose to the rank of attendant who proclaims affairs, senior clerk.

sentences.zh: 入隋，位司勳侍郎。

translations.literal: Entering Sui he held the post of Vice Director of the Ministry of Honors.
translations.idiomatic: After the Sui dynasty was founded, he served as vice director of the Ministry of Honors.

sentences.zh: 鷟弟慶。

translations.literal: Zhuo's younger brother Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's younger brother was Qing.

sentences.zh: 慶字更興。

translations.literal: Qing, styled Gengxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qing, styled Gengxing.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏有器量，博涉群書，不為章句，好飲酒，閑於占對。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever and perceptive with breadth of capacity. He read widely in many books without practicing textual glossing, was fond of drink, and was adept at impromptu conversation.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was clever and broad-minded. He read widely without fussing over textual glosses, loved wine, and was adept at impromptu conversation.

sentences.zh: 年十三，因暴書，父僧習試令慶于雜賦集中取賦一篇千餘言，誦之。

translations.literal: At thirteen, during the airing of books, his father Sengxi tested Qing by having him take from a miscellaneous fu collection one fu of over a thousand words and recite it.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, while books were being aired in the sun, his father Sengxi tested him by having Qing take from a miscellaneous collection of fu one piece of more than a thousand words and recite it.

sentences.zh: 慶立讀三遍，便誦之無所漏。

translations.literal: Qing read it on the spot three times and then recited it without omitting anything.
translations.idiomatic: Qing read it through three times on the spot and recited it without missing a word.

sentences.zh: 時僧習為潁川郡守，地接都畿，人多豪右。

translations.literal: At the time Sengxi was Administrator of Yingchuan commandery. The land bordered the capital region and many people were powerful magnates.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sengxi was administrator of Yingchuan commandery. The region bordered the capital, and many powerful local magnates lived there.

sentences.zh: 將選鄉官，皆依貴勢，競來請托。

translations.literal: When about to select local officials, all relied on noble power and competed in seeking entreaties.
translations.idiomatic: When local officials were to be selected, the powerful families all leaned on their influence and pressed their requests.

sentences.zh: 選用既定，僧習謂諸子曰：「權貴請托，吾並不用。

translations.literal: When the selections were settled, Sengxi said to his sons: "The nobles' entreaties I have not used at all.
translations.idiomatic: Once the selections were settled, Sengxi told his sons, "I have refused every request from the powerful.

sentences.zh: 其使欲還，皆須有答。

translations.literal: Those whose envoys wish to return must all be given a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Their messengers will still need answers on their way home.

sentences.zh: 汝各以意為吾作書。」

translations.literal: Each of you write letters for me as you see fit."
translations.idiomatic: Each of you write replies for me as you think best.

sentences.zh: 慶乃具書草。

translations.literal: Qing then drafted all the letters.
translations.idiomatic: Qing drafted all the letters.

sentences.zh: 僧習讀，歎曰：「此兒有意氣，丈夫理當如是。」

translations.literal: Sengxi read them and sighed: "This boy has spirit; a man ought to be like this."
translations.idiomatic: Sengxi read them and sighed, "This boy has backbone. That is how a man ought to be.

sentences.zh: 即依慶所草以報。

translations.literal: He then replied according to Qing's drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He sent replies based on Qing's drafts.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: He first entered service as Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 慶出後第四叔，及遭父憂，議者不許為服重。

translations.literal: Qing had been adopted as heir to his fourth uncle. When he suffered mourning for his father, discussants did not permit him to wear heavy mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Qing had been made heir to his fourth uncle. When his father died, critics argued that he should not wear the full mourning garb.

sentences.zh: 慶泣曰：「禮緣人情，若於出後之家，更有苴斬之服，可奪此以從彼。

translations.literal: Qing wept and said: "Rites arise from human feeling. If in a household into which one has been adopted as heir there is additionally the sackcloth-and-staff mourning, one may set this aside to follow that.
translations.idiomatic: Qing wept and said, "Rites grow out of human feeling. If one were still bound by mourning for the adoptive house, one might set this grief aside for that obligation.

sentences.zh: 今四叔薨背已久，情事不追。

translations.literal: Now the fourth uncle died long ago, and that bond can no longer be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: But my fourth uncle has been dead for years; that tie cannot be revived.

sentences.zh: 豈容奪禮，乖違天性！」

translations.literal: How can one cast off the rites and violate one's natural feelings!"
translations.idiomatic: How can I cast off the rites and betray my own nature!

sentences.zh: 時論不能抑，遂以苫塊終喪。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion could not restrain him, and he therefore observed the full mourning on a straw mat until the end.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion could not sway him, and he observed the full mourning on a straw mat to the end.

sentences.zh: 既葬，乃與諸兄負土成墳。

translations.literal: After the burial he joined his elder brothers in carrying earth to complete the mound.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he joined his elder brothers in carrying earth to build the tomb mound.

sentences.zh: 孝武將西遷，慶以散騎侍郎馳傳入關。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was about to move west, Qing as Palace Attendant Cavalier entered the pass by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu was about to move west, Qing entered the pass by express relay in his capacity as palace attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 慶至高平，見周文，共論時事。

translations.literal: Qing reached Gaoping and met Emperor Wen of Zhou; together they discussed current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Qing reached Gaoping, met Emperor Wen of Zhou, and discussed current affairs with him.

sentences.zh: 周文即請奉迎輿駕，仍令慶先還復命。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou immediately asked to escort the imperial carriage and still ordered Qing to return first with his report.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou at once asked to escort the imperial carriage and sent Qing back ahead to report.

sentences.zh: 時賀拔勝在荊州，帝屏左右謂慶曰：「朕欲往荊州，何如？」

translations.literal: At the time Heluo Sheng was in Jing Province. The emperor dismissed those around him and said to Qing: "I wish to go to Jing Province; what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Heluo Sheng was then in Jing Province. The emperor dismissed his attendants and asked Qing, "I am thinking of going to Jing Province. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 慶曰：「關中金城千里，天下之強國也。

translations.literal: Qing said: "Within the passes the land is a thousand li of golden ramparts, the strongest realm under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Qing said, "The Guanzhong region is a thousand-li fortress, the strongest realm under heaven.

sentences.zh: 荊州地無要害，寧足以固鴻基？」

translations.literal: Jing Province has no strategic strongpoints; can it truly secure the great foundation?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province has no strategic strongpoints. Can it truly secure the imperial foundation?

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 及帝西遷，慶以母老不從。

translations.literal: When the emperor moved west, Qing did not follow because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved west, Qing did not follow because his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信之鎮洛陽，乃得入關。

translations.literal: When Dugu Xin garrisoned Luoyang he was then able to enter the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Dugu Xin garrisoned Luoyang was he able to enter the pass.

sentences.zh: 除相府東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Eastern Pavilion Libationer in the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed eastern pavilion libationer in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 大統十年，除尚書都兵郎中，並領記室。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Datong he was appointed Lang of the Ministry of Personnel's Military Section, also concurrently serving as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Datong he was appointed lang of the Ministry of Personnel's military section, also serving concurrently as recorder.

sentences.zh: 時北雍州獻白鹿，群臣欲賀。

translations.literal: At the time Northern Yong Province presented a white deer, and the ministers wished to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Northern Yong Province presented a white deer, and the ministers wished to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 尚書蘇綽謂慶曰：「近代已來，文章華靡，逮于江左，彌復輕薄。

translations.literal: Minister Su Chuo said to Qing: "In recent times, writings have become ornate and extravagant; reaching the lands south of the Yangzi, they have become all the more frivolous and shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Su Chuo said to Qing, "In recent times literary style has grown ornate and extravagant, and south of the Yangzi it has become even more frivolous and shallow.

sentences.zh: 洛陽後進，祖述未已。

translations.literal: The younger generation in Luoyang still emulates and imitates without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Young writers in Luoyang still follow and imitate that fashion without letup.

sentences.zh: 相公柄人軌物，君職典文房，宜制此表，以革前弊。」

translations.literal: The Chancellor holds authority over men and sets standards for things; your post is to preside over the literary office. You should draft this memorial to reform the earlier abuses."
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor holds authority over men and sets standards for affairs, and your office is in charge of the literary bureau—you should draft this memorial to reform these abuses.

sentences.zh: 慶操筆立成，辭兼文質。

translations.literal: Qing took up the brush and completed it on the spot; the language combined literary elegance with solid substance.
translations.idiomatic: Qing took up his brush and finished it on the spot, his language combining grace with substance.

sentences.zh: 綽讀而笑曰：「枳橘猶自可移，況才子也！」

translations.literal: Chuo read it and laughed, saying: "Trifoliate orange and bitter orange can still change when transplanted—how much more so a talented man!"
translations.idiomatic: Chuo read it and laughed, saying, "If trifoliate orange and bitter orange can change when transplanted, how much more so can a talented man!"

sentences.zh: 尋以本官領雍州別駕。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, while retaining his original post, he was placed in charge as Adjunct Administrator of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Adjunct Administrator of Yong Province while retaining his original rank.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王欣，魏之懿親。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangling, Xin, was a close imperial relative of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangling Xin was a close kinsman of the Wei imperial house.

sentences.zh: 其甥孟氏，屢為凶橫。

translations.literal: His nephew, the Meng clan, repeatedly committed violent and overbearing acts.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew of the Meng clan repeatedly committed acts of violence and bullying.

sentences.zh: 或有告其盜牛。

translations.literal: Someone reported that he had stolen cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that he had stolen cattle.

sentences.zh: 慶捕得實，趣令就禁。

translations.literal: Qing arrested him and verified the facts, then hurried to have him placed under detention.
translations.idiomatic: Qing arrested him, verified the charge, and had him taken into custody at once.

sentences.zh: 孟氏殊無懼容，乃謂慶曰：「若加以桎梏，後獨何以脫之？」

translations.literal: Meng showed not the slightest fear, and said to Qing: "If shackles are put on me, how will you alone release me afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: Meng showed no fear at all and said to Qing, "If you put me in shackles, how will you get me out afterward?

sentences.zh: 欣亦遣使辨其無罪。

translations.literal: Xin also sent a messenger to argue that he was guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: Xin also sent a messenger to plead that he was innocent.

sentences.zh: 孟氏由此益驕。

translations.literal: From this the Meng clan became all the more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: After this the Meng clan grew even more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 慶乃大集僚吏，盛言孟氏倚權侵虐之狀。

translations.literal: Qing then summoned all the officials in great assembly and spoke at length of how the Meng clan relied on power to oppress and abuse others.
translations.idiomatic: Qing then assembled all his subordinates and spoke at length about how the Meng clan relied on power to bully and abuse others.

sentences.zh: 言畢，令笞殺之。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, he ordered that Meng be beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking, he ordered Meng flogged to death.

sentences.zh: 此後貴戚斂手。

translations.literal: After this the noble clans restrained their hands.
translations.idiomatic: After that the powerful families held themselves in check.

sentences.zh: 有賈人持金二十斤詣京師，寄人居止。

translations.literal: There was a merchant who, carrying twenty jin of gold, went to the capital and lodged with a host.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant carrying twenty jin of gold came to the capital and stayed as a guest in someone's home.

sentences.zh: 每欲出行，常自執管鑰。

translations.literal: Whenever he wished to go out, he always kept the keys in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went out he always kept the keys on him.

sentences.zh: 無何，緘閉不異而並失之。

translations.literal: Before long, though the seals and locks were unchanged, all of it was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, though locks and seals seemed undisturbed, the gold was gone.

sentences.zh: 謂主人所竊。

translations.literal: He asserted that the host had stolen it.
translations.idiomatic: He accused his host of stealing it.

sentences.zh: 郡縣訊問，主人自誣服。

translations.literal: The district and county interrogated the case, and the host falsely confessed under coercion.
translations.idiomatic: When the district and county interrogated the case, the host falsely confessed under duress.

sentences.zh: 慶疑之，乃召問賈人曰：「卿鑰恆置何處？」

translations.literal: Qing had doubts and summoned the merchant to question him, saying: "Where do you always keep the keys?"
translations.idiomatic: Qing was suspicious and summoned the merchant, asking, "Where do you usually keep the keys?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「恆自帶之。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I always carry them on my person."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I always carry them with me.

sentences.zh: 慶曰：「頗與人同宿乎？」

translations.literal: Qing said: "Do you ever lodge with others?"
translations.idiomatic: Qing asked, "Do you ever share lodging with anyone?

translations.literal: He said: "No."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "No."

sentences.zh: 「與同飲乎？」

translations.literal: Do you drink together with others?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you ever drink with anyone?

sentences.zh: 曰：「日者曾與一沙門再度酣宴，醉而晝寢。」

translations.literal: He said: "The other day I once shared two rounds of merry drinking with a Buddhist monk and, drunk, slept through the day."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The other day I drank twice with a monk till we were thoroughly merry; I got drunk and slept through the day.

sentences.zh: 慶曰：「沙門乃真盜耳。」

translations.literal: Qing said: "The monk is the real thief."
translations.idiomatic: Qing said, "The monk is the real thief.

sentences.zh: 即遣捕沙門，乃懷金逃匿。

translations.literal: He immediately sent men to arrest the monk, who was carrying the gold and had fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent men to arrest the monk, who was hiding with the gold.

sentences.zh: 後捕得，盡獲所失金。

translations.literal: Later he was captured, and all the lost gold was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The monk was later captured and all the missing gold was recovered.

sentences.zh: 十二年，改三十六曹為十二部，以慶為計部郎中，別駕如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the thirty-six bureaus were reorganized into twelve departments; Qing was appointed Lang of the Accounting Department, his post as Adjunct Administrator remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the thirty-six bureaus were reorganized into twelve departments; Qing was made lang of the Accounting Department while retaining his post as adjunct administrator.

sentences.zh: 又有胡家被劫，郡縣按察，莫知賊所，鄰近被囚者甚多。

translations.literal: Again there was a Hu family's house that was robbed; the district and county investigated but could not learn where the thieves were; many neighbors were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Another case involved a Hu household that was robbed; district and county investigators could not find the thieves, and many neighbors were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 慶以賊是烏合，可以詐求之。

translations.literal: Qing reasoned that the thieves were a loose mob and could be sought by deception.
translations.idiomatic: Qing judged that the thieves were a loosely banded mob and could be flushed out by a ruse.

sentences.zh: 乃作匿名書，多榜官門曰：「我等共劫胡家，徒侶混雜，終恐洩露。

translations.literal: He then wrote anonymous letters and posted many at the government gate, saying: "We jointly robbed the Hu household; our companions are mixed together, and we ultimately fear exposure.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote anonymous notices and posted many at the government gate: "We jointly robbed the Hu household; our group is mixed and disorganized, and we fear we will be exposed.

sentences.zh: 今欲首伏，懼不免誅。

translations.literal: Now we wish to surrender ourselves, but fear we cannot escape execution.
translations.idiomatic: We now wish to surrender, but fear we cannot escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 若聽先首免罪，便欲來告。」

translations.literal: If the first to surrender is allowed to escape punishment, we wish to come forward and report."
translations.idiomatic: If whoever turns himself in first is granted amnesty, we will come forward.

sentences.zh: 慶乃復施免罪之牒。

translations.literal: Qing then posted another proclamation offering amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Qing then posted another amnesty proclamation.

sentences.zh: 居二日，廣陵王欣家奴面縛自告牒下，因此盡獲黨與。

translations.literal: After two days, a household slave of Prince of Guangling Xin came forward with hands bound to surrender himself under the proclamation; through this the whole gang was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later a household slave of Prince Guangling Xin came forward, hands bound, to surrender under the proclamation; the whole gang was thus captured.

sentences.zh: 慶之守正明察，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Qing's upholding of integrity and clear discernment were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's integrity and sharp discernment were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 每歎曰：「或於公斷獄無私，辟高門以待封。

translations.literal: He often sighed and said: "They say Yu Gong judged cases without partiality, and a great gate was opened awaiting enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He often sighed, "They say that when Yu Gong judged without favor, his family was rewarded with high rank.

sentences.zh: 儻斯言有驗，吾其庶幾乎。」

translations.literal: If those words should prove true, perhaps I might come close to it."
translations.idiomatic: If that saying should prove true, perhaps I might come close to it.

sentences.zh: 封清河縣男，除尚書左丞，攝計部。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Qinghe County, appointed Left Assistant Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and acted as head of the Accounting Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Qinghe County, appointed left assistant director of the Ministry of Personnel, and put in charge of the Accounting Department.

sentences.zh: 周文嘗怒安定國臣王茂，將殺之，而非其罪。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen once grew angry at Wang Mao, a minister of Anding State, and was about to kill him, though he was not guilty of the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen once grew angry at Wang Mao, a minister of Anding domain, and was about to execute him though he was innocent.

sentences.zh: 朝臣咸知，而莫敢諫。

translations.literal: All the court ministers knew, yet none dared remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: The court ministers all knew, yet none dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 慶乃進爭之。

translations.literal: Qing then stepped forward to dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: Qing stepped forward to argue against it.

sentences.zh: 周文逾怒曰：「卿若明其無罪，亦須坐之。」

translations.literal: Zhou Wen grew even angrier and said: "If you make clear that he is guiltless, you too must be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen grew even angrier and said, "If you insist he is innocent, you will share his punishment.

sentences.zh: 乃執慶於前。

translations.literal: He then seized Qing before him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Qing seized and brought before him.

sentences.zh: 慶辭氣不撓，抗聲曰：「竊聞君有不達者為不明。

translations.literal: Qing's tone and bearing did not bend; raising his voice he said: "I have heard that a lord who does not penetrate matters is called unenlightened.
translations.idiomatic: Qing did not flinch; raising his voice he said, "I have heard that a ruler who fails to see clearly is unenlightened.

sentences.zh: 臣有不爭者為不忠。

translations.literal: A minister who does not contend is called disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: A minister who does not speak up is disloyal.

sentences.zh: 慶謹竭愚誠，實不敢愛死，但懼公為不明之君耳。」

translations.literal: Qing earnestly exerted his foolish sincerity, truly not daring to cherish his life, but only fearing that Your Lordship would be an unenlightened ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Qing spoke with all the sincerity he could muster; he did not hold back his life, but feared only that his lord would prove an unenlightened ruler.

sentences.zh: 周文乃悟而赦茂，已不及矣。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen then understood and pardoned Mao, but it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen then understood and pardoned Mao—but it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 周文默然。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen fell silent.

sentences.zh: 明日，謂慶曰：「吾不用卿言，遂令王茂冤死。

translations.literal: The next day he said to Qing: "I did not heed your words and thus caused Wang Mao to die wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he said to Qing, "I did not heed your advice, and Wang Mao died unjustly.

sentences.zh: 可賜茂家錢帛，以旌吾過。」

translations.literal: You may bestow money and silk on Mao's family to mark my fault."
translations.idiomatic: Bestow money and silk on Mao's family to mark my fault.

sentences.zh: 尋進爵為子。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward his rank was raised to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his noble rank was raised to viscount.

sentences.zh: 慶威儀端肅，樞機明辯。

translations.literal: Qing's bearing was dignified and solemn; in crucial matters he was clear and discerning.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was dignified in bearing and clear and decisive in critical affairs.

sentences.zh: 周文每發號令，常使慶宣之。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhou Wen issued orders, he always had Qing proclaim them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhou Wen issued orders, he had Qing proclaim them.

sentences.zh: 天性抗直，無所回避。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and frank, yielding to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and blunt, never yielding.

sentences.zh: 周文亦以此深委仗焉。

translations.literal: Zhou Wen also for this reason deeply entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Wen for this reason deeply relied on him.

sentences.zh: 恭帝初，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射，轉左僕射，領著作。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reign of Emperor Gong, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon with the privileges of the Three Excellencies, Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then transferred to Left Vice Director, and placed in charge of the Bureau of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Gong's reign he was promoted to general of agile cavalry, granted the privileges of an independent command equal to the Three Excellencies, made right vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, then left vice director, and put in charge of the compilation bureau.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜司會中大夫。

translations.literal: When the six offices were established, he was appointed Grand Master of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When the six offices were established, he was appointed grand master of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐祚，賜姓宇文氏，進爵平齊縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, he was granted the surname Yuwen and raised in rank to Duke of Pingqi County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou took the throne, Qing was granted the surname Yuwen and raised to duke of Pingqi county.

sentences.zh: 晉公護初執政，欲引為腹心。

translations.literal: When Duke of Jin Hu first took power, he wished to draw Qing into his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu first took power, he wished to make Qing his trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 慶辭之，頗忤旨。

translations.literal: Qing declined, somewhat going against the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Qing declined, which displeased him considerably.

sentences.zh: 又與楊寬有隙，及寬參知政事，慶遂見疏忌，出為萬州刺史。

translations.literal: He also had a rift with Yang Kuan, and when Kuan took part in managing state affairs, Qing came to be distanced and distrusted, and was sent out as Governor of Wan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He also had a feud with Yang Kuan; when Kuan joined in governing, Qing fell under suspicion and was sent out as governor of Wan province.

sentences.zh: 明帝尋悟，留為雍州別駕，領京兆尹。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming soon understood, kept him as Adjunct Administrator of Yong Province, and placed him in charge as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming soon saw his worth, kept him as adjunct administrator of Yong province, and made him metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，除宜州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng he was appointed Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wucheng he was appointed governor of Yi province.

sentences.zh: 慶自為郎，迄為司會，府庫倉儲，並其職也。

translations.literal: From the time Qing served as Lang until he became Treasurer, treasuries, storehouses, and granaries were all within his duties.
translations.idiomatic: From his time as a bureau lang until he became treasurer, treasuries, storehouses, and granaries had all been within his responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 及在宜州，寬為小塚宰，乃囚慶故吏，求其罪失。

translations.literal: When he was in Yi Province, Kuan served as junior steward and then imprisoned Qing's former clerks to seek out his faults and failures.
translations.idiomatic: While Qing was in Yi province, Yang Kuan served as junior steward and imprisoned Qing's former clerks, searching for evidence of wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 案驗積六十餘日，吏或有死於獄者，終無所言，唯得乘錦數匹。

translations.literal: The investigation lasted more than sixty days; some clerks died in prison, yet in the end none spoke out—only several bolts of brocade given as gifts were found.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation lasted more than sixty days; some clerks died in prison, yet none incriminated him—the only evidence was a few bolts of brocade he had accepted as gifts.

sentences.zh: 時人服其廉慎。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his integrity and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time admired his integrity and discretion.

sentences.zh: 又入為司會。

translations.literal: He again entered the capital to serve as Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed treasurer.

sentences.zh: 先是，慶兄檜為魏興郡守，為賊黃眾寶所害。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qing's elder brother Gui had been Administrator of Weixing Commandery and was killed by the bandit Huang Zhongbao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qing's elder brother Gui, administrator of Weixing commandery, had been killed by the bandit Huang Zhongbao.

sentences.zh: 檜子三人皆幼弱，慶撫養甚篤。

translations.literal: Gui's three sons were all young and weak; Qing raised and nurtured them with great devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's three sons were still very young; Qing raised them with devoted care.

sentences.zh: 後眾寶歸朝，朝廷待以優禮。

translations.literal: Later Zhongbao submitted to the court, and the court treated him with honored courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhongbao submitted to the court and was treated with special courtesy.

sentences.zh: 居數年，檜次子雄亮白日手刃眾寶于長安城中。

translations.literal: After several years, Gui's second son Xiongliang by daylight personally slew Zhongbao with a blade in the city of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Gui's second son Xiongliang openly killed Zhongbao with his own hand in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 晉公護聞而大怒，執慶諸子侄皆囚之，讓慶擅殺人。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu heard and was greatly enraged; he seized Qing's sons and nephews and imprisoned them all, reproaching Qing for unauthorized killing.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu was furious; he had Qing's sons and nephews seized and imprisoned, and rebuked Qing for unauthorized killing.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「慶聞父母之讎不同天，昆弟之讎不同國。

translations.literal: He replied: "Qing has heard that the enemy of one's parents cannot live under the same sky, and the enemy of one's brothers cannot live in the same state.
translations.idiomatic: Qing replied, "I have heard that one's parents' enemy cannot live under the same sky, and one's brother's enemy cannot live in the same state.

sentences.zh: 明公以孝臨天下，何乃責於此乎？」

translations.literal: Your Lordship rules the realm with filial piety—why reproach me on this account?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Lordship rules all under heaven through filial piety—why reproach me for this?

sentences.zh: 護逾怒，慶辭色無屈，竟以俱免。

translations.literal: Hu grew still angrier, but Qing's words and expression did not bend; in the end both were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Hu grew angrier still, but Qing did not flinch; in the end all were released.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 贈鄜、綏、丹三州刺史，諡曰景。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the three offices of Governor of Fu, Sui, and Dan Provinces, and his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the rank of governor over Fu, Sui, and Dan provinces, and given the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 子機嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ji succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 機字匡時。

translations.literal: Ji's style was Kuangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's courtesy name was Kuangshi.

sentences.zh: 偉容儀，有器局，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: He had a handsome appearance, possessed breadth of capacity, and was fairly well versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He had a handsome bearing, breadth of character, and considerable learning in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 年十九，周武帝時為魯公，引為記室。

translations.literal: At nineteen, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was Duke of Lu, Ji was invited to serve as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen, when the future Emperor Wu of Zhou was still Duke of Lu, he was made Ji's recorder.

sentences.zh: 及帝嗣位，累遷太子宮尹，封平齊縣公。

translations.literal: When the Emperor succeeded to the throne, Ji was repeatedly promoted to Palace Administrator of the Crown Prince and enfeoffed as Duke of Pingqi County.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor succeeded to the throne, Ji rose through successive posts to palace administrator of the crown prince and was enfeoffed as duke of Pingqi county.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，為禦正上大夫。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuan he served as Superior Grand Master of the Imperial Correctives.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he served as superior grand master of the imperial correctives.

sentences.zh: 機見帝失德，屢諫不聽，恐禍及己，托于鄭譯，求出，拜華州刺史。

translations.literal: Ji saw that the Emperor was losing virtue; he repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded; fearing disaster would reach him, he relied on Zheng Yi to seek an outside post and was appointed Governor of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor's misconduct, Ji remonstrated again and again without being heard; fearing he would be implicated, he turned to Zheng Yi, sought a provincial post, and was appointed governor of Hua province.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝作相，征還京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as Chancellor, Ji was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui became chancellor, Ji was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時周代舊臣皆勸禪讓，機獨義形於色，無所陳請。

translations.literal: At the time the old ministers of Zhou all urged abdication in his favor; Ji alone showed righteous indignation in his expression and made no petition.
translations.idiomatic: Old ministers of the Zhou all urged abdication in Yang Jian's favor; Ji alone showed open disapproval and made no petition.

sentences.zh: 俄拜衛州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Governor of Wei Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Wei province.

sentences.zh: 及踐祚，進爵建安郡公，徵為納言。

translations.literal: When Yang Jian took the throne, Ji's rank was raised to Duke of Jian'an Commandery and he was summoned to serve as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian took the throne, Ji was raised to duke of Jian'an commandery and recalled as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 機性寬簡，有雅望，當近侍，無所損益。

translations.literal: Ji was by nature easygoing and unassuming, held refined prestige, and in attendance at close quarters neither harmed nor benefited matters.
translations.idiomatic: Easygoing and unassuming, Ji enjoyed a fine reputation; as a close attendant he neither helped nor hindered affairs much.

sentences.zh: 又好飲酒，不親細務。

translations.literal: He also loved drinking wine and did not personally attend to minor matters.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved wine and did not bother with minor details.

sentences.zh: 數年，出為華州刺史，奉詔每月朝見。

translations.literal: After several years he was sent out as Governor of Hua Province, ordered by imperial edict to attend court each month.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was sent out as governor of Hua province, with orders to attend court monthly.

sentences.zh: 尋轉冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 後征入朝，以其子述尚蘭陵公主，禮遇益隆。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to court; because his son Shu had married Princess of Lanling, his honors and treatment grew all the more lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled to court; because his son Shu had married Princess Lanling, his honors grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 初，機在周，與族人文城公昂俱曆顯要，及此，昂、機並為外職。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ji was in Zhou, he and his clansman Duke of Wencheng, Ang, had both held prominent posts; by this time Ang and Ji were both in outside appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Zhou, Ji and his kinsman Duke Wencheng Ang had both held high office; by now both were serving outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 楊素時為納言，方用事，因上賜宴，素戲曰：「二柳俱摧，孤楊獨聳。」

translations.literal: Yang Su then served as Censor-in-Chief and was just then wielding power; at an imperial banquet Yang Su jested, saying: "Both willows are broken down, while the lone poplar stands tall alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, then censor-in-chief and very much in power, joked at an imperial banquet: "Both willows have fallen, while the lone poplar stands tall.

sentences.zh: 坐者歡笑，機竟無言。

translations.literal: Those seated laughed with delight; Ji in the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Those present burst out laughing; Ji said nothing in reply.

sentences.zh: 未幾還州。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to his province.

sentences.zh: 前後作守，俱稱寬惠。

translations.literal: In his earlier and later terms as prefect, all praised his leniency and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In successive terms as regional governor, he was praised alike for his leniency and kindness.

sentences.zh: 後以征還，卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled on imperial summons and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled to court and died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、青州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand General and Governor of Qing Province; posthumous title Jian (Simple).
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously named grand general and governor of Qing province, with the posthumous title Jian ("Simple").

sentences.zh: 子述嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 述字業隆。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Yelong.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, whose courtesy name was Yelong.

sentences.zh: 性明敏，有幹略，頗涉文藝。

translations.literal: By nature bright and quick, he had capacity and strategy, and dabbled considerably in literature and the arts.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and quick by nature, he had talent for leadership and was well versed in literature and the arts.

sentences.zh: 以父廕為太子親衛。

translations.literal: Through his father's inherited privilege he became a close guard of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's hereditary privilege he was made a close guard of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 後以尚主故，拜開府儀同三司、內史侍郎。

translations.literal: Later, because he had married an imperial princess, he was appointed Grand Master with Honor Equal to the Three Excellencies with an office of separate establishment, and Vice Minister of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, having married an imperial princess, he was made grand master with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies and vice minister of the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上于諸婿中特見寵遇。

translations.literal: The emperor among all his sons-in-law singled him out for favor and distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Among the emperor's sons-in-law he was singled out for special favor.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，判兵部尚書事。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was put in charge of the affairs of the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After a year or so, he was put in charge of war ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 父艱去職。

translations.literal: Upon his father's bereavement he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起攝給事黃門侍郎事，襲爵建安郡公。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to serve concurrently as Attendant Gentleman, Vice Minister in the Yellow Gate, and inherited the title Duke of Jian'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to serve concurrently as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and inherited the title duke of Jian'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，判吏部尚書事。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era he was put in charge of the affairs of the Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou reign era he was put in charge of personnel ministry affairs.

sentences.zh: 述雖職務修理，為當時所稱，然不達大體，暴於馭下，又怙寵驕豪，無所降屈。

translations.literal: Although Shu was thorough in his duties and praised by the age, he did not grasp the larger picture, was harsh toward those under him, and moreover, relying on favor, was arrogant and overbearing and would bow to no one.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shu ran his affairs efficiently and won praise at the time, he failed to see the larger picture, was harsh toward subordinates, and, secure in imperial favor, grew arrogant and bowed to no one.

sentences.zh: 楊素時方貴重，朝臣莫不讋憚，述每陵侮之，數於上前面折素短。

translations.literal: Yang Su was then at the height of power and prestige; no court minister did not fear and respect him. Shu regularly treated him with contempt and defiance, and several times before the emperor openly exposed Su's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su then held great power and prestige, and no courtier dared cross him—yet Shu habitually slighted and insulted him, openly exposing Su's faults before the emperor on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 判事有不合，素意或令述改，輒謂將命者曰：「語僕射，道尚書不肯。」

translations.literal: When a ruling did not accord with his wishes, Su would sometimes have Shu change it; Shu would then say to the bearer of the order: "Tell the Vice Minister: say that the Minister refuses.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruling did not suit Su, Su would sometimes order Shu to change it; Shu would tell the messenger: "Tell the vice minister that the minister refuses.

sentences.zh: 素由是銜之。

translations.literal: Su because of this bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Su therefore came to bear a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 俄而楊素被疏忌，不知省事。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Su came to be distanced and suspected, and was relieved of routine duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Su fell out of favor and was relieved of his routine duties.

sentences.zh: 述任寄逾重，拜兵部尚書，參掌機密。

translations.literal: Shu's trust and commission grew ever heavier; he was appointed Minister of War and took part in managing confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's responsibilities grew heavier still; he was appointed minister of war and took part in confidential state business.

sentences.zh: 述自以無功可紀，過叨匪服，抗表陳讓。

translations.literal: Shu himself felt he had no achievements worth recording and had received an unmerited appointment beyond his station, so he submitted a memorial declining.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling he had no achievements to his credit and had received an unmerited appointment, Shu submitted a memorial declining the post.

sentences.zh: 上許之，命攝兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor assented and ordered him to serve concurrently as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and had him serve concurrently as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 上于仁壽宮寢疾，述與楊素、黃門侍郎元岩等侍疾宮中。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, Shu together with Yang Su, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Yuan Yan, and others attended him in the palace during his illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill at Renshou Palace, Shu joined Yang Su, Yuan Yan of the yellow gate, and others in attending him in the palace.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子無禮于陳貴人，上知之，大怒，令述召房陵王。

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince had been disrespectful toward Lady Chen; the emperor learned of it, flew into a rage, and ordered Shu to summon the Prince of Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had been disrespectful toward Lady Chen; when the emperor learned of it he flew into a rage and ordered Shu to summon the Prince of Fangling.

sentences.zh: 述與元岩出外作敕書。

translations.literal: Shu and Yuan Yan went outside to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Shu and Yuan Yan went outside the palace to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 楊素見之，與皇太子謀，矯詔執述、岩屬吏。

translations.literal: Yang Su saw this, conspired with the crown prince, and forged an edict to arrest Shu and Yan and hand them over to the judicial officers.
