translations.idiomatic: Yang Su saw what was happening, conspired with the crown prince, and forged an edict to have Shu and Yan arrested and handed over to the judicial officers.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝嗣位，述坐除名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Shu was punished by removal from the registry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Shu was stripped from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 公主請與同徙，帝不聽。

translations.literal: The princess asked to be banished together with him; the emperor refused to permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The princess asked to share his exile; the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 述在龍川數年，復徙寧越，遇瘴癘死。

translations.literal: Shu was in Longchuan for several years, was then again transferred to Ningyue, and died there of miasma and pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Shu spent several years in Longchuan, was then transferred to Ningyue, and died there of pestilential disease.

sentences.zh: 機弟弘，字匡道。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Hong, styled Kuangdao.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Hong, whose courtesy name was Kuangdao.

sentences.zh: 少聰穎，工草隸，博涉群書，辭采雅贍。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and quick, skilled in cursive and clerical script, broadly versed in many books, with elegant and abundant literary style.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from youth, he was skilled in cursive and clerical script, widely read, and wrote with elegant, abundant style.

sentences.zh: 與弘農楊素為莫逆交。

translations.literal: With Yang Su of Hongnong he formed an inseparable friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a close friendship with Yang Su of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 解巾中外府記室。

translations.literal: When he first took up the headcloth he became secretary in a central or external office.
translations.idiomatic: On entering official life he became secretary in a government office.

sentences.zh: 建德初，除內史上士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiande era he was appointed Senior Clerk in the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiande era he was appointed senior clerk in the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曆小宮尹、禦正上士。

translations.literal: He served successively as Junior Palace Master and Senior Clerk of Imperial Rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as junior palace master and senior clerk of imperial rectitude.

sentences.zh: 陳遣王偃人來聘，武帝令弘勞之。

translations.literal: Chen sent Wang Yanren on a mission of friendly visit; Emperor Wu ordered Hong to extend hospitality to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen sent Wang Yanren on a diplomatic mission, and Emperor Wu had Hong receive and entertain him.

sentences.zh: 偃人謂弘曰：「來日至藍田，正逢滋水暴長，所賚國信，溺而從流。

translations.literal: Yanren said to Hong: "The day we arrived at Lantian we just met the Zi River in sudden flood; the national credentials we carried were drowned and carried off downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Yanren said to Hong: "On the day we reached Lantian we met the Zi River in sudden flood, and the state credentials we carried were drowned and swept downstream.

sentences.zh: 今所進，假之從吏。

translations.literal: What we present now has been borrowed from our accompanying clerks.
translations.idiomatic: What we are presenting now was borrowed from our accompanying clerks.

sentences.zh: 請勒下流人見為尋此物。」

translations.literal: We ask that you order people downstream who have seen them to search for these items.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that you order people downstream who have seen them to search for these items.

sentences.zh: 弘曰：「昔淳於之獻空籠，前史稱以為美。

translations.literal: Hong said: "In olden days Chunyu's presentation of an empty cage was praised in earlier histories as admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Hong said: "In former times Chunyu's presenting of an empty cage was praised in history as admirable.

sentences.zh: 足下假物而進，詎是陳君命乎？」

translations.literal: You, sir, present borrowed objects—can this be Lord Chen's command?
translations.idiomatic: You present borrowed items—can this really be on the orders of the lord of Chen?

sentences.zh: 偃人慚不能對。

translations.literal: Yanren was ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yanren was ashamed and had no reply.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞而嘉之，盡以偃人所進物賜弘，仍令報聘。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu heard and praised this; he gave all the items Yanren had presented to Hong and further ordered him to return the diplomatic visit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu heard of this and was pleased; he gave Hong all the items Yanren had presented and ordered him to return the diplomatic visit.

sentences.zh: 占對敏捷，見稱于時。

translations.literal: His impromptu responses were quick, and he was praised in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Quick and clever in debate, he was praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 後卒于禦正下大夫。

translations.literal: Later he died while serving as Junior Grand Master of Imperial Rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as junior grand master of imperial rectitude.

sentences.zh: 贈晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Governor of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously named governor of Jin province.

sentences.zh: 楊素誄之曰：「山陽王弼，風流長逝；

translations.literal: Yang Su composed an elegy for him, saying: "Wang Bi of Shanyang, his elegant spirit long departed;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su composed an elegy for him: "Wang Bi of Shanyang, gone with his elegant spirit;

sentences.zh: 潁川荀粲，零落無時。

translations.literal: Xun Can of Yingchuan, fallen away without warning.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Can of Yingchuan, cut down before his time.

sentences.zh: 修竹夾池，永絕梁園之賦；

translations.literal: Tall bamboos flanking the pond—forever ended are the fu of the Liang Garden;
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo groves flanking the pond—the Liang Garden fu is ended forever;

sentences.zh: 長楊映沼，無復洛川之文。」

translations.literal: The changyang trees reflected in the marsh—never again will there be the prose of the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: Changyang groves mirrored in the marsh—the Luo River prose will never return.

sentences.zh: 其為士友所痛惜如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he mourned by scholar friends.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the grief of his friends among the literati.

sentences.zh: 有文集行於世。

translations.literal: He had collected writings circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子燮，官至河內郡掾。

translations.literal: His son Xie reached the office of clerk in Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie rose to the rank of clerk in Henei commandery.

sentences.zh: 旦弟肅，字匡仁。

translations.literal: Dan's younger brother Su, styled Kuangren.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's younger brother Su, whose courtesy name was Kuangren.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，閑於占對。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and quick, skilled in impromptu responses.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from youth, he was skilled at impromptu repartee.

sentences.zh: 仕周，位宣納上士。

translations.literal: He served Zhou and held the post of Senior Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Zhou and held the post of senior clerk of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝作相，引為賓曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as Chancellor, he was invited to serve as Aide in the Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui became chancellor, he was invited to serve as aide in the guests bureau.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，授太子洗馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era he was appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaihuang era he was appointed groom of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 陳使謝泉來聘，以才學見稱，詔肅宴接，時論稱其華辯。

translations.literal: Chen sent Xie Quan on a mission of friendly visit; because of his talent and learning he was praised, and an edict ordered Su to host and receive him; opinion at the time praised his eloquence and brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen sent Xie Quan on a diplomatic mission, Su was ordered to host him; renowned for his talent and learning, Su was praised at the time for his eloquence and brilliance.

sentences.zh: 曆太子內舍人，遷太子僕。

translations.literal: He served successively as Inner Gentleman of the Heir Apparent and was promoted to Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as inner gentleman of the heir apparent and was promoted to steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子廢，坐除名。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, he was punished by removal from the registry.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed, he was struck from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 大業中，帝與段達語及庶人罪惡。

translations.literal: During the Daye era the emperor spoke with Duan Da about the deposed prince's crimes and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era the emperor spoke with Duan Da about the deposed prince's misconduct.

sentences.zh: 達云：「柳肅在宮，大見疏斥。」

translations.literal: Da said: "Liu Su, while at the palace, was greatly alienated and rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Da said: "While serving at the palace, Liu Su was greatly alienated and rejected.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked why.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「學士劉臻嘗進章仇太翼宮中，為巫蠱事。

translations.literal: He replied: "The scholar Liu Zhen once brought Zhang Qiu Taiyi into the palace for sorcery and witchcraft.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "The scholar Liu Zhen once brought Zhang Qiu Taiyi into the palace for sorcery.

sentences.zh: 肅知而諫曰：'殿下位當儲貳，戒在不孝，無患見疑。

translations.literal: Su learned of it and remonstrated, saying: 'Your Highness holds the position of heir apparent; guard against unfilial conduct—there is no need to fear being suspected.
translations.idiomatic: Su learned of it and remonstrated: 'Your Highness holds the position of heir apparent; guard against unfilial conduct—there is no need to fear suspicion.

sentences.zh: 劉臻書生，鼓搖脣舌，適足以相詿誤。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen is a mere bookish man who merely wags his lips and tongue—he is quite sufficient to lead one into error.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen is a mere bookish man who wags his lips and tongue—he is quite enough to lead you astray.

sentences.zh: 願勿納之。

translations.literal: I beg you not to admit him.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you not to admit him.

sentences.zh: '庶人不懌，他日，謂臻曰：'汝何漏泄，使柳肅知之，令面折我！

translations.literal: The commoner was displeased; another day he said to Zhen: 'Why did you leak this, letting Liu Su know and causing him to confront me to my face!
translations.idiomatic: The deposed prince was displeased; another day he said to Zhen: 'Why did you leak this, letting Liu Su know and causing him to confront me to my face!

sentences.zh: '自是後，言皆不用。」

translations.literal: From then on, none of his advice was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, none of his advice was heeded.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「肅橫除名。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Restore Su's name—he had been summarily struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Restore Liu Su's name—he should never have been struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 乃召守禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He then summoned him to serve concurrently as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned him to serve concurrently as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed because of an offense.

sentences.zh: 後守工部侍郎，大見親任，每幸遼東，常委于涿郡留守。

translations.literal: Later he served concurrently as Vice Minister of Works, was greatly trusted, and whenever the emperor went on campaign to Liaodong, regularly entrusted him with staying behind as guardian of Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served concurrently as vice minister of works and was greatly trusted; whenever the emperor went on campaign to Liaodong, he regularly entrusted him with staying behind as guardian of Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 機從子謇之，字公正。

translations.literal: Ji's nephew Jianzhi, styled Gongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's nephew Jianzhi, whose courtesy name was Gongzheng.

sentences.zh: 父蔡年，周順州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Cai Nian was Governor of Shun Province under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cai Nian was governor of Shun province under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 謇之身長七尺五寸，儀容甚偉，風神爽亮，進止可觀。

translations.literal: Jianzhi was seven feet five inches in height, with very imposing appearance, bright and clear in bearing and spirit, and comely in his movements and deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhi stood seven feet five inches tall, with a commanding appearance, bright and spirited bearing, and dignified deportment.

sentences.zh: 為童兒時，周齊王憲遇之於途，異而與語，大奇之，因奏為國子生。

translations.literal: When he was a child, Prince of Qi Xian of Zhou met him on the road, found him unusual and spoke with him, greatly marveled at him, and therefore memorialized to appoint him a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was met on the road by Prince Qi Xian of Zhou, who found him remarkable, spoke with him, and was so impressed that he had him enrolled as a student of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 以明經擢第，拜宮師中士，轉守廟下士。

translations.literal: Having passed the examination in the Classics with distinction, he was appointed Middle Clerk in the Palace Masters Office and was transferred to serve as Lower Clerk of the Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the classics examination with distinction, he was appointed middle clerk in the palace masters office and transferred to serve as lower clerk of the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 武帝有事太廟，謇之讀祝文，音韻清雅，觀者屬目。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu performed rites at the Grand Ancestral Temple, Jianzhi read the prayer text; his tones and cadence were clear and elegant, and onlookers fixed their eyes upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu performed rites at the grand ancestral temple, Jianzhi read the prayer text in clear, elegant tones, and all eyes turned to him.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，擢為宣納上士。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this and promoted him to Senior Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to senior clerk of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜通事舍人，尋遷內史舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era he was appointed Attendant Master of Affairs and soon transferred to Attendant of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaihuang era he was appointed attendant master of affairs and soon transferred to attendant of the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曆兵部、司勳二曹侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister in the Bureaus of War and of Meritorious Service.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as vice minister in the bureaus of war and of meritorious service.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以謇之雅望，善談謔，又飲酒至一石不亂，由是，每梁陳使至，輒令接對。

translations.literal: The court, because of Jianzhi's refined prestige, his skill in witty banter, and his ability to drink up to one shi without becoming disorderly, therefore whenever envoys from Liang or Chen arrived always ordered him to receive and respond to them.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Jianzhi's fine reputation, his gift for witty banter, and his ability to drink a full shi of wine without losing his composure, the court always had him receive envoys from Liang and Chen.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 出入十餘年，每參掌敷奏。

translations.literal: For more than ten years going in and out of office, he regularly took part in drafting and presenting memorials.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years in court service he regularly took part in drafting and presenting memorials.

sentences.zh: 會吐谷渾來降，朝廷以宗女光化公主妻之，以謇之兼散騎常侍，送公主于西域。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun came to surrender, the court gave a clanswoman, Princess Guanghua, in marriage to their leader and appointed Jianzhi concurrently as Regular Attendant of the Secretariat to escort the princess to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun submitted, the court married a clanswoman, Princess Guanghua, to their leader and appointed Jianzhi concurrently as regular attendant of the secretariat to escort the princess to the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 及突厥啟人可汗求和親，復令謇之送義成公主于突厥。

translations.literal: When the Türk Qimin Qaghan sought a marriage alliance, Jianzhi was again ordered to escort Princess Yicheng to the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türk Qimin Qaghan sought a marriage alliance, Jianzhi was again ordered to escort Princess Yicheng to the Türks.

sentences.zh: 前後使二國，得贈馬二千餘匹，雜物稱是，皆散之宗族，家無餘財。

translations.literal: On his missions to the two states, front and back, he received more than two thousand horses in gifts, with miscellaneous goods in proportion, and distributed them all to his clansmen, leaving no surplus wealth at home.
translations.idiomatic: On his two missions he received more than two thousand horses in gifts, along with a comparable amount of other goods, and distributed them all among his clansmen, leaving nothing for his household.

sentences.zh: 出為肅、息二州刺史，俱有惠政。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Su and Xi provinces, and in both he had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Su and Xi provinces, and in both he governed with benevolent policies.

sentences.zh: 煬帝踐祚，復拜光祿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was again appointed Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was again appointed director of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 大業初，啟人可汗自以內附，遂畜牧於定襄、馬邑間。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daye era Qimin Qaghan, considering himself internally attached to the dynasty, then pastured his herds between Dingxiang and Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daye era Qimin Qaghan, having submitted to the dynasty, pastured his herds between Dingxiang and Mayi.

sentences.zh: 帝使謇之諭令出塞。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Jianzhi to instruct him and order him to go beyond the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Jianzhi to instruct him to move beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 還，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Minister in the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed vice minister of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 時元德太子初薨，朝野注望，以齊王當立。

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Yuande had just died; court and countryside fixed their hopes, expecting the Prince of Qi to be installed.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yuande had just died, and court and country alike expected the Prince of Qi to be named heir.

sentences.zh: 帝方重王府之選，拜為齊王長史。

translations.literal: The emperor was then placing great weight on selections for princely establishments and appointed him Chief Administrator to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then placing great emphasis on appointments to princely households and made him chief administrator to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 帝法服臨軒，命齊王立於西朝堂，遣吏部尚書牛弘、內史令楊約、左衛大將軍宇文述等從殿廷引謇之詣齊王所，西面立。

translations.literal: The emperor in ceremonial robes came to the front hall, ordered the Prince of Qi to stand in the western court hall, and sent Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, Director of the Inner Secretariat Yang Yue, General of the Left Guard Yuwen Shu, and others from the palace hall to lead Jianzhi to the Prince of Qi's place, where he stood facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in ceremonial robes came to the front hall, had the Prince of Qi stand in the western court hall, and sent Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, Director of the Inner Secretariat Yang Yue, General of the Left Guard Yuwen Shu, and others from the palace hall to lead Jianzhi to the prince's side, where he stood facing west.

sentences.zh: 弘宣敕謂齊王曰：「我出蕃之初，時年十二。

translations.literal: Hong announced the edict and said to the Prince of Qi: "When I first went out to my fief, I was twelve years old.
translations.idiomatic: Hong announced the edict and said to the Prince of Qi: "When I first went out to my fief, I was twelve years old.

sentences.zh: 先帝立我於西朝堂，乃令高熲、虞慶則、元旻等從內送王子相于我。

translations.literal: The late emperor installed me in the Western Court Hall and ordered Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, Yuan Min, and others to escort Prince Zixiang to me from within.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor installed me in the Western Court Hall, he had Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, Yuan Min, and others bring Prince Zixiang to me from the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 誡我曰：' 以汝未更世事，令子相作輔於汝，事無大小，皆可委之。

translations.literal: He admonished me, saying: 'Because you have not yet experienced the affairs of the world, I appoint Zixiang to assist you; matters great and small may all be entrusted to him.'
translations.idiomatic: He warned me: 'You are still inexperienced in worldly affairs, so I set Zixiang to assist you. Great matters and small—you may entrust them all to him.'

sentences.zh: 無得昵近小人，疏遠子相。

translations.literal: Do not draw near petty men or keep Zixiang at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Do not cozy up to petty men or keep your distance from Zixiang.

sentences.zh: 若從我言者，有益於社稷，成立汝名行；

translations.literal: If you follow my words, it will benefit the altars of state and establish your reputation and conduct;
translations.idiomatic: If you heed my words, the realm will benefit and your name and conduct will stand firm;

sentences.zh: 如不用此言，唯國及身，敗無日矣。

translations.literal: if you do not use these words, for the state and for yourself ruin will come in no long time.
translations.idiomatic: if you ignore them, ruin for the state and for yourself will come soon.

sentences.zh: ' 吾受敕，奉以周旋，不敢失墜。

translations.literal: I received the command and have upheld it in all my dealings, not daring to let it fall away.
translations.idiomatic: I received that command and have lived by it ever since, not daring to let it slip.

sentences.zh: 微子相之力，吾幾無今日矣。

translations.literal: Were it not for Zixiang's strength, I would scarcely have today.
translations.idiomatic: Without Zixiang's help, I would scarcely be where I am today.

sentences.zh: 若與謇之從事，一如子相也。」

translations.literal: If you work with Jianzhi, treat him just as you would Zixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Work with Jianzhi as you would with Zixiang.

sentences.zh: 又敕謇之曰：「今以卿作輔于齊，副朕所望。

translations.literal: He also charged Jianzhi, saying: "Now I make you assistant to the Prince of Qi, in fulfillment of what I hope for.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Jianzhi: "I appoint you to assist the Prince of Qi, as I have long wished.

sentences.zh: 若齊王德業修備，富貴自當鍾卿一門。

translations.literal: If the Prince of Qi's virtue and achievement are fully cultivated, wealth and honor will naturally settle on your whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: If the Prince of Qi's virtue and achievement are complete, wealth and honor will naturally come to your whole house.

sentences.zh: 若有不善，罪亦相及。」

translations.literal: If there is anything unworthy, punishment will reach you as well."
translations.idiomatic: If anything goes wrong, you will share the blame as well."

sentences.zh: 時齊王擅寵，喬令則之徒，深見昵狎，謇之知其非，不能匡正。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi enjoyed exclusive favor; Qiao Lingze and his sort were deeply intimate with him. Jianzhi knew this was wrong but could not set it right.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi then held the emperor's exclusive favor; men like Qiao Lingze grew dangerously close to him. Jianzhi saw the danger but could not correct it.

sentences.zh: 及王得罪，謇之竟坐除名。

translations.literal: When the prince fell into guilt, Jianzhi in the end was punished by removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was condemned, Jianzhi was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 及帝幸遼東，召檢校燕郡事。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Liaodong, he was summoned to inspect affairs in Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned in Liaodong, Jianzhi was called to oversee Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝班師至燕郡，坐供頓不給，配戍嶺南，卒於洭口。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned the army to Yan commandery, Jianzhi was punished because supplies were not provided; he was assigned to garrison duty in Lingnan and died at Kuangkou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew to Yan commandery, Jianzhi was punished for failing to provision the army, sent to garrison Lingnan, and died at Kuangkou.

sentences.zh: 子威明。

translations.literal: His son was Weiming.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Weiming.

sentences.zh: 論曰：高氏藉四胡之勢，跨有山東，周文承二將之餘，創基關右，似商、周之不敵，若漢、楚之爭雄。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The Gao house relied on the power of the Four Hu and straddled Shandong; Zhou Wen inherited what remained from two generals and founded his base in the Guanxi west—like Shang and Zhou unmatched in strength, like Han and Chu contending for supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The Gao clan rode the power of the frontier peoples and held the east; Zhou Wen took up the legacy of two great generals and founded his realm in the Guanxi west—like the clash of Shang and Zhou, like the rivalry of Han and Chu.

sentences.zh: 又連官渡之兵，未定鴻溝之約。

translations.literal: Again they linked battle after battle as at Guandu, yet never settled a covenant as at Honggou.
translations.idiomatic: Battle followed battle as at Guandu, yet no truce like that at Honggou ever held.

sentences.zh: 雖弘農、沙苑，齊卒先奔；

translations.literal: Although at Hongnong and Shayuan the soldiers of Qi fled first;
translations.idiomatic: Though at Hongnong and Shayuan Qi's troops broke first;

sentences.zh: 而河橋、北芒，周師橈敗。

translations.literal: at Heqiao and Beimang the Zhou armies were turned to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: at Heqiao and Beimang Zhou's armies were routed.

sentences.zh: 於是競圖進取，各務兵戈，齊謂兼併有餘，周則自守不足。

translations.literal: Thereupon each side strove to advance and devoted itself to arms; Qi thought it had surplus strength for annexation, while Zhou felt its self-defense was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Each side then pressed for advantage and poured everything into war: Qi believed conquest was within reach, while Zhou felt it could barely hold its own.

sentences.zh: 韋孝寬奇材異度，緯武經文，居要害之地，受幹城之托。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan was a man of extraordinary talent and singular measure, weaving martial and civil arts together; he occupied a vital position and received the trust of a shield to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan was a man of rare ability, equally adept in arms and letters, holding a critical post entrusted with the defense of the realm.

sentences.zh: 東人怙恃其眾，悉力來攻，將欲釃酒未央，飲馬清渭。

translations.literal: The easterners relied on their numbers and came with full force, intending to pour libation wine in Weiyang and water their horses in the clear Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The easterners trusted in their numbers and attacked with full force, intending to celebrate in Weiyang and water their horses in the Wei.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乃馮茲雉堞，抗彼仇讎，事甚析骸，勢危負戶，終能奮其智勇，應變無方，城守六旬，竟摧大敵。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan then leaned on these battlements and resisted that foe; the affair was like splitting bones for food, the situation as perilous as carrying households on one's back—yet in the end he roused his wisdom and courage, responded to change without fixed method, held the city for sixty days, and at last shattered the great enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan manned those walls against his foes through hunger and desperation, yet roused all his wit and courage, adapted without fixed plan, held the city sixty days, and broke the great enemy at last.

sentences.zh: 齊人既焚營宵遁，高氏遂憤恚而殂。

translations.literal: When the men of Qi burned their camps and fled by night, the Gao house thereupon died of resentment and rage.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi burned its camps and stole away by night, Gao Huan brooded himself to death.

sentences.zh: 雖即墨破燕，晉陽存趙，何以能尚？

translations.literal: Though Jimo broke Yan and Jinyang preserved Zhao—how could those be ranked above this?
translations.idiomatic: The sieges of Jimo and Jinyang pale beside this—how could they compare?

sentences.zh: 若使平陽不守，鄴城無眾人之師；

translations.literal: If Pingyang had not been held, Ye would have had no army of the masses;
translations.idiomatic: Had Pingyang fallen, Ye would have lost its army;

sentences.zh: 玉壁啟關，函谷失封泥之固。

translations.literal: if Yubi opened its gates, Hangu Pass would have lost the security of its sealed clay.
translations.idiomatic: had Yubi's gates opened, Hangu Pass would have lost its seal.

sentences.zh: 斯豈一城之得喪，實亦二國之興亡者歟。

translations.literal: Was this not merely the gain or loss of one city, but truly the rise or fall of two states?
translations.idiomatic: This was not merely one city's fate—it was the rise or fall of two kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 韋夐陷不負人，貞不絕俗，怡神墳籍，養素丘園，哀樂無以動其心，名利不足幹其慮，確乎不拔，實近代之高人也。

translations.literal: Wei Xiong in hardship did not betray others, in integrity did not cut himself off from the world; he delighted his spirit in the tombs of the classics and nourished simplicity in garden and field; joy and grief could not move his heart, fame and profit could not sway his thoughts—firm and unyielding, he was truly a lofty man of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiong did not betray others in hardship and did not cut himself off from the world in integrity. He found joy in the classics and simplicity in his garden; neither joy nor grief moved him, neither fame nor profit swayed him—unyielding, a true lofty spirit of his age.

sentences.zh: 明帝比諸園、綺，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming compared him to Yuan and Qi, was it for nothing!
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming compared him to the recluses Yuan and Qi, he did not speak in vain!

sentences.zh: 世康風神雅量，一代稱偉，簪纓人物，見重京華。

translations.literal: Shikang's bearing and elegant measure were called great in his generation; as a man of cap and tassel he was esteemed in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang's bearing and generous spirit made him the wonder of his generation; as a court gentleman he was honored in the capital.

sentences.zh: 瑱素望高風，亦云美矣。

translations.literal: Zhen's plain repute and lofty wind were also said to be admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's unadorned reputation and lofty integrity were admirable as well.

sentences.zh: 柳虯兄弟，雅道是基，並能譽重搢紳，豈虛至也。

translations.literal: The brothers Liu Qiu took refined conduct as their foundation and both won heavy repute among the gentry—how could such praise be empty?
translations.idiomatic: The Liu Qiu brothers grounded themselves in refined conduct and won the esteem of the gentry—such praise was not undeserved.

sentences.zh: 慶束帶立朝，匪躬是蹈，蒞官從政，清白著美。

translations.literal: Qing stood at court with girded sash and trod the path of selfless service; in taking office and conducting government, his purity was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Qing served at court with sash bound tight, devoted himself without reserve, and won fame for integrity in office.

sentences.zh: 至於畏避權寵，違忤宰臣，雖取詘于一時，實獲申於千載矣。

translations.literal: As for his fearing and avoiding power and favor, and opposing chief ministers—though he suffered setback for a time, he was truly vindicated for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: In shunning power and defying chief ministers he suffered for a season, yet won vindication for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 機立身行已，本以寬雅流譽，至於登朝正色，可謂不違直道。

translations.literal: Ji in establishing himself and conducting his person was originally famed for generous elegance; when he came to court with upright color, it may be said he did not depart from the straight path.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was known for generous elegance in his conduct; when he took his place at court with stern integrity, he did not stray from the straight path.

sentences.zh: 雖陵谷遷貿，終以雅正自居，古所謂以道事人，斯之謂矣。

translations.literal: Though hills and valleys shifted and exchanged, in the end he took refined rectitude as his station—what the ancients called serving others by the Way: this is what was meant.
translations.idiomatic: Though fortunes rose and fell, he held to refined integrity to the end—what the ancients meant by serving others through the Way.

sentences.zh: 述雖幹略見稱，終乃敗於驕寵，惜矣。

translations.literal: Though Shu was praised for capacity and strategy, in the end he was ruined by arrogant favor—alas.
translations.idiomatic: Shu won praise for ability and strategy, yet was destroyed by arrogant favor—a pity.
